# Business Rule Register

## 01_PRODUCT/06_BUSINESS_MODEL_AND_CROSS_MODULE_RULES.md

Source: [01_PRODUCT/06_BUSINESS_MODEL_AND_CROSS_MODULE_RULES.md](../01_PRODUCT/06_BUSINESS_MODEL_AND_CROSS_MODULE_RULES.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-XCT-001 | A person owns their career identity: profile, evidence, learning records, applications, consents. No org, institution or enterprise becomes the owner of a person's career identity through employment, enrollment, sponsorship or contract; such parties own only the records they create about their own processes. | Portability and trust | `PRF`, `EVD`, `SET`, contracts | [SRC: STR-01 §5 "Learner owns career identity"] |
| BR-XCT-002 | Every core entity has exactly one owning module; only the owner writes it; others read through the owner's contract or events (see 07 §3). | One semantic model | All modules | [SRC: SSOT §3.1 "One semantic model"; DER] |
| BR-XCT-003 | Org-owned hiring records (jobs, requisitions, notes, scorecards, offers, API keys, integrations) belong to the org and survive a member's departure; offboarding reassigns them. | Continuity | `EMP`, `ATS`, `PLT` | [SRC: USR-01 REV2; DER] |
| BR-XCT-004 | An issuer (platform, institution, employer org, instructor) controls the validity of a credential it issued (issue, correct, revoke with reason); the holder controls whether it is displayed. | Issuer accountability, holder control | `EVD` | [SRC: SSOT §6.3] |
| BR-XCT-005 | Course and content ownership follows the authoring agreement: independent instructors own their courses and license the platform to distribute; institution and enterprise courses are owned by that tenant; first-party courses by the platform. | Clear rights | `STU` | [SRC: COMMERCIAL_OPERATIONS §13; DER] |
| BR-XCT-006 | When a person is erased, records shared with others keep the counterparty's copy: messages show "Deleted user"; reviews they wrote are removed; scorecards about them in an org are handled by the org's retention class; referee responses they gave remain attached to the candidate's evidence with the referee shown as "Former user". | Erasure without destroying others' records | `SET`, owning modules | [SRC: Appendix E V61-19; DER] |
| BR-XCT-080 | One account may hold many grants; every request carries one active context; capabilities are evaluated for that context only and never escalate across contexts. | Multi-role safety | `IDN`, policy service | [SRC: USR-01 REV2 §1; DER] |
| BR-XCT-007 | Consent is purpose-bound, versioned and taken from one catalogue of scope ids; every scope defaults to off, except `application.share_snapshot`, which is granted by the act of applying. | Privacy by purpose | `SET` | [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE] |
| BR-XCT-008 | Revocation takes effect at the first read after the revoking commit; no module caches consent; signed URLs issued under a revoked scope lapse within their short life (at most 5 minutes). | Immediate control | `SET`, `PLT` | [SRC: Appendix E V61-16] |
| BR-XCT-009 | Consent is never bundled with terms of service or made a condition of the core loop, except processing strictly necessary to provide what the person asked for. | Freely given | `SET`, all UI | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-010 | Nobody grants consent on behalf of another person; org admins, institution admins and enterprise admins cannot consent for members or learners. | Autonomy | `SET` | [SRC: USR-01 REV2 §2.1] |
| BR-XCT-011 | Every grant is visible in one consent centre with grantee, date, expiry, last use and a revoke control; receipts are downloadable. | Transparency | `SET` | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-012 | Every read of a person's non-public data by another party requires a live consent scope, an application snapshot, a booking share, or a lawful-basis exception named in the module spec (for example institution-run course work, mandated enterprise learning). | Consent bridge | Policy service, every module | [SRC: USR-01 §4 "consent scopes gate every recruiter read"] |
| BR-XCT-013 | Scopes with an expiry remind the person 14 days before; re-confirmation prompts are not expiries. | Avoid silent lapse | `SET`, `NTF` | [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE] |
| BR-XCT-014 | Visibility levels are private, connections, discoverable to verified employers, and public; new accounts default to private for evidence and to not public for the profile page. | Safe defaults | `SET`, `PRF` | [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE defaults off] |
| BR-XCT-015 | Email and phone are masked from every other party unless `profile.share_contact` is live for that party or the person shared them in an accepted conversation. | Contact protection | `PRF`, `MSG` | [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE] |
| BR-XCT-016 | Evidence is always displayed with its rung (claimed, artifact-backed, peer-attested, authority-verified) and, for authority-verified, its issuer class; the word "verified" never appears for claimed items, and instructor attestation never displays as platform-verified. | Verified over claimed | `EVD`, all UI | [SRC: Appendix E V61-17] |
| BR-XCT-017 | A block overrides every consent, visibility and discoverability setting: the blocked party cannot view, search, message, refer, review or invite the blocker. | Safety | Policy service | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-018 | Evaluative notes and scorecards about a person are never shown to that person in product; they are disclosed only through a legally required data-subject access response handled by `SUP` with review. | Candid evaluation within law | `ATS`, `INT`, `SET` | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-019 | Profile-view and evidence-view disclosure to the person defaults to semi-anonymous (org class and date, not the viewer's name); stronger or weaker disclosure is an owner decision. | Balance of interests | `PRF`, `EVD` | [SRC: SSOT OD-36] |
| BR-XCT-020 | No pay-to-rank: no billing field, plan or payment is an input to search ranking, matching, suggested order or recommendations; any paid visibility (if `OD-PRD-18` admits it) is labelled and placed in separate slots. | Fairness | `SRC`, `AIC` | [SRC: ADR-T22; INV-T19] |
| BR-XCT-021 | No autonomous adverse decision: rejection, ranking out, suspension, sanction or adverse background-check action requires a recorded human actor; bulk actions require explicit confirmation by a human. | Human-controlled AI | `ATS`, `TSF`, `BGV`, `AIC` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2; STR-01 §7] |
| BR-XCT-022 | Every match or recommendation shown carries its rationale and an uncertainty statement. | Explainability | `AIC` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2] |
| BR-XCT-023 | Protected attributes are never ranking features; they are collected only voluntarily, for audit-only purposes, stored separately and readable only by the audit role. | Non-discrimination | `AIC`, `ANL` | [SRC: STR-01 REV2 GOAL-03] |
| BR-XCT-024 | An adverse-impact review is held each quarter on audit-only attributes; the result is recorded; a ratio below the counsel-set threshold opens a human review. | Fairness monitoring | `ANL`, `AIC` | [SRC: STR-01 REV2 GOAL-03] |
| BR-XCT-025 | Anomaly is not guilt: integrity, fraud and abuse signals trigger human review and temporary holds, never automatic sanctions beyond rate limiting. | Due process | `TSF`, `ASM`, `BGV` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2] |
| BR-XCT-026 | Rejections use a reason code from a fixed list and send a respectful notice to the candidate on the human's action. | Candidate dignity | `ATS`, `NTF` | [SRC: SSOT §3.1] |
| BR-XCT-027 | The core loop is free and equal for every candidate regardless of plan: creating and verifying evidence, applying, messaging in consented threads, privacy controls and export. | Fair access | `BIL`, all modules | [SRC: STR-01 §5] |
| BR-XCT-028 | Assessment accommodations are available on request and are never disclosed to employers or shown on results. | Accessibility and fairness | `ASM` | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-029 | Aggregates about people (analytics, cohort reports, salary benchmarks, skills inventories) are published only for cells of at least `min_cohort_k` contributors, with complementary suppression against differencing. | Re-identification risk | `ANL`, `MKT`, `INS`, `ENT` | [SRC: SSOT Amendment G; `OD-PRD-12`] |
| BR-XCT-030 | Every entity is assigned one retention class (ephemeral, operational, tenant-configurable, financial, legal-hold-eligible, audit); values are policy configuration. | Predictable lifecycle | Each module's entity table | [SRC: SSOT Amendment G] |
| BR-XCT-031 | Erasure runs on three separate clocks: cancel window, completion deadline and deactivation purge; their values are `OD-PRD-13`. | Clarity | `SET` | [SRC: Appendix E V61-07] |
| BR-XCT-032 | Append-only histories reference a person only through an opaque subject reference; erasure deletes the identity mapping instead of rewriting history. | Erasure with integrity | `SET`, `ADM` | [SRC: Appendix E V61-19] |
| BR-XCT-033 | A legal hold supersedes erasure for the held records only; the person is told which categories are held and why, unless law forbids. | Legal obligations | `SET` | [SRC: COMMERCIAL_OPERATIONS §3 records] |
| BR-XCT-034 | An application snapshot expires at the application's terminal state plus a retention period (default 12 months [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE]); the candidate may withdraw earlier, which tombstones live items. | Bounded employer retention | `JOB`, `SET` | [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE] |
| BR-XCT-035 | Backups age out within the backup retention window; a restore re-applies erasures recorded after the backup point before the data is served. | Erasure survives restore | Platform operations | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-036 | AI output never becomes evidence or changes a rung; AI-assisted text is labelled in version history; anything a person accepts from AI is their own claim. | Integrity of evidence | `AIC`, `EVD` | [SRC: SSOT Amendment C] |
| BR-XCT-037 | Sending a person's content to an AI provider requires `ai.assist.process`, with redaction of contact details and identifiers. | Privacy | AI gateway (`AIC`) | [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE] |
| BR-XCT-038 | `AI_PROHIBITED` assessment mode is enforced server-side across every TalentSphere AI entry point for the candidate during the attempt window; UI hiding is not enforcement. | Assessment integrity | AI gateway, `ASM` | [SRC: SSOT Amendment D] |
| BR-XCT-039 | Free users cause no paid AI inference unless an explicit, active cost policy allows it. | Cost control | AI gateway, `BIL` | [SRC: SSOT §16.4] |
| BR-XCT-040 | AI memory is separate from profile truth; the person can view and delete it. | Control | `AIC` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2] |
| BR-XCT-041 | No AI-generated message, outreach, job description or feedback is sent without a human reviewing and pressing send. | Accountability | `AIC`, `MSG`, `ATS` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2] |
| BR-XCT-042 | AI in hiring is descriptive and advisory only; candidate-level predictive scores and automated screening-out are excluded unless admitted by `OD-PRD-14`. | Regulatory and fairness risk | `AIC`, `ATS` | [SRC: SSOT Amendment E] |
| BR-XCT-043 | Entitlements derive only from verified billing state (processor webhooks reconciled to the ledger); a redirect, a support action or a client claim grants nothing. | Correctness | `BIL` | [SRC: INV-T17] |
| BR-XCT-044 | Refunds, credits and dispute outcomes follow a published policy, are executed only by `FIN` through `BIL`, and are audited; `SUP` can request but not issue. | Financial control | `BIL`, `ADM` | [SRC: COMMERCIAL_OPERATIONS §5] |
| BR-XCT-045 | Billing state never deletes user or tenant data; downgrade or non-payment limits new activity only. | Trust | `BIL`, all modules | [SRC: COMMERCIAL_OPERATIONS §3] |
| BR-XCT-046 | Plans and prices are immutable catalogue versions; a change creates a new version with an explicit grandfathering rule. | Auditability | `BIL` | [SRC: COMMERCIAL_OPERATIONS §2] |
| BR-XCT-047 | Candidates never pay to apply, to be seen by employers, or to be verified. | Fair access | `BIL`, `JOB`, `EVD` | [SRC: COMMERCIAL_OPERATIONS §1] |
| BR-XCT-048 | Payouts to instructors, mentors, freelancers or organizers require provider-verified payee identity and tax details; funds for open disputes are held. | Fraud and tax | `BIL` | [SRC: Appendix E V61-21] |
| BR-XCT-049 | No third-party money flows into or through the platform until `OD-PRD-04` decides the seller of record, payouts, tax and refunds. | Liability | `BIL`, `STU`, `MEN`, `GIG`, `EVT` | [SRC: Appendix E V61-21] |
| BR-XCT-050 | Enforcement sources take precedence in this order: legal obligation or court order; safety emergency; platform policy; tenant policy (org or institution community rules); the person's own settings. | Predictable outcomes | `TSF` | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-051 | Every moderation action carries a reason code, a notice to the affected person and an appeal path, except where law forbids notice or the content is spam. | Due process | `TSF`, `NTF` | [SRC: UJ-19] |
| BR-XCT-052 | An appeal is decided by a moderator other than the one who took the action. | Independence | `TSF` | [SRC: SSOT §5.9] |
| BR-XCT-053 | Reported content stays visible until decided unless its severity class meets the interim-hide threshold. | Avoid weaponized reporting | `TSF` | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-054 | Taken-down content is preserved under hold for the appeal period plus any legal requirement, then deleted. | Appeals and law | `TSF` | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-055 | The tenant of every request is derived from the server-side grant; cross-tenant reads occur only across consent bridges; API keys are bound to one tenant with explicit scopes and need subject consent for personal data. | Cross-tenant exposure is critical | Policy service, `PLT` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2, §5.1] |
| BR-XCT-056 | One screen or response holds one context's data; the personal inbox and calendar may aggregate with per-item context badges. | No blending | All UI, API | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-057 | Agency recruiters see client data only inside an accepted engagement and only for candidates they submitted with consent; the first valid consented submission owns the candidacy for a configurable window (default 180 days [PROP]). | Agency isolation | `EMP`, `ATS`, `JOB` | [SRC: SSOT J-10; DER] |
| BR-XCT-058 | No self-approval: the requester of a requisition, offer, refund, payout, privileged grant, course review or break-glass cannot approve it. | Separation of duties | Policy service | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-059 | Conflict-of-interest exclusions: instructors cannot attest their own evidence or review their own course; referees cannot be the candidate; moderators cannot act on content they are party to or connected with; org admins cannot review their own org; judges cannot score teams with a connection; applicants are removed from their own application's hiring team. | Integrity | Policy service | [SRC: SSOT §5.9; USR-01 REV2] |
| BR-XCT-060 | Platform staff roles live on staff accounts separate from personal accounts; staff tooling refuses actions on the staff member's own personal account. | Insider risk | `IDN`, `ADM` | [PROP] |
| BR-XCT-061 | Finance dual control: refunds above the threshold and every payout batch need a second `FIN`. | Fraud | `BIL` | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-062 | Privileged grants (`MOD`, `SUP`, `FIN`, `PAD`, `SAD`) need two approvers other than the grantee and requester; reviewed monthly; dormant grants expire after 60 days. | Least privilege | `ADM`, `IDN` | [SRC: USR-01 §6] |
| BR-XCT-063 | Delegation is limited to capabilities the delegator holds, in the same scope, time-bounded, revocable, audited, and not re-delegable. | Controlled flexibility | Policy service | [PROP] |
| BR-XCT-064 | Ownership transfer, consent, data-rights requests, break-glass, privileged grants, credential issuance, refunds, payouts and appeal decisions are not delegable. | High-risk actions | Policy service | [PROP] |
| BR-XCT-065 | Break-glass is available only to `SAD` with an incident or legal-case id, second-`SAD` approval, named scope, auto-expiry, full audit, post-incident review and notice where law requires. | Accountable emergency access | `ADM` | [PROP] |
| BR-XCT-066 | Notifications are classed as security, transactional, or marketing; security notices cannot be turned off; marketing requires `comms.marketing_email`. | Lawful communication | `NTF` | [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE] |
| BR-XCT-067 | Non-security notifications respect quiet hours, digests and a per-class frequency cap (parameter `ntf.max_nudges_per_day`, default 1 for reminders [PROP]). | Respect attention | `NTF` | [DER] |
| BR-XCT-068 | Evidence rung transitions happen only server-side through the ladder: claimed → artifact-backed → peer-attested → authority-verified; only defined verification events or case decisions move a rung. | Verified over claimed | `EVD` | [SRC: Appendix E V61-17] |
| BR-XCT-069 | Corrections create a new version; revocations are visible with a reason category; applications whose snapshot contains a revoked or superseded item show a flag to the hiring team. | Lineage | `EVD`, `JOB` | [SRC: SSOT Amendment F] |
| BR-XCT-070 | A credential export is labelled with a portable standard only after the export is validated against that standard. | Honesty | `EVD` | [SRC: SSOT Amendment F] |
| BR-XCT-071 | People below the minimum age cannot register; managed learners who are minors have discoverability, outreach and marketplace features locked off. | Protection of minors | `IDN`, `SET` | [SRC: Appendix E V61-24; `OD-PRD-11`] |
| BR-XCT-072 | Every journey is completable with keyboard and screen reader; no gate relies on an inaccessible challenge (for example a visual-only CAPTCHA). | Accessible by default | All UI | [SRC: SSOT §21] |
| BR-XCT-073 | Reputation is contextual: popularity measures (followers, likes, views) are never displayed or used as credibility. | Evidence over popularity | `REP`, `SRC`, `AIC` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2] |
| BR-XCT-074 | No core function depends at runtime on a competitor platform; external platforms are import or syndication adapters only. | Independence | `PLT` | [SRC: SSOT §4.3] |
| BR-XCT-075 | Recruiter first contact is a request that needs `outreach.recruiter_contact` and quota; the candidate accepts, declines or blocks before any free messaging. | Consent and dignity | `MSG` | [SRC: CONSENT_SCOPE_CATALOGUE] |
| BR-XCT-076 | Every consequential side effect is idempotent and audited, including the acting principal and, under delegation, the delegator. | Integrity | All modules, `ADM` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2] |

| BR-XCT-078 | Offline caches are never authoritative: server-authoritative actions (submit application, take assessment, pay, change consent) require a connection; only drafts and messages queue. | Correctness | `PWA` | [SRC: SSOT §3.2, §19] |
| BR-XCT-079 | Interview and session recording is off by default and requires the consent of every participant before it starts. | Privacy | `INT`, `MEN` | [SRC: SSOT OD-48] |

## ADM

Source: [02_MODULES/ADM_Admin_Console_Support_Operations.md](../02_MODULES/ADM_Admin_Console_Support_Operations.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-ADM-001 | Admin console access requires an active staff role, a phishing-resistant factor (passkey or security key) or SSO, and for any mutation a step-up authentication no older than 15 minutes. | Staff accounts are the highest-value target. | Admin authentication service; mutation middleware | [DER] [PROP] 15 minutes |
| BR-ADM-002 | Every staff mutation carries a reason code (and free text where the catalogue requires) and writes one audit event with actor, role, target, before and after summary, reason, request id and session id. A mutation that cannot write its audit event does not execute. | Accountability; reversibility. | Action envelope (FR-ADM-004); audit API | [SRC: SSOT BR-29] |
| BR-ADM-003 | A staff member cannot act on their own account, role assignment, grant, approval request or ticket as agent. The requester of a two-person action can never be its approver. | Separation of duties. | Policy layer on every admin action | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-004 | Actions in the dangerous-action catalogue execute only after approval by a second authorized identity, against a frozen payload; approval expires after 24 hours. | Limits damage from error or compromise. | Approval engine (FR-ADM-010) | [SRC: SSOT BR-29] [DER] |
| BR-ADM-005 | Personal data in admin views is masked by default. Unmasking requires an active privileged grant for that subject and data class. Lookups use exact identifiers; partial-match browsing of personal data is refused. | Least privilege; anti-enumeration. | Admin read projections; search | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-006 | Support view-as sessions require the user's explicit, revocable consent, are read-only and time-boxed; non-consented sessions are limited to SAD with two-person approval and a stated legal or security basis. | Trust; privacy. | Impersonation service (FR-ADM-024) | [PROP] |
| BR-ADM-007 | Break-glass access is limited to a named roster, requires an open P0 or P1 incident, lasts at most 60 minutes (one 30-minute extension), pages Security immediately and must be reviewed by a different person within 2 business days. | Emergency access without silent abuse. | Break-glass service (FR-ADM-011) | [DER] [PROP] parameters |
| BR-ADM-008 | Privileged grants are scoped to one subject and data class, last at most 8 hours, expire server-side on every request, and end when their ticket closes. | Time-boxed access. | Grant service (FR-ADM-009) | [SRC: Yash 18 PROC-04] |
| BR-ADM-009 | The audit log is append-only and tamper-evident (hash chain, external anchoring); no API deletes or edits an event; viewing it is audited; ingestion gaps and integrity failures raise alerts. | Evidence value. | Audit store (FR-ADM-032) | [SRC: SSOT §20.2] [DER] |
| BR-ADM-010 | Every feature flag has a code-declared key, a type, an owner and an expiry (default 90 days); evaluation order is kill switch, explicit override, targeting rules, percentage, default; flags never hold secrets; authorization-relevant flags evaluate server-side only. | Flag sprawl and leakage control. | Flag service (FR-ADM-014) | [SRC: SSOT F-35] [PROP] expiry |
| BR-ADM-011 | A kill switch overrides flags; each switch declares a degraded behavior and message before it can be activated; activation propagates within 15 seconds and call sites fail static (defined response, no unhandled error); switch state survives dependency outages. | Safe, fast containment. | Switch service (FR-ADM-015) | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-012 | Configuration values are typed, schema-validated, versioned and reversible; secrets are never stored as configuration; security-class and financial-class keys require two-person approval; changes cannot be applied inside an active change freeze without an approved exception. | Safe operability. | Config service (FR-ADM-016, FR-ADM-019) | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-013 | Critical and maintenance announcements are not dismissible; at most one critical banner is live; audience is resolved at display time; links must be https and allowlisted or marked external. | Reliable incident communication. | Announcement service | [PROP] |
| BR-ADM-014 | Legal document versions are immutable once published and remain reachable at dated URLs; material changes require counsel reference, two-person approval and the minimum notice period (30 days default) before effect and trigger re-consent through SET. | Legal certainty. | Legal publishing (FR-ADM-030) | [DER] [PROP] notice |
| BR-ADM-015 | SLA clocks start at ticket creation, follow the policy's business calendar, pause only in `pending_user` and `on_hold_external`, and are recomputed from event history; breaches are recorded with a cause. | Measurable service. | SLA service (FR-ADM-022) | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-016 | Support never requests passwords, one-time codes or full card numbers; outbound replies are scanned for credential patterns and blocked; automatic technical details attached to tickets use a whitelist (no tokens, cookies or form contents); pasted secrets in notes are rejected. | Social-engineering and leakage prevention. | Composer validation; intake | [SRC: Yash 18 INV-T14] |
| BR-ADM-017 | Sealed data classes (assessment answers and keys, message bodies, identity documents, background-check reports, health-class data) are never visible to SUP or FIN through any grant; access is only through the legal-process procedure with two-person approval. | Strong containment of the most sensitive data. | Projection layer; grant service | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-018 | Erasure and retention in ADM records: tickets, notes and audit events about an erased subject are pseudonymized, not deleted, where needed for accountability; a legal hold blocks erasure; privacy requests are tracked against jurisdiction deadlines and cannot close with any module incomplete. | Compliance with accountability. | Data-request console; SET | [SRC: Yash 18 PROC-09] [DEC-REQ] |
| BR-ADM-019 | Refunds and disputes are executed only through BIL, with idempotency keys; amounts above the FIN-L threshold require a second approver; the console labels provider state `live`, `inferred` or `degraded` and never edits billing truth directly. | Financial integrity. | Finance tooling (FR-ADM-035) | [SRC: SSOT BR-32, BR-28] |
| BR-ADM-020 | Admin exports are reasoned, row-limited (5,000 without approval), watermarked with exporter identity, CSV-injection safe, encrypted, delivered by single-use signed link valid 24 hours, and audited. | Leak attribution. | Export service (FR-ADM-036) | [DER] [PROP] limits |
| BR-ADM-021 | A dead job can be replayed only if its kind is flagged replay-safe; replay preserves the original idempotency key; payload views are redacted unless a grant applies; purge needs two-person approval and archives metadata. | No duplicate side effects. | Job console (FR-ADM-037) | [SRC: SSOT §13.5 DLQ] |
| BR-ADM-022 | Incidents use severities P0 to P3 with response targets (10 minutes, 30 minutes, 4 hours, 1 business day) and update cadences; public updates contain no personal data and are never knowingly false or optimistic; a post-incident review follows P0 and P1. | Honest operations. | Incident tooling (FR-ADM-038) | [SRC: SSOT §20.5] |
| BR-ADM-023 | A role assignment cannot grant a permission the assigner does not hold and have flagged delegable; PAD cannot assign SAD-tier roles; role expiry is mandatory (maximum 24 months). | No privilege escalation. | Role service (FR-ADM-007) | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-024 | Bulk operations require a dry-run younger than one hour on the identical target set; over 500 records need two-person approval; the run stops automatically when more than 5% of attempted records fail; one run per operation type at a time. | Blast-radius control. | Bulk executor (FR-ADM-034) | [SRC: SSOT BR-31 dry-run default] |
| BR-ADM-025 | The account holder is notified of administrative actions on their account through a verified channel, except when SAD records a legal or safety basis for non-disclosure with a review date. | Transparency with limited exceptions. | Notification step in action pipeline | [DER] [DEC-REQ] OD-ADM-08 |
| BR-ADM-026 | Admin sessions: idle timeout 30 minutes, absolute lifetime 8 hours, at most 2 concurrent sessions, separate origin and cookies from end-user sessions, optional network allowlist, and impossible-travel blocking. | Session hijack resistance. | Admin session service | [DER] [PROP] values |
| BR-ADM-027 | All staff-authored rich content (announcements, KB, CMS, macros, legal) is sanitized against an allowlist; scripts, inline event handlers and unknown embeds are removed; images require alt text; links follow the allowlist. | XSS and accessibility. | Sanitizer; publish validators | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-028 | Internal notes are append-only, attributed and never shown to end users; they cannot be edited after 5 minutes (corrections are new notes). | Integrity of case history. | Notes service | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-029 | Maintenance read-only mode keeps authentication, health endpoints, payment-provider webhooks, the admin console and status publishing available; all other writes return 503 with Retry-After. | Safe maintenance. | Request middleware | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-030 | View-as sessions can never change passwords or MFA, make payments, send messages, accept terms, submit assessments or applications, export data, change notification preferences or view sealed content; the API enforces this independent of the UI. | Prevent abuse via impersonation. | View-as token scope | [PROP] |
| BR-ADM-031 | Help articles have an owner and review date (180 days); overdue articles are labeled; retired articles redirect; audience-gated articles are not served to unauthorized visitors. | Content accuracy. | KB service | [PROP] |
| BR-ADM-032 | Staff access is recertified quarterly; unreviewed roles unused for 90 days are removed at the deadline; at least two active SAD identities must exist; toxic role combinations need SAD-approved, time-limited exceptions. | Access hygiene. | Access review service | [SRC: Yash 18 PROC-07] [PROP] numbers |
| BR-ADM-033 | Suspending an organization shows a cascade preview and pauses (never deletes) jobs, applications intake and org messaging; candidate data is untouched; reinstatement restores the prior state. | Non-destructive enforcement. | Org admin service | [DER] |
| BR-ADM-034 | Ticket merges keep both ids and thread chronology; a ticket has at most one primary problem link; tickets reopen within 14 days, afterwards a linked new ticket is created. | Clean case history. | Ticket service | [PROP] |

## AIC

Source: [02_MODULES/AIC_AI_Career_Assistant_Matching_Recommendations.md](../02_MODULES/AIC_AI_Career_Assistant_Matching_Recommendations.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-AIC-001 | AI may suggest, draft, explain, summarize and recommend. AI never decides, hires, rejects, disqualifies, penalizes, sanctions or terminates. | Human accountability. | Gateway, sink registry | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.1] |
| BR-AIC-002 | No code path exists from AI output to an authoritative state change (profile, evidence, application status, grade, moderation outcome, payment, publication) without a human confirmation token issued from a user action in the owning module. | Enforced human gate. | Sink registry, CI tests | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.1] |
| BR-AIC-003 | Impact classes are INFORMATION, DRAFT, RECOMMENDATION, ANALYSIS, DECISION_SUPPORT, CONSEQUENTIAL_DECISION; the last is blocked at the gateway. | Governed by impact. | Gateway | [SRC: SSOT §16.7] |
| BR-AIC-004 | AI drafts that will be sent to others or published require the user to review and take the send action; no auto-send, no scheduled AI send, no AI agent that contacts others. Employer-side AI drafts of feedback or rejections require human review before sending. | Prevents unreviewed outbound AI. | Host composers, gateway | [SRC: SSOT BR-221] |
| BR-AIC-005 | Prohibited: autonomous hiring or rejection, autonomous disqualification, real-time behavioral profiling for screening, emotion or sentiment analysis of candidates, resume fabrication, predictive performance scoring, AI grading of peer reviews, AI-decided refunds, AI auto-publishing of courses, inference of protected attributes. | Zero tolerance list. | Gateway deny list, code review | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.2] |
| BR-AIC-006 | No opaque universal talent score. Any fit indicator shows its meaningful dimensions and limitations. | Explainability. | Match output schema | [SRC: SSOT §18.1] |
| BR-AIC-007 | Confidence gates: below 0.5 suppress; 0.5 to 0.7 show with disclaimer; 0.7 and above show with evidence; auto-apply only non-consequential changes at 0.85 or above and only where the user enabled it. | Calibrated trust. | Output validation | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.5] |
| BR-AIC-008 | AI conversation memory, user profile, talent graph and verified evidence are separate. AI suggestions never silently alter verified state. | Integrity of evidence. | Gateway, host APIs | [SRC: SSOT §16.6] |
| BR-AIC-009 | TalentSphere incurs no paid third-party inference cost for a free user unless an explicit active cost policy permits it; no silent paid fallback. | Cost invariant. | Gateway entitlement stage | [SRC: SSOT §16.4] |
| BR-AIC-010 | Execution order: on-device when capable, genuinely free provider quota, user-authorized provider, TalentSphere cloud only when policy permits, non-AI fallback. | Cost and privacy. | Gateway routing | [SRC: SSOT §16.3] |
| BR-AIC-011 | All AI calls go through the gateway; modules hold no provider credentials. | Central control. | Architecture, CI | [SRC: SSOT §16.1] |
| BR-AIC-012 | Data is classified PUBLIC, INTERNAL, PRIVATE, SENSITIVE, RESTRICTED, NEVER-EXTERNAL; context is minimized; SENSITIVE and above never go to external providers; NEVER-EXTERNAL never leaves. | Data boundary. | Context firewall | [SRC: SSOT §16.5] |
| BR-AIC-013 | Mandatory redaction before any external provider call: names, emails, phones, addresses, national ids, configured company exclusions; restored for display only; cannot be disabled. | Privacy. | Context firewall | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.3] |
| BR-AIC-014 | Prompt-injection defenses: sanitization, structural enclosure, canary token, low temperature for extraction and matching, strict output validation; canary leak drops the response, alerts and flags the account for review. | Security. | Gateway | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.4] |
| BR-AIC-015 | Every AI output retains provenance: request id, capability, provider and model, mode, timestamp, data class, context references, policy decision, sources, output, user modifications; suggestions carry rationale, source handles, calibrated confidence, assumptions, redactions, prompt hash. | Auditability. | Provenance service | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.6, §16.8] |
| BR-AIC-016 | Recommendations disclose factors ("why am I seeing this"), never use protected attributes, are dismissible (dismissals train the member's own results), carry a sponsored label if sponsored and never mix sponsored into organic ranking, and engines are replaceable behind a contract. | Trust and flexibility. | Recommendation service | [SRC: SSOT BR-184..188] |
| BR-AIC-017 | Matching order: hard constraints, eligibility, required capabilities, evidence quality, experience, recency, transferable skills, preferences, uncertainty, explainable result. Verified evidence outweighs self-reported; self-attestation counts at 0.5. | Evidence-based matching. | Matching service | [SRC: SSOT §18.1; BR-229] |
| BR-AIC-018 | Recruiter-side AI fit is decision support: opt-in per job or session, labelled, never auto-rejects, never hides candidates, never bulk-actions by fit; recruiters give human reasons for decisions. | No autonomous screening. | ATS integration, matching UI | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT §15.10.1] |
| BR-AIC-019 | While an assessment is AI-prohibited, all AI features deny assistance server-side on any device of the member; context loss fails closed. | Integrity. | Gateway | [SRC: SSOT §17.2, §17.3] |
| BR-AIC-020 | Metadata is always logged (24 months); prompt and response content is stored only in the member's history (default 90 days), or with explicit share, incident need (30 days), or consented de-identified evaluation; no use of member content for advertising or training by TalentSphere or providers; staff access to content needs consent or incident approval and is logged. | Minimization. | Provenance, access service | [PROP] |
| BR-AIC-021 | Matching, ranking, feedback drafting and screening-adjacent capabilities pass a bias audit (counterfactual and outcome tests) before release and quarterly; failing blocks promotion. Groups under 30 are not reported. | Fairness. | Release gate | [PROP] from [SRC: SSOT §18.3] |
| BR-AIC-022 | Every model, prompt template and classifier is registered with a model card, evaluation results and approvals before production use. | Governance. | Model registry | [PROP] |
| BR-AIC-023 | Outputs pass safety filters (harm, leakage, fabricated facts, discrimination); blocked output is replaced with a safe message. | Safety. | Gateway output stage | [DER] |
| BR-AIC-024 | When AI is unavailable, over budget or denied, features fall back to a deterministic non-AI path or show an explicit unavailable state; retries never violate `BR-AIC-009`. | Resilience. | Gateway, engines | [SRC: SSOT §16.3] |
| BR-AIC-025 | AI usage is metered; allowances are set per plan by BIL; global budget guards degrade routes at 80 percent and stop paid routes at 100 percent. | Cost control. | Metering service | [PROP] values `OD-AIC-02` |
| BR-AIC-026 | Members can opt out of AI personalization or AI altogether; no core career-loop step requires AI. | Agency. | Settings, features | [DER] |
| BR-AIC-027 | AI-generated content is labelled; the assistant states it is an AI and never claims actions it did not perform. | Honesty. | UI and gateway | [DER] |
| BR-AIC-028 | Member feedback and dismissals affect that member's own results; aggregate learning uses only consented, de-identified data. | Privacy-preserving learning. | Feedback service | [SRC: SSOT BR-186] [DER] |
| BR-AIC-029 | Interview practice is private; no emotion, tone, voice or face analysis; audio not stored; transcripts kept 30 days by default; never shared with employers or used for matching. | Prevents profiling. | Practice service | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.2] [PROP] |
| BR-AIC-030 | Members aged 16 and 17 use restricted AI: assistant limited to learning and career exploration, no personalization with sensitive attributes, no people recommendations except vetted institution mentors, institution may disable. | Protects minors. | Gateway policy | [PROP] `OD-AIC-03` |
| BR-AIC-031 | Assistant scope is career help; it gives only general information on legal, immigration, medical, tax and investment topics with disclaimers and refuses to forge, deceive, harass or discriminate. | Safe scope. | Assistant policy | [PROP] |
| BR-AIC-032 | Forecasts and plans are conditional and time-bounded, with sources, collection time, geography, population, coverage, methodology and limitations. | Honest uncertainty. | Plan and market outputs | [SRC: SSOT §18.4] |
| BR-AIC-033 | On-device runs send no content; user-authorized providers use only provider-supported authorization (consumer subscriptions are not API rights) and still pass the gateway; SENSITIVE or above runs only on-device or in TalentSphere-controlled infrastructure. | Respect provider terms and privacy. | Gateway, provider adapters | [SRC: SSOT §16.2] |
| BR-AIC-034 | AI incidents are triaged by severity with kill switches; S1 requires capability shutdown within 1 hour and SAD notification. | Rapid containment. | Incident process | [PROP] |
| BR-AIC-035 | Matching and recommendation inputs are limited to an allowlist (profile, verified and self-reported evidence labelled as such, declared preferences, learning and assessment results with consent, limited on-platform behavior). Never used: protected attributes or proxies (name, photo, age, graduation year as age proxy, precise address), health, inferred sensitive traits, private messages, referral tags, practice sessions, assessment integrity signals. | Fairness. | Feature store allowlist | [SRC: SSOT BR-185] [DER] |
| BR-AIC-036 | Candidates are told when employer AI-assisted tools may be used, can see which factors were assessed, and can request human review; the employer must respond within 7 days. | Candidate rights. | ATS integration | [PROP] `OD-AIC-06` |
| BR-AIC-037 | AI-extracted skills are `ai_suggested` until the member confirms, then `self_reported` until verified; unconfirmed suggestions never affect matching. | Evidence honesty. | Skill service | [SRC: SSOT MIG-04, BR-229] [DER] |

## ANL

Source: [02_MODULES/ANL_Analytics_Reporting_Insights.md](../02_MODULES/ANL_Analytics_Reporting_Insights.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-ANL-001 | Every metric has a permanent id, owner role, definition, formula (numerator, denominator, population), source, privacy class, allowed dimensions, consent basis, dedup key, review cadence, integrity check and a decision it supports. A metric without a decision is not registered. Definitions cannot be redefined silently. | One number, one meaning. | Metric registry, query service | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §1 principle 2, §8, §9.1] |
| BR-ANL-002 | Business-critical counts come from server-side domain events (outbox), not client beacons; client events cover only UX interactions the server cannot know. | Accuracy and resistance to blockers and tampering. | Schema registry, ingest | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §1 principle 5, §4.1] |
| BR-ANL-003 | Every analytics field carries a privacy class: P0 no personal data, P1 pseudonymous event, P2 aggregate-only with minimum cohort, P3 special handling (fairness data and anything sensitive). | Proportionate protection. | Data catalogue, ingest | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §6.1] |
| BR-ANL-004 | No aggregate is returned with fewer than `min_cohort_k` distinct people (or the metric's registered unit) in a cell; stricter feature values stay as overrides (learning outcomes 30, career transitions 20); a value below default needs a decision record. | Re-identification control. | Suppression service | [SRC: SSOT BR-178, BR-189, BR-160, V61-04] |
| BR-ANL-005 | Suppression is complementary (hidden cells cannot be derived from totals, siblings or overlapping queries), counts are rounded, and dimensions per query and query budget per client are capped. | Blocks differencing. | Suppression service | [DER] |
| BR-ANL-006 | Tenant users (employer, institution, enterprise) see only their own tenant's analytics; tenancy is enforced in the query service, not the UI; cross-tenant benchmarks are anonymous medians above the cohort minimum. | Tenant isolation. | Query service, tests | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §5 Access; MET-042] |
| BR-ANL-007 | ANL provides no individual-level performance tracking or ranking of recruiters, instructors, support agents, moderators or employees; team-level aggregates only, above the cohort minimum. | Analytics must not become staff surveillance. | Dashboard design review, authz | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §1 principle 4] |
| BR-ANL-008 | Person-keyed product analytics beyond what is needed to operate the service requires consent `analytics.product`; the consent reference travels in the event envelope; without consent only identifier-free aggregate counters are kept; experiments additionally require `analytics.experiments`. | Lawful, transparent collection. | Ingest, flag service | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §6.2 Consent; INV-T15]; legal basis `OD-ANL-02` |
| BR-ANL-009 | Events use the standard envelope and property allowlists; no free text, emails, names, phone numbers, message bodies, resume content or tokens; schema changes are additive only; a breaking change is a new event name. | Safety and stability. | Schema registry, ingest | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §4.1] |
| BR-ANL-010 | Product analytics, operational telemetry and the audit log are separate signals: not merged, not stored together by default, not used for each other's purpose; analytics opt-out never shortens audit retention. | Different bases and risks. | Architecture, access control | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §9.2] |
| BR-ANL-011 | Actors are identified by rotating pseudonymous ids; joins to identity happen only in the restricted zone, for an approved, time-boxed purpose, and are audited. | Limits re-identification. | Warehouse zones, access approvals | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §4.1, §5] |
| BR-ANL-012 | Synthetic, test and staff test traffic is tagged at ingest and excluded from every metric. | Clean numbers. | Ingest | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §4.1] |
| BR-ANL-013 | Ingest is idempotent by `event_id`; loaders are replay-safe; late events are accepted for 7 days and reprocessed. | Exactness. | Ingest | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §4.1]; late window [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-014 | Erasure removes or irreversibly de-identifies a person's person-keyed events (pseudonym mapping destroyed); aggregates are not recomputed but small cells are re-evaluated for suppression. | Data rights with analytic continuity. | Erasure job | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §5 Retention] |
| BR-ANL-015 | Fairness and demographic data is voluntary, separately stored (P3), revocable, never visible to recruiters, never a matching or scoring feature, and purpose-limited to audit. | Fairness measurement without discrimination. | Fairness store, authz | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §6.4; INV-T19] |
| BR-ANL-016 | Outcome and trend statements are labelled descriptive or correlational unless produced by a registered experiment; no guarantee or causal claim appears in the product. | Honesty. | UI templates, copy review | [SRC: SSOT BR-193] |
| BR-ANL-017 | Every widget shows its definition link, data freshness and sample size; stale data (older than twice its cadence) carries a banner; a metric under investigation carries a banner. | Trustworthy dashboards. | Dashboard framework | [DER] |
| BR-ANL-018 | Every experiment is registered with hypothesis, primary metric, guardrails, population, duration and owner and reviewed by its risk class; experiments on ranking, matching, verification, assessment, moderation, pricing, consent or notification frequency need ethics review; forbidden: pay-to-rank, hiding or downgrading verification status, removing match explanations, weakening consent, security, accessibility or integrity, deceptive pricing; matching experiments must show outcome parity before rollout. | Responsible experimentation. | Experiment registry | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §7] |
| BR-ANL-019 | Dark patterns are prohibited in experiments, consent flows and notification design: confirmshaming, fake urgency, pre-ticked consent, hidden unsubscribe, guilt-based streaks. | User dignity. | Review checklist | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §7] |
| BR-ANL-020 | A guardrail breach (opt-out rate, ticket rate, accessibility regressions, SLO burn, AI cost, refund rate) auto-halts the experiment; every experiment has a kill switch effective within 1 minute. | Fast safety stop. | Flag service | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §7]; 1 minute [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-021 | Minors and users in sensitive circumstances are excluded from experiments unless specifically reviewed. | Protect vulnerable users. | Eligibility filter | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §7; OPEN-09] |
| BR-ANL-022 | Exports contain aggregates only, pass suppression, carry definitions, versions and filters, are watermarked, expire in 7 days and are logged in the audit log; individual-level exports exist only as a data subject's own data-rights export. | Prevents leakage. | Export service | [DER]; limits [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-023 | A scheduled report runs with the owner's current permissions and verifies each recipient's current access at send time; when the owner loses access the schedule suspends. | No stale access. | Scheduler | [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-024 | Reports and API calls compile to registered metrics and dimensions and are suppressed after compilation; no filter, grouping or sharing can bypass suppression; non-analysts have no free SQL. | Governed self-service. | Query service | [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-025 | Metric versions are immutable once certified; dashboards pin metric versions; a certified dashboard uses only certified metrics and includes the counter-metrics or guardrails its metrics require; changes show a "What changed" banner. | Stable and explainable numbers. | Registry, dashboard certification | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §8, §9.1]; banner [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-026 | Analytics queries never run on the transactional primary; the analytics store is read-only to application code and separate when volume or isolation requires it. | Protects the product. | Architecture | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §5; OPEN-25] |
| BR-ANL-027 | Alert rules have an owner, an evaluation window and a deduplication window (default 24 hours); alerts on stale or suppressed data do not evaluate. | Alert quality. | Alert engine | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG MET-037]; defaults [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-028 | Certified metrics reconcile to source counts within tolerance (default 0.5%); an inconclusive check counts as failing; failures flag the metric on every surface. | Detect wrong numbers. | Reconciliation jobs | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §5, §9.1]; tolerance [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-029 | Cohort and activity definitions are registered metrics: cohort week by first-event week in tenant time zone, activation within 7 days of registration, "active" per the registered activity list. | Comparable cohorts. | Registry | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG MET-002, MET-022] |
| BR-ANL-030 | Institution and placement analytics are cohort-level; faculty and placement staff cannot see non-consented private job-search data; outcome counts include only consenting students; segments must meet the cohort minimum before any message goes out. | Student privacy. | Authz, segment service | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §6.2 Institution analytics] |
| BR-ANL-031 | The candidate dashboard is private to the candidate, built from their own records, ranks them against no one, and shows peer comparisons only as anonymous aggregates above the cohort minimum. | Candidate dignity. | Authz | [DER] |
| BR-ANL-032 | Learning-to-outcome analytics require at least 30 learners per cell, a feature override stricter than `min_cohort_k`. | Statistical and privacy robustness. | Suppression service | [SRC: SSOT BR-189, V61-04] |
| BR-ANL-033 | Analyst access requires a role, a training attestation, an approved purpose and a time limit; every query is logged; identity joins need separate approval; individual-level data cannot leave the workspace. | Governed analyst access. | Access service | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §5 Access]; attestation [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-034 | Partner API keys and embed tokens are tenant-scoped, rate-limited, hashed at rest, revocable and subject to the same suppression as the UI. | Safe delivery. | API gateway | [PROP] |
| BR-ANL-035 | Time is stored in UTC and displayed in the tenant time zone; grains and fiscal periods follow the tenant calendar; money uses minor units and ISO-4217 currency. | Correct period boundaries. | Query service | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT BR-179] |
| BR-ANL-036 | Cost and revenue metrics are P0 or P2 aggregates readable only by finance and platform roles; forecast values are labelled forecast and never mixed silently with actuals. | Honest finance reporting. | Authz, UI | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG §3.5, §9.1] |
| BR-ANL-037 | Every chart has a data-table alternative, does not rely on color alone, and meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and keyboard operation. | Accessibility. | Component library | [SRC: METRICS_CATALOG MET-041 accessibility defects]; [DER] |

## ASM

Source: [02_MODULES/ASM_Assessments_Challenges_Integrity.md](../02_MODULES/ASM_Assessments_Challenges_Integrity.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-ASM-001 | Every assessment has one AI policy mode: `AI_PROHIBITED`, `AI_RESTRICTED`, `AI_ALLOWED` or `POST_ASSESSMENT_ONLY`. Any assessment that can mint verified evidence must be `AI_PROHIBITED`. While an `AI_PROHIBITED` attempt is active, no answers, solving hints, generated code, debugging, screenshot-to-answer help, alternative solution paths or indirect help may be provided by any platform feature or provider; the restriction is enforced inline in the AI gateway, never only in the UI. | Protect result validity. | Assessment builder, AI gateway | [SRC: SSOT §17.1 to §17.3; V61-22] |
| BR-ASM-002 | Time is server-authoritative: deadlines and durations come from database time; client clocks never extend or shorten them. | Prevent time manipulation. | Attempt service | [SRC: SSOT §17.4] |
| BR-ASM-003 | Answer keys, hidden tests, rubric answer notes and grading configuration never appear in client payloads, logs or exports to candidates; only the grading service and authorized authors can read them. | Prevent leakage. | API, storage | [SRC: SSOT §17.4; VER-024] |
| BR-ASM-004 | A published assessment version is immutable; edits create a new version; running attempts stay on their version. | Fairness and auditability. | Version service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.1] |
| BR-ASM-005 | Evidence may be minted only from `passed` attempts of a `published_eligible` version, non-practice, with integrity level at least L1, AI policy `AI_PROHIBITED`, and no open integrity case. | Honest evidence. | Evidence consumer | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.5; INV-T26] |
| BR-ASM-006 | At most one `in_progress` attempt per (account, assessment); a second concurrent session is refused or replaces the first only where policy allows, and is logged as a signal. | Prevent parallel sessions. | Attempt service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §9] |
| BR-ASM-007 | Autosave is idempotent: the server keeps the highest `clientSeq` per question; writes after the deadline are rejected with `409 attempt_closed`. | Offline tolerance and correctness. | Attempt service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.2] |
| BR-ASM-008 | `deadline_at = started_at + duration × accommodationMultiplier`; the attempt is auto-submitted at the deadline, with lazy deadline checks on any later request. | Deadline correctness regardless of job lag. | Attempt service, scheduler | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.2] |
| BR-ASM-009 | Default attempt limits for standalone assessments: cooldown {24 hours} after a fail and at most {3} attempts per rolling 7 days; certification exams and course quizzes use their own configured policies; practice is unlimited. | Prevent brute-force retries. | Attempt service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.8; SSOT BR-107] [PROP] OD-ASM-04 |
| BR-ASM-010 | Score = points earned divided by points available times 100, rounded half-up to 0.01; pass is inclusive of the threshold; multi-select partial credit = (correct selected minus incorrect selected) over total correct, floored at 0; unanswered scores 0. | Deterministic scoring. | Grading service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.5] |
| BR-ASM-011 | Code, SQL and data are executed only in the isolated sandbox with no network, read-only base filesystem, resource limits, and public tests only for Run; hidden tests run only on Submit and are never revealed. | Safety and fairness. | Sandbox service | [SRC: SSOT BR-049, BR-050, BR-051] |
| BR-ASM-012 | If a code attempt cannot be verified because the runner is unavailable past the retry budget, its state is `unverified`: no score, no pass or fail wording, no evidence; eligible attempts (at most 30 days old) are re-graded when a runner exists. | Never fake a pass. | Judge service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.4; V61-22] |
| BR-ASM-013 | Evidence is never minted from `unverified`, `voided` or `under_review` attempts; at most one mint per attempt (idempotent on attemptId); minting for a flagged pass waits for the integrity decision. | Evidence integrity. | Evidence consumer | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.5; INV-T26, INV-T27] |
| BR-ASM-014 | Integrity signals and AI-detection outputs are indicators for human review, never proof; they cannot fail, void or penalize an attempt automatically. | Fairness. | Integrity services | [SRC: SSOT §17.4] |
| BR-ASM-015 | Every attempt discloses before start the integrity signals collected, AI policy, retake and release rules; the signal set is minimal: no keystroke logging, screen capture or webcam except at L3 with consent. | Transparency and minimization. | Start screen, collectors | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.7] |
| BR-ASM-016 | Remote proctoring applies only to assessments configured at L3, requires explicit consent and a lawful alternative where proctoring is mandatory for a credential, and uses no inference of personal traits. | Privacy and fairness. | Proctoring service | [SRC: SSOT §7 F-45] [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-017 | Similarity and plagiarism checks run asynchronously and open review cases; they never penalize on their own. | Avoid false penalties. | Similarity service | [SRC: SSOT BR-052] |
| BR-ASM-018 | Each integrity decision or grade may be appealed once; an appeal is decided by a reviewer who did not take part in the original decision, within {7 days}. | Independent review. | Appeal service | [SRC: SSOT F-115 step 11; YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.7] |
| BR-ASM-019 | Accommodation multipliers are {1.25, 1.5, 2.0}, stored on the attempt, granted after verification of need, and never shown to employers, recruiters or on shared results and score reports. | Dignity and privacy. | Accommodation service, share views | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.8; BR-T030] |
| BR-ASM-020 | Manual scores reference rubric criteria; the rubric version is pinned to the assessment version and each submission; double grading and moderation apply per policy. | Consistent grading. | Grading service | [DER] |
| BR-ASM-021 | AI grading suggestions are drafts for human graders only, are off by default for evidence-eligible assessments, send no identity or protected attributes, and are never the final grade. | Human accountability. | Grading workbench, AI gateway | [SRC: SSOT §16] [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-022 | Question items have a lifecycle (draft, in review, active, flagged, retired); editing an active item creates a new version; retired items cannot be drawn into new assessments. | Stability of published assessments. | Bank service | [SRC: SSOT BR-113] |
| BR-ASM-023 | Each attempt pins the item versions drawn at start; later edits or retirements never change an attempt in progress or past attempts. | No retroactive edits. | Attempt service | [SRC: SSOT BR-113; F-115 edge cases] |
| BR-ASM-024 | Forms are generated from a stored per-attempt seed (order, options, pool draw) so they are reproducible for audit. | Auditability. | Form generator | [SRC: SSOT §17.4] [DER] |
| BR-ASM-025 | Practice attempts (and mock rounds) never mint evidence and do not count for leaderboards or evidence-related XP. | Separate learning from proof. | Evidence consumer, leaderboard | [SRC: SSOT §9.2 F-08 step 10] |
| BR-ASM-026 | Viewing a full solution before solving marks the challenge `assisted`; assisted solves are excluded from evidence and rankings; hints and solutions are unavailable in `AI_PROHIBITED` graded attempts. | Fair rankings. | Hint service | [DER] |
| BR-ASM-027 | Shared solutions and spoilers may be posted only after the poster has solved the challenge; evidence-eligible and employer-private assessments have no discussion. | Protect assessments. | Discussion service | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-028 | Contest submissions lock at the server-authoritative end time; clock skew never extends; a submission received before the end is judged and counts even if judged later. | Fair contests. | Contest service | [SRC: SSOT BR-139] |
| BR-ASM-029 | Leaderboards include only graded, unflagged, unassisted solves from opted-in display names; voided entries are removed; ties break by earlier achievement time. | Integrity of rankings. | Leaderboard service | [DER] |
| BR-ASM-030 | A certification pass requires the configured score in a single attempt; retake policy is per exam (default cooldown {7 days}); issuance waits for any open integrity case. | Credential credibility. | Certification service | [SRC: SSOT BR-140; F-115] |
| BR-ASM-031 | Certification validity is per definition (default perpetual {OD-ASM-05}); expired and revoked certifications stay verifiable with status and reason class. | Honest verification. | Certification service | [SRC: SSOT OD-18] [DEC-REQ] OD-ASM-05 |
| BR-ASM-032 | An employer may assign an assessment only to a candidate who is an applicant or has opted into employer contact; the candidate sees exactly what the employer will see and may decline without penalty. | Consent. | Assignment service | [SRC: SSOT §3 principles] [DER] |
| BR-ASM-033 | Result shares are scoped, time-bound and revocable; revoked or expired shares return `410`; shares never expose accommodations, raw signals or other attempts. | Candidate control. | Share service | [SRC: SSOT BR-190] [DER] |
| BR-ASM-034 | Skill levels are derived from documented per-skill bands on calibrated assessments; retakes can upgrade a level only through a new qualifying attempt and never overwrite earlier evidence. | No inflation. | Skill mapping | [DER] |
| BR-ASM-035 | Item and assessment statistics are computed after minimum samples {200 attempts, 50 per item}; an assessment becomes `published_eligible` only when reliability, coverage and standard-setting thresholds are met. | Valid measurement. | Calibration jobs | [PROP] OD-ASM-08 |
| BR-ASM-036 | Statistics and fairness reports hide groups smaller than {10} (outcome and demographic analyses {30}); demographic data is voluntary, consented and never inferred. | Privacy and statistical validity. | Analytics services | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-037 | Assessment delivery meets WCAG 2.2 AA; no mandatory fullscreen, camera or microphone below L3; accessible alternatives exist for every item type used in evidence-eligible assessments. | Inclusion. | UI, authoring checks | [SRC: SSOT §21.4; YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §8] |
| BR-ASM-038 | Only allowlisted, pinned language runtimes (image digests) and library sets are used; packages are never installed at run time; deprecated runtimes still serve existing attempts and re-grades. | Reproducibility. | Runtime catalog | [SRC: SSOT BR-024] |
| BR-ASM-039 | Rate limits per user: Run {30 per minute}; Submit {10 per minute}. | Protect the sandbox. | API gateway | [SRC: SSOT §9.2 F-08] |
| BR-ASM-040 | Secure items have exposure caps and rotation; confirmed leaks trigger retirement and review of affected attempts with possible rescoring. | Test security. | Item security service | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-041 | Integrity signals are retained {90 days} unless a case is open. | Minimization. | Retention job | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §8] |
| BR-ASM-042 | Confirmed item defects are remedied by fix, credit or exclusion with rescoring from pinned data; outcome changes are audited and downgrades need human confirmation and notice. | Fair remediation. | Regrade service | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-043 | Employer-authored assessments are labeled and never mint platform-verified evidence; results flow only to the employer by candidate consent. | Prevent borrowed authority. | Evidence consumer | [DER] |
| BR-ASM-044 | Registration for scheduled exams reserves seats atomically; cancellation before the cutoff {24 hours} has no penalty; a no-show consumes an attempt only if the policy states so. | Predictability. | Registration service | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-045 | Identity verification results are stored as result, method, time and provider reference only; images are not stored by ASM; failures route to manual review, never auto-rejection. | Privacy. | Identity service | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-046 | Authors, graders and reviewers cannot grade, review or decide on their own attempts or those of related accounts or the same organization where conflict rules apply. | Independence. | Assignment services | [SRC: YASH-MICRO AC-05-04-53, AC-05-04-54] |
| BR-ASM-047 | A submission snapshot (code, files, hashes) is immutable once submitted; grading and re-grading use the snapshot hash. | Auditability. | Submission service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.3] |
| BR-ASM-048 | The results release policy (score, breakdown, per-question feedback, correct answers) is set per assessment and recorded; for evidence-eligible assessments correct answers are not shown before the retake window closes unless OD-ASM-03 decides otherwise. | Item security vs learning. | Results service | [PROP] OD-ASM-03 |
| BR-ASM-049 | Only published challenges appear in the public catalog; retired challenges remain visible to those who solved them; employer-private and institution-private items are never listed publicly. | Visibility control. | Catalog service | [DER] |
| BR-ASM-050 | Projects, system designs, essays and scenarios graded by humans require a finalized human review before any evidence is minted. | No auto-pass on subjective work. | Evidence consumer | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-051 | Runner results carry a signature and the snapshot hash; the grader verifies both; writes are fenced by job generation so only the highest generation stores a result. | Tamper resistance and concurrency. | Judge service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.3] |
| BR-ASM-052 | Datasets for SQL and data challenges are synthetic or properly licensed and contain no personal data. | Privacy and licensing. | Authoring checks | [DER] |
| BR-ASM-053 | Score reports have a verification id and hash; verification shows the current status of the attempt (valid, under review, voided, revoked). | Honest verification. | Report service | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-054 | Proctoring recordings are retained {30 days} unless a case is open and are accessible only to the vendor and assigned reviewers. | Minimization. | Retention job | [PROP] |
| BR-ASM-055 | Pass thresholds for evidence-eligible assessments are set through a documented standard-setting process (for example Angoff or bookmark) and reviewed when item statistics change materially. | Defensible cut scores. | Publish workflow | [PROP] OD-ASM-08 |
| BR-ASM-056 | The candidate must accept the current rules (AI policy, integrity signals, retake rules) before an evidence-eligible attempt starts; acceptance records the policy version hash. | Informed consent. | Start flow | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.2] |
| BR-ASM-057 | Start and submit endpoints are idempotent with an idempotency key. | Safe retries. | API | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §5] |
| BR-ASM-058 | A voided attempt mints nothing and revokes any evidence or certification minted from it; revocation is propagated to result shares. | Consistency after decisions. | Integrity and evidence services | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-05 §3.5] |

## ATS

Source: [02_MODULES/ATS_Recruiter_Workspace_Hiring_Pipeline.md](../02_MODULES/ATS_Recruiter_Workspace_Hiring_Pipeline.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-ATS-001 | Only users with the Recruiter or Employer Admin role and an active seat may create requisitions and job postings; hiring managers may request or draft only. | Accountability. | API authorization | [SRC: BR-01] |
| BR-ATS-002 | Every ATS record carries `organization_id`; cross-tenant reads and writes are prohibited. | Tenant isolation. | Data layer and policies | [SRC: BR-080, BR-040] |
| BR-ATS-003 | A job posting may be published only against an approved requisition unless org policy explicitly allows requisition-free postings. | Budget control. | Publish command | [DER] |
| BR-ATS-004 | Jobs require an approved organization and a verified owner; verified organizations receive accelerated automatic approval, unverified go to platform review. | Fraud control. | Publish workflow | [SRC: BR-036, BR-062] |
| BR-ATS-005 | Publish readiness is validated server-side: title, description length, location or eligibility, employment type, level, 3+ skills, pay where required, apply method, hiring manager, no hard-fail language. | Quality and law. | Publish command | [SRC: BR-10] |
| BR-ATS-006 | Where a job location falls under a pay-disclosure rule, pay range is mandatory and cannot be hidden. | Pay transparency law. | Readiness check | [DER] [DEC-REQ OD-JOB-07] |
| BR-ATS-007 | Posting lifecycle changes are server-owned and follow SM-ATS-02; only own-organization postings may be changed. | Integrity. | Domain command | [SRC: BR-11, BR-12] |
| BR-ATS-008 | Postings auto-close after expiry; default 60 days, configurable 14 to 90. | Freshness. | Scheduler | [SRC: BR-057; OD-JOB-03] |
| BR-ATS-009 | Reposting creates a new posting version for the same requisition, preserves applicants, and is blocked while another posting is active for the same requisition and location. | No duplicates. | Repost command | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-010 | Posting text is linted: explicit protected-attribute requirements are hard-fail; biased wording is a warning needing a recorded reason to dismiss. | Non-discrimination. | Authoring, publish | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-011 | Every pipeline stage maps to exactly one system category and thereby to one candidate-visible status. | Consistent status. | Pipeline config validation | [DER] [SRC: V61-18] |
| BR-ATS-012 | Stage transitions are server-owned, validated, idempotent and append a status event; backward moves need a reason; invalid transitions are blocked. | Auditability. | Transition command | [SRC: BR-17, BR-041, BR-20] |
| BR-ATS-013 | Rejection and other terminal dispositions require a reason category from the managed taxonomy. | Candidate feedback and reporting. | Command | [SRC: BR-217] |
| BR-ATS-014 | Rejection messages send with a configurable delay (default 24 hours); a candidate must be notified of rejection; free text is visible only to the candidate. | Dignity, correctness. | Message scheduler | [SRC: BR-045, BR-219] [PROP: mandatory notice] |
| BR-ATS-015 | Automation rules may not reject or rank candidates; the only automated decline is a knockout decline on approved objective rule types in strict mode, with human review on request. | Human oversight. | Rule validator | [SRC: BR-171] [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-016 | Scorecards, notes and ratings are private to the hiring team and never candidate-visible. | Candour. | Projection, API | [SRC: BR-19] |
| BR-ATS-017 | Blind review (default on): a reviewer cannot see others' scorecards before submitting their own. | Independent judgment. | Scorecard API | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-018 | Submitted scorecards are immutable; changes happen by addendum (compensating entry). | Evidence integrity. | Scorecard service | [SRC: BR-174] |
| BR-ATS-019 | Candidate comparison uses structured rubrics only; no free-form scores or automated overall ranking. | Fair comparison. | Comparison service | [SRC: BR-176] |
| BR-ATS-020 | Notes are visible only to the job's hiring team; mentions grant no access; they may be subject to data access requests. | Privacy. | Notes service | [SRC: BR-19] [DER] |
| BR-ATS-021 | Bulk actions: max 500 items per batch; preview for more than 25 items or any reject/email; per-item results; no silent partial imports. | Safety. | Batch service | [SRC: BR-077] [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-022 | Outreach to sourced candidates only if the candidate's visibility permits and the employer is not blocked; opt-outs are honored globally for 12 months. | Consent. | Sourcing and outreach | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-023 | Talent pool membership requires a lawful basis (consent or sourced with notice within 30 days) and expires after 12 months unless renewed. | Data protection. | Pool service | [DER] |
| BR-ATS-024 | Duplicate candidates are never merged automatically; merges are human-confirmed and reversible for 30 days. | Accuracy. | Duplicate service | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-025 | An offer can be created only after required scorecards for the offer stage are complete. | Evidence before offer. | Offer command | [SRC: BR-042] |
| BR-ATS-026 | Offers follow an approval chain; approvers cannot approve their own offers; material edits void prior approvals; approval records are immutable. | Control. | Approval engine | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-027 | One active offer per application. | Clarity. | Unique constraint | [SRC: SSOT F-06 step 6] |
| BR-ATS-028 | Offers have a mandatory expiry (default 7 days); expiry is automatic. | Closure. | Scheduler | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-029 | Offer letters are immutable snapshots tied to an offer version; letter pay must match offer pay; e-sign is through a connected provider. | Consistency. | Letter service | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-030 | Hired requires an accepted offer; hiring decrements headcount, closes the requisition at zero and closes other applications for that requisition. | Integrity. | Hire command | [DER] |
| BR-ATS-031 | SLA defaults: review within 5 business days; interviewer reminder at 3 and escalation at 7; candidate non-response reminders at 5 and flag at 8; escalations propose, never auto-change status. | Candidate experience. | SLA job | [SRC: BR-069, BR-070 partly] [PROP; OD-ATS-03] |
| BR-ATS-032 | Requisitions inactive more than 21 days are flagged; at 30 days postings are auto-paused with notice. | Prevent abandoned requisitions. | Aging job | [SRC: BR-071] |
| BR-ATS-033 | Self-identification data is voluntary, stored separately, never visible to reviewers, never an input to search, rules, AI or scoring. | Fairness. | Data model and API | [DER] [SRC: BR-172] |
| BR-ATS-034 | Adverse-impact monitoring uses the four-fifths screening rule with minimum sample sizes; results are for governance, not individual decisions. | Compliance. | Reporting | [DER] |
| BR-ATS-035 | Retention: unsuccessful applications default 24 months after close (6 to 36 allowed); legal hold overrides purge; purge removes personal data but keeps aggregates and pseudonymous audit. | Data minimization. | Purge job | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-036 | Candidate rights requests are fulfilled within 30 days (one documented extension); erasure completes in all stores and indexes within 24 hours of execution unless a legal exception applies. | GDPR. | Rights workflow | [SRC: BR-063] [DER] |
| BR-ATS-037 | Every state-changing command writes an immutable audit entry in the same transaction. | Accountability. | Command layer | [SRC: BR-067] |
| BR-ATS-038 | AI output is advisory, labelled, confidence thresholds apply (below 0.5 suppressed, below 0.7 disclaimer), excludes protected attributes, and never decides stage, rejection or ranking. | Safe AI. | AI gateway | [SRC: BR-065, BR-066, BR-171, BR-172, BR-221] |
| BR-ATS-039 | Candidate documents are scanned before extraction and served only from scanned copies via signed URLs. | Security. | File service | [SRC: BR-043, BR-044] |
| BR-ATS-040 | Access to a job's candidates is limited to its hiring team and EAD; interviewers see only candidates in their assigned stages by default. | Least privilege. | Access policy | [SRC: BR-040, BR-12] [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-041 | Report cohorts below 10 are labelled small sample and demographic cells below 10 are suppressed. | Privacy. | Reporting | [SRC: BR-207, BR-220 principle] |
| BR-ATS-042 | Agency submissions create applications only after candidate consent; attribution goes to the first confirmed submission within the agreement window. | Fairness and consent. | Submission service | [PROP; OD-ATS-07] |
| BR-ATS-043 | Outreach sequences have at most 4 steps, stop on reply or application, include an opt-out, and are capped per recruiter per day (default 100). | Anti-spam. | Outreach service | [PROP; OD-ATS-06] |
| BR-ATS-044 | Recruiters see verified signals, labelled by provenance; unverified claims are marked; reputation data appears only with candidate consent or an active application. | Honesty and consent. | Evidence API | [SRC: BR-064, BR-167] |
| BR-ATS-045 | Candidate privacy settings are honored: blocked employers cannot source or contact; sourcing visibility off excludes the candidate; external boards and agencies receive no data without consent. | Candidate control. | Sourcing, distribution, submission | [PROP] aligned [SRC: BR-JOB-036] |
| BR-ATS-046 | Every job posting save creates a retained revision; published versions are never overwritten. | Traceability. | Authoring service | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-047 | Blind screening mode masks identity fields server-side until the configured reveal stage; reveal is logged. | Bias reduction. | Projection | [PROP] |
| BR-ATS-048 | Previous applications by the same candidate to the same org are shown only to authorized reviewers, within retention, with an anchoring warning, and may be turned off by org policy. | Fair review. | Application detail | [PROP] |

## BGV

Source: [02_MODULES/BGV_Verification_Background_Checks.md](../02_MODULES/BGV_Verification_Background_Checks.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-BGV-001 | No check is ordered without a valid, specific, informed consent from the candidate that names the check types, the requesting employer, the vendor(s) and the purpose. Consent is per request and expires with it. | Lawful basis, trust. | Order service (rejects orders not covered by consent) | [SRC: SSOT §6 Consent "purpose-bound, versioned"]; [DER] |
| BR-BGV-002 | The disclosure is a standalone document in the candidate's language, versioned and hash-stored. Biometric processing needs its own separate consent. | Clear, uncluttered disclosure. | Consent flow | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-003 | A check may be ordered only if the jurisdiction rule pack permits that type at the current stage (for example after a conditional offer where required). Unknown jurisdiction blocks sensitive checks. Rule engine failure blocks ordering. | Fair-chance and timing laws. | Rule engine at initiation and order | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-004 | Employers may order only check types enabled in the catalog and included in a package approved for the role family; checks must be justified by the role. | Proportionality. | Package builder; initiation | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-005 | Criminal check scope follows the strictest applicable rule pack: lookback, convictions versus arrests, and exclusion of sealed, expunged and juvenile records. The platform filters out-of-scope records even if a vendor returns them. | Legal scope control. | Result normalizer | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-006 | The platform makes no automated hiring decision and provides no pass/fail score from check results. Humans adjudicate. | Accountability. | Product design; ATS integration blocks auto-rejection from BGV status | [DER] |
| BR-BGV-007 | Before any adverse decision based on a report, an individualized assessment (nature and gravity, time elapsed, relevance to duties, accuracy, rehabilitation evidence) with written rationale is required; discrepancies and potential matches go to the candidate for explanation before being treated as findings. | Fairness; contestability. | Adjudication case workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-008 | A pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the report and rights information is sent before a final adverse action, followed by a waiting period (default 5 business days, rule-pack override) during which the candidate can respond or dispute. | Opportunity to respond. | Notice workflow; final-adverse guard | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-009 | A final adverse action notice with required content is sent and recorded before the ATS rejection reason `background_check` is stored. | Compliance trail. | Notice workflow; ATS integration | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-010 | A candidate dispute is forwarded to the vendor within 1 business day, pauses adverse action, and the vendor has 30 days to reinvestigate. Disputed items are excluded from adjudication until resolved. | Accuracy and fairness. | Dispute workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-011 | A candidate may always obtain a copy of their report (while retained) through the secure portal after step-up authentication. | Transparency. | Portal | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-012 | Only users with the adjudicator permission in the ordering organization can view report content, with a reason code and step-up authentication; other users see status only. Support agents never see content. | Least privilege. | Report viewer authz | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-013 | Check results and adjudication data never appear in profiles, search, matching, recommendations, reputation or analytics. The only public artifact is the opt-in "Identity verified" mark. | Prevents discriminatory spillover. | Architecture boundary; contract tests on other modules' payloads | [DER] |
| BR-BGV-014 | Identity documents and biometrics stay with the vendor under contract; the platform stores only the assurance result, document type, country, dates and a name hash.
