Biometric consent is explicit and a non-biometric alternative is always offered. | Minimization of sensitive data. | Identity adapter and storage | [SRC: SSOT §15 privacy by purpose]; [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-015 | The identity mark is opt-in, shows only "Identity verified" with date, is valid 24 months, and is withdrawn on legal-name change until re-verified. | Controlled disclosure. | Badge service | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-016 | Prior verified results may be reused only when still valid (identity 24 months, employment 12 months, education until disputed), meeting the employer's minimum level, and with the candidate's per-employer consent. Criminal results are never reused across employers. | Avoids stale or out-of-context data. | Reuse resolver | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-017 | Verification outcomes are `verified`, `discrepancy`, `unable_to_verify` (not adverse in itself) or `in_progress`. Minor format differences are normalized before a discrepancy is raised. | Avoid false negatives. | Normalizer | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-018 | A candidate's decision to decline or withdraw consent is recorded neutrally; employers see only "declined" and the platform shows an information text that the employer should apply policy uniformly. | Avoid penalizing privacy choices unfairly. | Consent flow; employer UI | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-019 | Reference checks contact only candidate-nominated referees, use approved questionnaires without protected-attribute topics, and responses are confidential to the hiring team. | Fairness and confidentiality. | Reference service | [DER] from SSOT F-94 |
| BR-BGV-020 | A candidate's current employer is never contacted without explicit permission for that check. The prospective employer's name is disclosed to verifiers only if the candidate agreed. | Protects candidates' current jobs. | Employment check; reference check | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-021 | Right-to-work checks collect only what the national method requires, are applied to all hires uniformly, and are not started before the permitted stage. | Non-discrimination. | Right-to-work service; rule engine | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-022 | Only vendors that are contracted, security-reviewed and registered with declared countries, check types, data residency and retention terms may be used. | Third-party risk. | Vendor registry | [SRC: SSOT §13.4 integration layer]; [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-023 | Orders are idempotent per (request, check type); vendor webhooks are signature-verified, replay-protected (5-minute window), deduplicated by vendor event id and applied in order. | Exactly-once effects. | Order service; webhook intake | [DER] |
| BR-BGV-024 | Only data needed for the check is sent to the vendor; national ids and similar identifiers are entered on vendor-hosted forms and not stored by the platform. | Minimization. | Adapters | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-025 | All BGV data is classified Restricted: encrypted at rest with field-level keys, stored apart from general data, never copied to analytics stores, and accessed through audited services. | Sensitive data protection. | Storage design | [SRC: SSOT §15 field-level encryption]; [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-026 | Retention defaults (to be set by jurisdiction): report content and raw payloads deleted 12 months after final decision (90 days if no decision); consent, notices and adjudication records kept 5 years or the legal minimum; identity assurance kept for its validity period; unfinished requests purged 30 days after expiry. Legal hold overrides. | Data minimization with legal defensibility. | Retention job | [PROP]; [DEC-REQ] OD-BGV-06 |
| BR-BGV-027 | Candidates may request access, correction and deletion; deletion is refused only for records within a legal minimum retention, and the response states which categories remain and until when. | Data rights. | DSAR handler with SET | [SRC: SSOT §15.9 privacy]; [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-028 | A check invitation expires after 30 days without consent; an in-progress request expires 60 days after consent; a result may be used in a decision for 90 days from completion; older results require a re-run with fresh consent. | Currency of data. | Scheduler; adjudication guard | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-029 | Withdrawal of consent before ordering cancels the request with no vendor call; after ordering it triggers vendor cancellation and quarantine and deletion of any results received. | Honor consent. | Lifecycle service | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-030 | Cancellation costs follow the vendor terms and are recorded in the ledger; employers are shown the possible cost before cancelling after order. | Transparency. | Billing hook | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-031 | Employers see an estimate before ordering and pay for employer-initiated checks; candidates are not charged. Candidate-initiated portable verification is priced via BIL (planned). Orders do not proceed if billing is inactive. | Clear economics. | Billing hook | [PROP]; amounts [DEC-REQ] (BIL) |
| BR-BGV-032 | Fair-hiring monitoring uses aggregates only; cells below k (default 10) are suppressed; no protected attribute is stored by BGV. | Monitoring without profiling. | Analytics job | [SRC: SSOT BR-158 k ≥ 10 default]; [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-033 | Employer-ordered checks cannot be run on subjects under 18; criminal checks are never available for minors. | Child protection. | Eligibility check using IDN age flag | [DER] |
| BR-BGV-034 | Every consent, order, status change, report view, decision, notice, dispute and configuration change is written to an append-only, hash-chained audit log. A failed audit write fails the action. Staff break-glass access needs a case reason and notifies the candidate and the org admin. | Accountability. | Audit service | [SRC: SSOT BR-67]; [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-035 | Sanctions and watchlist screening is available only to organizations that attest a regulatory basis for the role family and covers official lists only; a potential match is a lead requiring human confirmation. | Narrow scope, avoid false positives. | Package builder; adjudication | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-036 | Rule packs, vendor enablement and go-live need two different approvers, are versioned with effective dates, and in-flight requests keep their pinned version unless law requires otherwise. | Change control. | Admin console | [SRC: SSOT BR-29 confirmation + audit]; [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-037 | A vendor may be replaced or failed over only to vendors listed in the consent disclosure; otherwise the candidate must re-consent. | Consent specificity. | Router | [PROP] |
| BR-BGV-038 | Check data is never used for advertising, product analytics beyond operational metrics, model training or any purpose beyond the consented check. | Purpose limitation. | Data access policy; audits | [SRC: SSOT §15.2 privacy by purpose]; [PROP] |

## BIL

Source: [02_MODULES/BIL_Billing_Plans_Entitlements.md](../02_MODULES/BIL_Billing_Plans_Entitlements.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-BIL-001 | Entitlements derive only from verified provider state, contract grants, seat pools or the free default; never from client claims or redirects. | Prevents free access and spoofing. | Entitlement resolver | [SRC: BR-056; docs/PRICING.md] |
| BR-BIL-002 | Subscription and order state is webhook-owned; a checkout success redirect grants nothing. | Provider is the source of truth. | Checkout return handler, webhook handlers | [SRC: BR-32] |
| BR-BIL-003 | Provider events are verified by signature, stored once by provider event id, processed idempotently and tolerate out-of-order delivery. | Zero double-billing. | Webhook endpoint | [SRC: SCI-06; F-16] |
| BR-BIL-004 | No plan, coupon, contract or grant may sell credibility, verification level, hiring or search rank, assessment bypass, access to private evidence, or moderation outcomes. | Platform trust; SSOT bans opaque pay-to-rank. | Integrity guard at publish and grant | [SRC: docs/PRICING.md invariants; §4.2] |
| BR-BIL-005 | Published price versions are immutable; price changes create new versions with an effective date. | Auditability and fairness. | Price book service | [DER] |
| BR-BIL-006 | Money is integer minor units with an ISO 4217 currency; one currency per subscription. | Avoids rounding errors. | Domain money type | [SRC: CON-010] |
| BR-BIL-007 | Upgrades apply immediately with proration; downgrades and cheaper interval changes apply at period end by default. | Fairness and predictable revenue. | Subscription change service | [SRC: BR-055] |
| BR-BIL-008 | Downgrade or lapse never deletes user data; over-limit resources become read-only or paused after notice and the owner chooses which to keep. | Trust and data safety. | Plan change and limit services | [SRC: docs/PRICING.md "downgrades do not unpublish"] [DER] |
| BR-BIL-009 | Entitlements follow the billing owner of the covered context: personal plan for the individual, organization plan for covered members within the organization. | Resolves the per-user versus per-organization gap. | Resolver | [SRC: docs/PRICING.md review note] [DEC-REQ] OD-BIL-06 |
| BR-BIL-010 | One trial per user per plan family and per payment fingerprint. | Abuse control. | Trial service | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-011 | Coupons cannot reduce a price below the platform minimum, exceed `coupon_max_percent` (default 75), or be redeemed more than allowed. | Margin protection. | Coupon service | [SRC: BR-099; OD-43] |
| BR-BIL-012 | Course purchase refunds: full within the window at or below the progress threshold, pro-rated within the window otherwise (defaults 30 days, 20 percent). | Published fair policy. | Refund policy engine | [SRC: BR-100; OD-29] |
| BR-BIL-013 | Failed payments follow the dunning schedule; after the grace period paid entitlements resolve to free values; data is retained. | Clear consequences. | Dunning service, resolver | [SRC: docs/PRICING.md] [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-014 | Card data never touches TalentSphere systems; only provider tokens and masked display data are stored. | PCI scope minimization. | Checkout and portal design | [DER] |
| BR-BIL-015 | Tax is calculated by the tax engine at checkout; no tax is collected in an unregistered jurisdiction; no assumed rates. | Compliance. | Tax service | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-016 | Finalized invoices are immutable; corrections are credit notes and new invoices; numbering is gapless per issuing entity and year. | Legal validity. | Invoice service | [DER] |
| BR-BIL-017 | Seat and organization-limit consumption is atomic: assigned seats never exceed total and limits never oversell under concurrency. | Fairness and revenue integrity. | Row locks, check constraints | [SRC: BR-074] |
| BR-BIL-018 | Institutional and enterprise prices come from the price book (volume tiers per package) or an approved quote; never hard-coded. | Pricing is configurable and OD-gated. | Price book, quote service | [SRC: BR-081; OD-15] |
| BR-BIL-019 | No paid inference for a free user without an explicit active cost policy; AI quota is reserved before the call and settled after. | Cost control. | AI meter | [SRC: §16.4; Amendment C] |
| BR-BIL-020 | Usage meters are durable, atomic, idempotent on usage event key and use documented windows with reset time shown to users. | Accurate limits across instances. | Meter service | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-021 | Outreach caps are weekly per seat, values from the plan; custom values only by contract. | Anti-spam and plan clarity. | Outreach check | [SRC: BR-130] |
| BR-BIL-022 | Refunds and adjustments above `refund_dual_approval_amount` or `adjustment_dual_approval_amount`, and all entitlement grants above bounds, need a second approver who is not the proposer. | Fraud and error control. | Approval workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-023 | Refunds return to the original payment method; credits are goodwill only, non-withdrawable and expiring per policy. | Anti-laundering. | Refund and credit services | [DER] |
| BR-BIL-024 | Earner balances carry a hold period, require completed payout onboarding, and are subject to clawback for refunds and disputes. | Protects against reversals. | Payout service | [SRC: WF-28; BR-101] [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-025 | Holding funds for third-party work (escrow) is not part of ordinary balances and exists only if the escrow decision gate is approved. | Regulatory and non-goal risk. | Payout service feature flag | [DEC-REQ] OD-BIL-10 |
| BR-BIL-026 | Every gated capability checks one registered entitlement key on the server; UI hints are never authoritative; an unregistered key is an error. | No UI-only gating. | Enforcement-point registry | [SRC: CLAUDE rule business rules in domain] |
| BR-BIL-027 | Seat revocation, grace and release follow INS rules; BIL only returns seats to the pool and expires pools. | Single owner per rule. | Seat service | [SRC: BR-073, BR-075] |
| BR-BIL-028 | Region and currency come from the billing country, validated against card issuer and tax evidence, never from IP alone. | Prevents price arbitrage and tax errors. | Checkout, region service | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-029 | Reconciliation never changes money silently; discrepancies become items resolved by authorized actions. | Auditable books. | Reconciliation service | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-030 | Ledger entries are append-only and balanced; corrections are reversing entries in the open period. | Accounting integrity. | Ledger service | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-031 | Enterprise custom terms are stored as contract grants with expiry; no hidden manual flags; quotes are documents, not a pipeline. | Visibility and non-goal protection. | Contract and grant services | [DER] [SRC: §4.2] |
| BR-BIL-032 | Billing records are retained for the statutory period (default 7 years) with minimized personal fields after account deletion. | Legal obligation. | Retention job | [PROP] OD-BIL-02 |
| BR-BIL-033 | Billing actions follow the buyer's context: candidates and learners buy personal plans and courses, employers buy employer plans, institutions buy seats; roles without a billing capability cannot purchase. | Resolves legacy BR-07. | Authorization layer | [SRC: BR-07 conflict] [DEC-REQ] OD-BIL-11 |
| BR-BIL-034 | Test mode and live mode are isolated: data, keys and webhooks never cross; live requires explicit enablement. | Prevents accidental charges. | Environment guard | [SRC: docs/PRICING.md] |
| BR-BIL-035 | Organizations without a subscription are limited by `free_active_jobs_limit`; the value is undecided and the decision is recorded. | Legacy policy gap. | Limit service | [SRC: docs/PRICING.md] [DEC-REQ] OD-BIL-05 |
| BR-BIL-036 | Region rules decide tax display, reverse charge for valid business tax ids and invoice wording. | Compliance. | Tax and invoice services | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-037 | A higher price for an existing subscriber needs at least 30 days' notice before renewal. | Consumer fairness. | Price change scheduler | [PROP] |
| BR-BIL-038 | Trial parameters (days, card required, access on cancel) are per plan and never inferred. | Configurable policy. | Plan version | [PROP] OD-BIL-04 |

## EMP

Source: [02_MODULES/EMP_Employer_Organisation_Teams_Brand.md](../02_MODULES/EMP_Employer_Organisation_Teams_Brand.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-EMP-001 | An organisation is created by a verified person who becomes its owner (EAD) and must accept the terms and data notice; every organisation has at least one active EAD at all times. | Accountability. | Org creation, member removal | [DER] |
| BR-EMP-002 | Unverified organisations may draft jobs but cannot publish without platform review; limits on active jobs and sourcing apply until verified. | Fraud control. | Publish workflow | [SRC: BR-036, BR-062] [PROP: limits] |
| BR-EMP-003 | Verification requires domain control proof plus at least one of registry match or reviewed legal documents; verified status is revalidated at least every 12 months and on risk triggers. | Authenticity. | Verification service | [PROP] [SRC: BR-036] |
| BR-EMP-004 | Members must use an email on an allowed org domain unless an expiring EAD-approved exception exists; free-mail domains are not accepted for employer accounts. | Identity integrity. | Invitation and sign-in | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-005 | Company profile, brand and review-response content is scanned and moderated; prohibited content (hate, discrimination, personal data, misleading claims, scams) is rejected. | Safety. | Content services | [SRC: BR-083 pattern] [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-006 | Company slugs are unique, permanent (with redirects), and reserved or protected names cannot be claimed. | Trust. | Slug service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-007 | Custom careers domains require DNS verification and enforce HTTPS; removal restores the default URL. | Security. | Domain service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-008 | Brand media requires alt text and captions; featuring a person requires their recorded, revocable consent honored within 24 hours of withdrawal; contrast and accessibility checks must pass before publishing careers pages. | Accessibility and consent. | Publishing checks | [SRC: BR-079 consent pattern] [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-009 | Embeds and feeds serve only published jobs, check an origin allowlist, and set no tracking cookies on third-party sites. | Privacy and safety. | Embed service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-010 | Unclaimed company profiles are labelled; claims need domain proof; disputes lock sensitive edits until resolved by PAD. | Fair ownership. | Claim workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-011 | Invitations are single-use, bound to the invited email, expire in 7 days and can be revoked; max 200 pending. | Access control. | Invitation service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-012 | Seat assignment is atomic and never oversells the last seat; released seats return immediately; members keep read-only access to their past work for 7 days after release. | Commercial integrity. | Seat service | [SRC: BR-074, BR-075 pattern] [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-013 | Built-in roles are fixed; custom roles cannot exceed the creator's permissions; the last EAD cannot be removed or demoted; billing roles have no candidate data access. | Least privilege. | Role service | [SRC: BR-078 pattern] [DER] |
| BR-EMP-014 | Permission and role changes take effect within 60 seconds and are audit logged; sensitive actions require re-authentication. | Security. | Authorization layer | [SRC: BR-09, BR-067] [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-015 | Approval policies are versioned; changes apply to new requests only; a policy must resolve to at least one approver who is not the requester. | Fairness and control. | Policy service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-016 | Organisation data is scoped by `organization_id`; sub-organisations are isolated unless sharing is explicitly enabled with candidate notice; no cross-tenant reads. | Tenant isolation. | Data layer | [SRC: BR-080] |
| BR-EMP-017 | Organisation hiring policies must lie within platform minimum and maximum bounds, and location-specific legal rules override org settings. | Compliance. | Policy validation | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-018 | An agency acts only within an active, client-approved relationship scope and permissions; each request carries a client context that is authorized. | Consent and isolation. | Authorization layer | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-019 | Agencies see only their own submitted candidates and the client jobs in scope; clients see agency attribution; no cross-client data for agencies. | Privacy. | Agency workspace | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-020 | Terminating a relationship ends agency access immediately; the agency retains only records of candidates it submitted; the DPA governs the remainder. | Data control. | Relationship service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-021 | Only people with a verified relationship (employee via EVD or work email, applicant or interviewee via platform records, contractor) may review; one review per relationship per 12 months. | Authentic reviews. | Review service | [DER] [SRC: F-75] |
| BR-EMP-022 | Anonymous reviews hide the reviewer's identity from the employer and public, never from PAD and legal process. | Safe speech. | Review storage and API | [SRC: BR-136] |
| BR-EMP-023 | Company responses are appended and never edit the original review; one response and one follow-up per review. | Fairness. | Review service | [SRC: BR-137] |
| BR-EMP-024 | Reputation components and ratings are shown publicly only when at least 10 data points support them; badges derive from objective thresholds and cannot be purchased or hidden. | Statistical honesty. | Reputation service | [SRC: BR-207, BR-180 principle] [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-025 | Employers cannot delete or edit reviews; they may flag them; removal occurs only by moderation under published guidelines. | Integrity. | Moderation workflow | [DER] |
| BR-EMP-026 | Candidate experience ratings are shown to employers only as de-identified aggregates with sample at least 10, never to the recruiters who handled the candidate. | Anti-retaliation. | Reporting | [PROP] aligns [SRC: BR-220] |
| BR-EMP-027 | Entitlements come only from BIL subscription state (webhook-owned); limits are enforced server-side; downgrades restrict creation but never delete data. | Commercial integrity. | Entitlement service | [SRC: BR-032, BR-055, BR-056] |
| BR-EMP-028 | A signed DPA (where required) is a precondition for accessing received applications after 14 days; new versions require re-acceptance within 30 days; sub-processor changes are notified 30 days ahead. | Legal compliance. | Gate in ATS access | [PROP] [DEC-REQ OD-EMP-03] |
| BR-EMP-029 | Webhooks are https-only, HMAC-signed, retried with backoff over 24 hours, auto-disabled after 50 consecutive failures, and carry minimal personal data. | Reliability and privacy. | Webhook service | [SRC: BR-31] [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-030 | API keys and connectors are org-bound, scope-limited, never exceed the creator's permissions, are shown once, stored hashed, rotatable and logged. | Least privilege. | Key service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-031 | SCIM deactivation removes access within 5 minutes; SSO enforcement requires a tested configuration and a break-glass owner with 2FA. | Prompt de-provisioning. | SSO service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-032 | Security policies (2FA, session limits, IP rules) are enforced server-side; dangerous actions require re-authentication. | Security. | Auth layer | [DER] |
| BR-EMP-033 | Employer audit entries are append-only, tamper-evident, and retained 7 years. | Accountability. | Audit service | [SRC: BR-067] [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-034 | Names, domains and logos are screened for lookalikes against verified organisations and a protected-brand list before verification. | Anti-impersonation. | Screening service | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-035 | Sanctions are proportionate (warning, restrict, suspend, terminate); termination needs dual PAD approval; every sanction offers one appeal reviewed by a different PAD; affected candidates are informed neutrally. | Due process. | Sanction workflow | [SRC: BR-068, BR-29] |
| BR-EMP-036 | Security, legal and approval-deadline notifications are mandatory and cannot be disabled by members. | Safety. | Notification layer | [PROP] |
| BR-EMP-037 | Employer analytics are aggregate-only with k at least 10 and offer no demographic breakdown. | Privacy. | Analytics service | [SRC: BR-207, BR-201] |
| BR-EMP-038 | On closure the owner may export all data; export completes within 30 days; a 30-day cooling-off precedes deletion; candidate data is purged per retention rules. | Data rights. | Closure workflow | [SRC: BR-063] [PROP] |

## ENT

Source: [02_MODULES/ENT_Enterprise_Talent_Internal_Mobility.md](../02_MODULES/ENT_Enterprise_Talent_Internal_Mobility.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-ENT-001 | Enterprise features require a verified employer organization and an active enterprise entitlement; without either, no enterprise data is created or readable. | Commercial and trust gate. | Workspace service, entitlement check | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-002 | ENT never stores or processes payroll, compensation, benefits, performance ratings, disciplinary or grievance records, leave, attendance or time-tracking data. HRIS import allow-lists, forms and free-text scanning enforce a blocklist. | Stays inside the SSOT non-goal on generic HR/payroll. | Import allow-list, schema, text scanner | [SRC: SSOT §4.2]; [DER] |
| BR-ENT-003 | A person's personal TalentSphere account belongs to the person. The enterprise sees only an enterprise-scoped projection: HRIS attributes, the enterprise skills inventory, assigned learning, and data the person has explicitly shared. | Privacy boundary between employee and employer. | Projection service, authz | [DER] |
| BR-ENT-004 | HRIS-sourced attributes (org unit, manager, job profile, status) are read-only in ENT; the HRIS is the source of truth; ENT writes nothing back except an optional transfer request message. | Avoids a shadow HRIS. | Sync service | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-005 | Skills data reaches the enterprise only through the enterprise inventory, with per-entry visibility choices; personal-profile evidence is visible only if the employee shares it per skill; aggregate use excludes employees who hid entries. | Consent and control. | Inventory authz | [PROP] (`OD-ENT-05`) |
| BR-ENT-006 | A manager endorsement or self-attested step is labelled as such and is never presented as verified evidence. | Evidence honesty. | UI templates, API labels | [SRC: SSOT §6.1] |
| BR-ENT-007 | Internal eligibility rules use only job-related, documented attributes (tenure in role up to the policy cap, job family, location, language, required skills) and never protected attributes or proxies. | Fair opportunity. | Posting validation | [DER] |
| BR-ENT-008 | Internal applications and gig applications are confidential from the applicant's current manager and from HR partners unless org policy allows HR visibility and the applicant is told before submitting. | Protects employees who explore moves. | Authz, UI disclosure | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-009 | The current manager is notified at the policy stage (default: offer accepted) and the release date is agreed within the policy cap (default 60 days). | Orderly transfers. | Workflow engine | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-010 | Internal applicants receive a decision and feedback within the SLA (default 10 business days); breaches escalate to the talent admin. | Fair treatment and transparency. | SLA scheduler | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-011 | Matching suggestions are opt-in for employees, explained with reasons, never auto-decide, use no performance or protected data, and can be hidden by the employee at any time. | No ungoverned autonomous decisions. | Matching service | [SRC: SSOT §4.2]; [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-012 | Internal gigs are time-boxed (≤ 6 months), have an agreed allocation percentage within the cap, need current-manager approval, and carry no time or hour tracking. | Avoids time-tracking/HR scope. | Gig service | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-013 | Mandatory (compliance) assignments cannot be removed by the employee; completion evidence (time, score, content version) is immutable; waivers require an authorized admin, a reason and an expiry. | Audit integrity. | Assignment service | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-014 | Compliance completion records are retained for the org-configured period (default 7 years [PROP], `OD-ENT-09`) even after the employee leaves. | Regulatory evidence. | Retention job | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-015 | Enterprise-issued certificates may be added to a person's personal profile only with the person's consent; once issued and accepted, they remain the person's after leaving. | Portability. | Credential hand-off with `EVD` | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-016 | Learning requests record approval only; the platform does not process payment, reimbursement or budgets. | Scope boundary. | Request service | [PROP] (`OD-ENT-09`) |
| BR-ENT-017 | Talent review and succession inputs are limited to inventory skills, stated interests, tenure band and manager nominations; outcomes are recorded human decisions with rationale; no performance ratings, compensation, protected attributes or automated ranking decisions. | Fairness; stays narrow. | Review service, text scanner | [PROP] (`OD-ENT-02`) |
| BR-ENT-018 | Talent review and succession data is visible only to designated reviewers; employee access to their own record follows the org policy decided under `OD-ENT-03`, never below the legal right of access. | Confidentiality vs rights. | Authz | [PROP]; [DEC-REQ] |
| BR-ENT-019 | Any aggregate grouping smaller than `min_cohort_k` (default 10; org may raise) is suppressed; managers see operational status for individual direct reports but never skills heat maps for teams below the threshold. | Re-identification control. | Report service | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT Amendment G, BR-178] |
| BR-ENT-020 | Individual-level exports are allowed only for compliance and learning completion status, need a stated purpose, and are watermarked and logged; skills, mobility, plans and talent review data export only in aggregate. | Purpose limitation. | Export service | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-021 | SSO is JIT-provisioning capable; SCIM or HRIS deactivation removes enterprise access within 15 minutes and never deletes the person's personal account. | Safe identity lifecycle. | Identity integration | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-022 | After offboarding, skills inventory, plans, mobility preferences and talent review data are deleted or anonymized after 90 days unless a legal hold (reason, expiry) exists; compliance records follow `BR-ENT-014`. | Data minimization. | Retention job | [PROP] (`OD-ENT-09`) |
| BR-ENT-023 | Every enterprise-role read of an individual employee's data is logged with actor, purpose and time; the employee can see the log; log write failure fails the read. | Transparency and accountability. | Access-log service | [DER] |
| BR-ENT-024 | Features that process employee data run per country only after the regional policy allows them; sensitive jurisdictions default to off until an acknowledgement is recorded; missing country defaults to the strictest preset. | Local-law and consultation duties. | Feature flags | [PROP] (`OD-ENT-10`) |
| BR-ENT-025 | Every ENT record and query is scoped by tenant; no cross-tenant read is possible. | Tenant isolation. | Data layer, tests | [SRC: SSOT tenant isolation; METRICS_CATALOG MET-042] |
| BR-ENT-026 | SSO, SCIM, role and policy changes need two admins (requester and approver); at most two break-glass local admins with MFA exist. | Prevents lockout and abuse. | Admin workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-027 | Overdue training follows the configured escalation (employee, manager, L&D); the system sends notices only and takes no punitive or access-removing action. | Non-punitive stance. | Scheduler | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-028 | Enterprise data residency follows the choice made at workspace setup, subject to platform availability. | Customer requirement. | Storage routing | [PROP] (`OD-ENT-08`) |
| BR-ENT-029 | When the HRIS and ENT disagree on an org attribute, the HRIS wins; user-entered skill data is never overwritten by sync. | Clear precedence. | Sync service | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-030 | Linking a personal account to an enterprise record needs the person's consent and a verified email; the person can unlink at any time. | Two-sided consent. | Link service | [DER] |
| BR-ENT-031 | Imported external learning records are labelled as imported and unverified by TalentSphere and satisfy a compliance requirement only if that requirement allows imported evidence. | Evidence honesty. | Import and requirement logic | [PROP] |
| BR-ENT-032 | Mandatory notice classes (`work-required`) cannot be disabled by employees, but channel choice is theirs; chat-tool messages carry minimal content and confidential application updates never go to shared channels. | Reliable compliance with privacy. | Notification routing | [PROP] |

## EVD

Source: [02_MODULES/EVD_Evidence_Work_History_Credentials.md](../02_MODULES/EVD_Evidence_Work_History_Credentials.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-EVD-001 | A claim is not evidence. A verified rung can be set only by the evidence service in response to a qualifying source event; client input and direct database updates cannot set it. | Honest verification (SSOT principle "Verified over claimed"). | Evidence service; database constraint on rung columns | [SRC: SSOT §6.1; V61-17 INV-T04 (Proposed)] |
| BR-EVD-002 | The ladder has four rungs: `claimed`, `artifact_backed`, `peer_attested`, `authority_verified`. `authority_verified` always carries an `issuerClass` (platform, institution, employer_org, instructor) that the UI shows. | One vocabulary everywhere; class matters to matching. | Evidence service; UI chip component | [SRC: SSOT Appendix E V61-17 (Proposed)] |
| BR-EVD-003 | Instructor attestations require instructor ≠ learner plus independence checks (no enrollment conflict, no shared ownership), are revocable, and never count as platform-verified. | An instructor cannot mint the top rung for their own learner. | Review service | [SRC: V61-17 (Proposed)] |
| BR-EVD-004 | Employer-domain email proof reaches only `artifact_backed`, unless the domain is bound to a verified employer organization and an authorized verifier of that organization confirms the facts, which yields `authority_verified` (employer_org). | A domain proves association, not title or dates. | Work history service | [SRC: V61-17 (Proposed)] |
| BR-EVD-005 | Evidence records, status records and events are append-only. Corrections are new records that supersede; nothing is silently rewritten. Artifacts must pass sanity checks (scannable, non-empty, not an unflagged duplicate hash) before counting. | Auditability and tamper evidence. | Database grants; services | [SRC: SSOT BR-149, BR-151, §6.3] |
| BR-EVD-006 | Credentials are append-only; suspension, revocation, renewal and expiry create new status records and keep the original. Evidence links on an issued credential are immutable. | Preserve history. | Database grants; credential service | [SRC: SSOT BR-149, BR-151] |
| BR-EVD-007 | A credential's public verification page exposes no personal data by default. The holder's display name appears only if the holder opted in for that credential. Signed payloads identify the holder by opaque subject reference. | Resolves the SSOT conflict between "no PII" (BR-150) and "first name + last initial" (F-96 step 3) in favor of privacy; see OD-EVD-01. | Verification page; payload builder | [SRC: SSOT BR-150, F-96 step 3 (open)]; resolution [DEC-REQ] OD-EVD-01 |
| BR-EVD-008 | A credential or evidence item is created only from a platform-verified achievement event (course completion meeting criteria, passed assessment with clear integrity, employer or institution issuance by a registered issuer). Issuance is idempotent per (achievement id, template id). | No credentials without real achievement. | Issuance service | [SRC: SSOT BR-156, BR-048] |
| BR-EVD-009 | The public verification endpoint is rate limited (default 60 per minute per IP). A revocation or suspension is visible on the verification page within 5 minutes; caches are purged on status change. | Abuse protection and freshness. | Edge and verification service | [SRC: SSOT F-96 security]; 5 minutes [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-010 | Each credential has a SHA-256 hash of its canonical payload and a signature by the issuer's registered key. Verification recomputes both; a mismatch shows an integrity failure and raises an alert. | Tamper detection. | Credential service | [SRC: SSOT F-96 step 2]; signature [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-011 | A verifier must be authenticated by (a) an account at a verified employer organization with verification authority, or (b) a one-time code to a work email on a domain bound to the employer. The candidate's own addresses can never verify the candidate. | Independence of the authority. | Responder portal | [SRC: SSOT F-94 "company email verification"]; [DER] |
| BR-EVD-012 | Verifiers and referees must be distinct persons from the candidate and use distinct addresses. No more than 2 referees from the same organization per role. | Anti-fraud (SSOT leaves referee rules open). | Reference and verification services | [SRC: SSOT F-94 (open)]; limit [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-013 | An employer verification asks only for employment facts (organization, title, dates, employment type) and optionally candidate-listed achievements. It never asks for salary, performance rating, reason for leaving, medical, or protected-attribute data. | Data minimization; discrimination avoidance. | Request builder | [DER] |
| BR-EVD-014 | A work history request expires after 14 days with reminders on day 3 and day 7; the target verifier response time is under 7 days. | Timely verification. | Scheduler | [SRC: SSOT F-94 "Employment verification < 7d"]; schedule [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-015 | Endorsements, reviews and references are never anonymous. When an author is erased, their contributions are deleted, not anonymized. | Accountability; avoids creating anonymous endorsements. | All attestation services; erasure handler | [SRC: SSOT BR-153] |
| BR-EVD-016 | An endorser must be an authenticated, directly connected user with an account at least 7 days old, cannot endorse themselves, and has one active endorsement per (holder, skill); at most 20 are given per day. Weight = min(endorser reputation, 1.0) + 0.2 direct-connection boost; endorsers without reputation weigh 0.1. | Reproducible weighting, anti-gaming. | Endorsement service | [SRC: SSOT BR-131, BR-152, F-96 step 5]; caps [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-017 | A rung reflects only currently valid sources. Revocation, expiry, suspension, withdrawal or an open dispute removes that source's contribution and the rung is recomputed; the history is kept. | Truth at read time. | Evidence service; impact job | [SRC: SSOT §6.3, §14.3] |
| BR-EVD-018 | Evidence strength is shown as components (provenance, directness, recency, independence, rigor) and a disclosed composite used for sorting only. It is never the sole basis for automated rejection or ranking out of a candidate. | Explainability and fairness. | Quality service; recruiter views | [SRC: SSOT §6.1]; [DER] |
| BR-EVD-019 | Imported credentials are verified by method priority: cryptographic signature, issuer API lookup, fetch from allowlisted issuer domain, manual review. Only the first two (or an approved manual review) reach `authority_verified`; a reachable URL alone is `artifact_backed`. | Do not overclaim verification. | Import service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-020 | Credential expiry is evaluated at the end of the validity date in the holder's time zone. Freshness decay is advisory, never deletes evidence, and does not apply to credentials with explicit validity. | Clear semantics. | Scheduler; quality service | [SRC: SSOT F-123, §14.3] |
| BR-EVD-021 | Revocation, suspension and dispute reasons are visible only to the holder, the issuer and staff; the public sees status only. | Privacy and defamation risk. | Verification page; APIs | [SRC: SSOT F-96 permissions (open)]; resolution [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-022 | Revocation requires a reason code and a note and triggers downstream impact analysis (rungs, share links, matching, search, in-flight applications, notifications). Revoking platform-class credentials older than 365 days needs dual approval. | Controlled, traceable consequences. | Credential service; admin console | [SRC: SSOT §6.3]; dual approval [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-023 | Portable credentials target W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 and Open Badges 3.0. A hash commitment is never labeled zero-knowledge. | Open standards, honest claims. | Export service | [SRC: SSOT F-96 step 8] |
| BR-EVD-024 | Sharing is purpose-bound: each share link has a recipient scope, purpose, item list and expiry (default 14 days, max 90), is recorded as consent, and revocation takes effect at the next read with no consent cache. | Consent revocation must be immediate. | Share service | [SRC: SSOT V61-16 (Proposed)] |
| BR-EVD-025 | Others see only evidence the holder made visible to them or shared with them; private items appear only as a "not shared" count. | Holder control. | Serializer | [DER] |
| BR-EVD-026 | All recruiter and employer access to evidence is logged (viewer, org, items, time). API reads cannot enumerate; unknown and unauthorized ids return the same response. Access-log write failure denies access. | Accountability and enumeration defense. | Share and API services | [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-027 | Selective-disclosure presentations are nonce-bound, short-lived (5 minutes to 24 hours) and check live status at verification. | Replay protection. | Presentation service | [PROP]; [SRC: SSOT BR-155] |
| BR-EVD-028 | A dispute receives a first decision within 7 days of opening; parties respond within 3 days; one appeal is allowed; a user may have at most 5 open disputes. | Timely, fair resolution. | Dispute service | [SRC: SSOT BR-154]; other numbers [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-029 | Append-only history refers to people only by an opaque subject reference. On erasure the identity map is deleted, mutable records are deleted or tombstoned, and credentials remain verifiable as "holder record erased". Legal retention exceptions are listed. | Erasure with auditability. | Erasure handler | [SRC: SSOT V61-07, V61-19 (Proposed)] |
| BR-EVD-030 | Evidence files are malware scanned, limited to 50 MB and allowlisted types, private by default, never publicly addressable, and served only via short-lived signed URLs. | Safe handling. | Upload pipeline | [DER] |
| BR-EVD-031 | External contribution connections use read-only minimal OAuth scopes; tokens are encrypted and deleted on disconnect; only metadata and counts are stored; forks without upstream merges, bots and trivial changes are excluded. | Minimal data, fair metrics. | Integration service | [SRC: SSOT F-89]; [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-032 | Reference forms exclude questions about protected attributes, health, family or age; submissions are immutable except one correction within 7 days. | Fair, clean references. | Form templates | [DER] |
| BR-EVD-033 | Only registered, verified issuers (domain control and identity proven) may issue; every signing key is held in a managed key store, rotation preserves old public keys for verification, and a compromised key triggers re-verification of credentials signed after the compromise date. | Trust anchor. | Issuer registry; KMS | [PROP] |
| BR-EVD-034 | Evidence quality never uses protected attributes, photo, name, nationality or institution prestige as inputs. | Fairness. | Quality service; audits | [DER] |
| BR-EVD-035 | Narratives are labeled self-authored, never raise a rung, and AI drafts never auto-commit. | Claims are not evidence. | Narrative service | [SRC: SSOT BR-33]; [DER] |
| BR-EVD-036 | Skill claims reference canonical skills only; skills inferred from artifacts or contributions are suggestions the holder must accept. | Taxonomy integrity. | Claim service | [SRC: SSOT BR-141, BR-144] |
| BR-EVD-037 | Manual grants of `authority_verified` for high-impact items (degrees, professional licenses, employer records without an issuer) require two different staff approvals; staff cannot review their own or related accounts. | Prevent insider fraud. | Review queue | [PROP] |

## EVT

Source: [02_MODULES/EVT_Events_Hackathons_Community_Programmes.md](../02_MODULES/EVT_Events_Hackathons_Community_Programmes.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-EVT-001 | Only these roles may host: `INS` (own events), approved `MNT`, `REC`/`EAD` for their organization, `IAD`/`PLO` for their institution, `PAD`. A `CAN`/`STD` may not host public events (`OD-EVT-02`). Hosting rights can be suspended by `MOD`/`PAD`. | Limits spam and scam events; keeps the module inside the career domain. | Create and publish services; role check | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-002 | To publish, an event needs title, summary, description ≥ 50 chars, start and end with IANA timezone, mode, venue or join method, capacity or unlimited, host identity, code-of-conduct acknowledgement; paid events also need a refund policy. | Prevents incomplete public pages. | Publish validation | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-003 | Times are stored in UTC with the event's IANA timezone; shown in the viewer timezone with the event timezone in parentheses; ICS uses UTC and stable `UID`. | Avoids DST and cross-region errors. | Domain layer, ICS generator | [DER] |
| BR-EVT-004 | Confirmed registrations never exceed capacity (overall and per ticket type). Waitlist is FIFO by `joinedAt`; a freed seat is offered to the next entry for `waitlist_offer_hours` (default 24, `[PROP]`, shrinks near start). | Fairness and no oversell. | Registration transaction | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-005 | One active registration per (event, user, ticket type); repeated requests are idempotent and return the existing record. A user cannot hold two overlapping career-fair slots. | Prevents duplicates and double-booking. | Unique constraint plus service | [DER] |
| BR-EVT-006 | The refund policy is snapshotted at purchase. After the first sale a host may only change it to a more favorable policy for attendees. | Consumer protection. | Ticket service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-007 | A change is material if it alters start/end by more than 15 minutes, venue, mode, join provider, or price. Material changes notify registrants, increment the ICS sequence, and let registrants cancel free of charge regardless of policy. Cancellation is always material. | Registrants are not bound to terms they did not accept. | Event update service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-008 | Attendee personal data is shared with sponsors or employers only after the attendee's explicit, per-organization, revocable opt-in. Defaults are off. Hosts receive only what the service needs (name, email, answers). | Privacy by default. | Consent ledger and read APIs | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT privacy principles]; [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-009 | Events open to minors require a minimum age and guardian-consent flow set by the host; default minimum age is 18 for employer-hosted events and hackathons (`OD-EVT-07`). | Child safety and law. | Registration eligibility | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-010 | Check-in tokens are signed, bound to one registration and event, and single-use for the same check-in type; rescanning returns "already checked in" and records nothing. QR codes rotate at least once per 24 hours before the event. | Prevents sharing and duplicate counting. | Check-in service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-011 | Recording requires a consent notice shown at registration and at join; recordings expire per host setting (default 12 months) and attendees may request removal of their appearance. | Consent and data rights. | Recording service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-012 | In a hackathon a participant belongs to at most one team; team size stays within the published min and max; teams lock at the submission deadline; a submission belongs to exactly one team. | Fairness and clear ownership. | Team and submission services | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-013 | Every submission is scored by at least `judges_min` judges (default 3, `[PROP]`); judges declare conflicts; a judge cannot score a submission from their own team or organization; final score is the weighted sum of criteria; tie-break rule is fixed before the build phase. | Defensible judging. | Judging service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-014 | Rules, criteria, team size and prizes are frozen when the build phase starts. Only `PAD` may change them, with notice to all participants and a 48-hour penalty-free withdrawal window. | Participants rely on published terms. | Hackathon service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-015 | Participants keep ownership of their work unless the published rules state a license; rules must contain an IP clause. Sponsors and hosts cannot influence scores; sponsor prize tracks are judged under the same criteria process. | Avoids IP disputes and pay-to-win. | Publish validation, judging | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-016 | A certificate is issued only to an attendee with checked-in attendance of at least the configured threshold (default 80%) or, for hackathons, a submitted project; revoked on disqualification. | Credential integrity. | Certificate service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-017 | Career-fair employer booths require a verified employer organization. Booth staff see a candidate's profile data only through a candidate's explicit "share", scoped to chosen fields; anonymous aggregate visit counts are allowed. | Candidate control. | Booth and share services | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-018 | Events must follow the content policy; banned users and hosts under suspension cannot register or publish; the host may remove an attendee with a reason; reports go to `MOD`. | Safety. | Moderation hooks | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-019 | When an event is cancelled or taken down, every paid registration is refunded in full automatically and unpaid pending payments are voided. | Consumer protection. | Cancel flow with `BIL` | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-020 | Default reminders are 24 hours, 1 hour and 10 minutes before start; reminders are opt-out per event; cancellation and material-change notices cannot be opted out. | Reliability vs consent. | Reminder scheduler | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-021 | Organizer analytics show attendee-level data only for the host's own events; any cross-event or platform benchmark uses at least `min_cohort_k` (default 10) events or attendees; survey breakdowns appear only with at least 5 responses. | Re-identification control. | Analytics read layer | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT Amendment G, BR-178] |
| BR-EVT-022 | Sponsorship, fees or tier never influence event discovery ranking, judging, or access to candidate data; sponsor recognition is labelled "Sponsor". Paid placement is not offered. | Non-goal compliance (no ad network, no pay-to-rank). | Ranking service, UI | [SRC: SSOT §4.2] |
| BR-EVT-023 | Hackathon eligibility (age, country restrictions required by law, sponsor-employee exclusion) is evaluated at registration; only pass/fail is stored visible to hosts. | Legal eligibility without exposing data. | Registration service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-024 | Attendee personal data for an event is retained 24 months after the event end and then anonymized; registration answers are erased with account deletion; consent ledger rows are anonymized not deleted. | Data minimization. | Retention job | [PROP] (`OD-EVT-06`) |
| BR-EVT-025 | Anonymous Q&A hides the author from other attendees only; moderators and hosts can see the author. Blocked users' posts are hidden from everyone but the author. | Safe participation with accountability. | Q&A service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-026 | A programme is complete when the attendee attended at least the required number of sessions; completion triggers a programme certificate. | Clear completion rule. | Series service | [PROP] |
| BR-EVT-027 | Editing a recurring series with "this and following" changes future instances only; past instances and their registrations are immutable. | Preserves history. | Series service | [PROP] |

## GIG

Source: [02_MODULES/GIG_Freelance_Contract_Project_Work.md](../02_MODULES/GIG_Freelance_Contract_Project_Work.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-GIG-001 | Freelancer mode is opt-in, off by default, and does not change job-seeker visibility or ranking. | Candidate control. | Mode service | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-002 | Listings are limited to skill-based professional project categories on an allowlist; prohibited: illegal work, adult content, regulated professions without licence, weapons, gambling, multi-level schemes, discriminatory requirements, misleading identity use. | Stay inside SSOT §4.2 (no general marketplace). | Scope guard | [PROP] [SRC: §4.2] [DEC-REQ] OD-GIG-09 |
| BR-GIG-003 | Listings that ask someone to complete another person's graded work, exams or assessments, or to fake credentials, are prohibited. | Academic and credential integrity. | Scope guard | [SRC: ASM integrity principles] [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-004 | The contract is between client and freelancer; the platform is not the employer, agent or a party to the work and offers no payroll, benefits or employer-of-record. | Non-goal and liability. | Terms template, product scope | [SRC: §4.2] |
| BR-GIG-005 | Every contract is fixed-price with at least one milestone, each with written acceptance criteria. | Clarity and dispute basis. | Contract builder | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-006 | The platform does not hold third-party funds except in a mode approved by the escrow decision gate through a licensed structure; the default mode is pay on acceptance. | Regulatory and non-goal risk. | Mode flag | [DEC-REQ] OD-GIG-02 |
| BR-GIG-007 | Time tracking exists only if approved; it is consent-based, with no covert monitoring (no keystroke, mouse, webcam capture). | Privacy and classification risk. | Feature flag, time service | [DEC-REQ] OD-GIG-03 |
| BR-GIG-008 | Review windows are fixed (default 7 days); after the window plus a 3-day reminder period an unanswered submission auto-accepts, with a 7-day dispute right. | Prevents holding freelancers hostage. | Scheduler | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-009 | Revisions per milestone are limited (default 2) and must cite unmet criteria; more need a change request. | Scope control. | Review service | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-010 | Fees are disclosed before award, identical per fee table for everyone, and fixed in the terms snapshot. | Transparency. | Fee preview, BIL | [SRC: BR-101 pattern] [DEC-REQ] OD-GIG-08 |
| BR-GIG-011 | No payment, plan or promotion influences listing order, proposal order, freelancer ranking, badges or reputation; plans change capacity only. | No pay-to-rank. | Ranking services | [SRC: §4.2; BR-BIL-004] |
| BR-GIG-012 | Contact details and off-platform payment solicitation are masked before contract acceptance; off-platform payment during a contract is prohibited. | Marketplace integrity. | Message filter | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-013 | Payouts require valid identity, payout account and tax information; the platform reports where legally required and gives no tax advice. | Compliance. | Eligibility and payout guards | [PROP] [DEC-REQ] OD-GIG-05 |
| BR-GIG-014 | The platform blocks terms that require exclusivity and warns on employment-like control (fixed hours, supervision, equipment); it never decides legal classification. | Misclassification risk. | Classification guard | [PROP] [DEC-REQ] OD-GIG-04 |
| BR-GIG-015 | Parties and payouts must be in supported countries and clear sanctions screening; one currency per contract. | Legal compliance. | Award and payout checks | [PROP] [DEC-REQ] OD-GIG-06 |
| BR-GIG-016 | IP is assigned to the client on payment in full for the relevant milestone unless the contract says otherwise; the freelancer keeps pre-existing materials. | Clear ownership. | Terms template | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-017 | NDA work shows only category, skills and dates publicly unless the client permits more; portfolio use needs client permission under NDA. | Confidentiality. | Evidence and portfolio visibility | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-018 | Reviews need a contract with a paid milestone, are mutual, hidden until both submit or 14 days pass, and cannot be a condition of payment. | Honest reviews. | Review service | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-019 | Work evidence from a contract reaches "client confirmed" only by the client's confirmation; freelancers cannot self-verify. | Verification ladder integrity. | Evidence service | [SRC: verification ladder; subject cannot verify own evidence] |
| BR-GIG-020 | Disputes follow a ladder (respond, negotiate, mediate, appeal once); decisions are reasoned, based on terms and criteria, and reviewers must be independent. | Fair resolution. | Dispute service | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-021 | Freelancers and clients acting for themselves must be adults under local law (minimum 18); learning projects for minors are only through institution programs. | Legal capacity. | Eligibility | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-022 | When a party is suspended, running contracts follow a defined path: the other party may continue or cancel, unreleased funds are returned or held per mode, accepted work stays payable. | Fairness. | Contract and enforcement services | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-023 | Clients need a verified payment method and organization verification; new clients have a spend limit that rises with clean history. | Payment risk. | Posting and award guards | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-024 | Unpaid spec work is prohibited; any trial task must be paid or be a time-boxed (maximum 1 hour) assessment with no reuse rights. | Fair labor. | Scope guard | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-025 | Proposals are limited by a plan quota, duplicates are blocked, edits after viewing are marked and notified, quota is refunded when a listing is cancelled or removed. | Fair access and anti-spam. | Proposal service, BIL | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-026 | Hiring a freelancer through JOB is always allowed; any conversion fee is a decision parameter (default none); non-solicitation is not enforced. | Candidate freedom. | Conversion service | [DEC-REQ] OD-GIG-08 |
| BR-GIG-027 | Freelancer contract data, rates and earnings are invisible to employers evaluating the person as a job candidate unless shared; clients cannot request private evidence beyond the contract's needs. | Separation of roles. | Visibility rules | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-028 | Learning projects are labeled, optional and educational; partners attest that they do not substitute for paid roles; patterns of free-labor use are reviewed. | Prevents exploitation. | Learning project guard | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-029 | Contract workroom records, terms and deliverable metadata are retained for the statutory period (default 7 years for money-related records) and are the evidence base for disputes. | Legal and dispute support. | Retention job | [PROP] |
| BR-GIG-030 | Payments are idempotent per milestone acceptance; refunds and clawbacks follow BIL rules; accepted work stays payable after termination. | No double payment. | Payment service | [SRC: BR-BIL-003, BR-BIL-024] |

## IDN

Source: [02_MODULES/IDN_Identity_Authentication_Account.md](../02_MODULES/IDN_Identity_Authentication_Account.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-IDN-001 | Email is normalized (trim, NFKC, lower-cased domain; local part compared case-insensitively) and unique among non-erased accounts; concurrent registrations differing by case yield one account. | Prevents duplicate identities and enumeration by case. | Domain layer + unique index on normalized email | [SRC: Yash SPEC-01 §3.1] |
| BR-IDN-002 | A password is 12–128 characters, any Unicode, not on a breached list, not equal to the email local part; no composition rules; hashed with a memory-hard function. If the breach service is unavailable, accept only ≥ 14 characters and schedule a re-check. | Length beats composition; fail safe. | Domain layer + breach port | [SRC: Yash BR-T051] |
| BR-IDN-003 | Registration, sign-in, reset, magic-link and recovery responses (status, body, and latency within tolerance) never depend on whether an email has an account. | Blocks account enumeration. | API layer + dummy hash path | [SRC: Yash SPEC-01 §3.2] |
| BR-IDN-004 | Verification and sign-in codes are 6 digits, TTL {15 min}, ≤ 5 attempts, single use, hashed at rest; a new code invalidates earlier ones. | Bounded guessing. | Domain layer | [SRC: Yash BR-T053, CONST-S08] |
| BR-IDN-005 | A `pending_verification` account has no profile visibility, cannot apply, message, or hold roles beyond onboarding progress, and is purged after {7 days}. | Limits abuse by unverified accounts. | Account state guard + worker | [SRC: Yash SM-ACCOUNT t2] |
| BR-IDN-006 | After {5} consecutive failures per (normalized email, IP bucket) a progressive delay applies, doubling from {15 s} up to {15 min}; during a delay even correct credentials return `429`; per-IP limits apply across accounts; the same curve covers MFA, step-up and magic-link code failures. | Stops stuffing without an oracle. | Rate-limit layer | [SRC: Yash BR-T052; SSOT HDN-008] |
| BR-IDN-007 | Session lifetimes: access {15 min}; idle {14 d}; absolute {30 d}; remember-me absolute {90 d}; privileged roles idle 30 min and absolute 8 h; org policy may shorten but never lengthen. | Bounded exposure. | Session service | [SRC: Yash CONST-S01..S05] |
| BR-IDN-008 | Access and refresh credentials live only in `Secure; HttpOnly` cookies; never in script-readable storage, URLs, bodies or logs; unsafe requests need a per-session CSRF header and an allowed `Origin`. | Removes script-theft and CSRF. | Edge + API | [SRC: SSOT §12.8 V61-13] |
| BR-IDN-009 | Refresh credentials rotate each use; reuse of a superseded generation beyond a {5 s} leeway revokes the whole session family and notifies the holder; refresh for a non-`active` account is refused. | Detects theft. | Session service | [SRC: Yash BR-T050, CONST-S07] |
| BR-IDN-010 | Sensitive actions require re-authentication no older than {300 s}: change email, phone, password, passkey, MFA; deactivate; delete; download export; create API token; billing change; SSO config; privileged role grant; revoke-all-others when MFA is on. | Contains session hijack. | Policy layer | [SRC: Yash BR-T057, CONST-S06] |
| BR-IDN-011 | Privileged roles (MOD, SUP, FIN, PAD, SAD) require MFA or passkey with user verification; no remember-me, no trusted-device bypass, no magic-link sign-in; org admins may require MFA for members with a grace period. | Staff accounts are the highest-value target. | Role-context resolver | [SRC: Yash BR-T044] |
| BR-IDN-012 | An account has ≤ {10} passkeys; the last remaining sign-in method cannot be removed; a counter regression marks the credential `suspect` and notifies the holder. | Prevent lockout and cloning. | Domain layer | [SRC: Yash BR-T055] |
| BR-IDN-013 | TOTP uses a 30 s step with ±1 window, and a used step cannot repeat; 10 single-use recovery codes are hashed, shown once, and regeneration invalidates the old set. | Standard TOTP safety. | Domain layer | [PROP] |
| BR-IDN-014 | MFA cannot be turned off while a platform or org policy requires it for any of the account's roles. | Policy cannot be undone by the user. | Domain layer | [DER] |
| BR-IDN-015 | A password change revokes all other session families and trusted-device cookies; a password reset revokes all sessions including the current one. | Eliminates attacker persistence. | Session service | [SRC: Yash BR-T054] |
| BR-IDN-016 | Reset tokens are ≥ 128-bit random, hashed, TTL {30 min}, single use; at most {3} per recipient per hour and {5} per minute per IP; expired, used and unknown share one error. | Bounded abuse of email as a channel. | Domain + rate limit | [SRC: SSOT §9.1 step 7; Yash BR-T054] |
| BR-IDN-017 | An email change needs step-up, confirmation at the new address, a notice to the old address, and an undo window of {7 days}. | Recoverability from takeover. | Domain layer | [SRC: Yash BR-T058] |
| BR-IDN-018 | Sign-in from an unrecognized device emails the holder with a revoke link, at most once per device per 24 h; suppressed for the first sign-in after registration. | Early warning. | Worker | [SRC: Yash BR-T059] |
| BR-IDN-019 | Self-service recovery (all factors lost) requires proof of control of every verified contact channel, a {24 h} hold, notices on all channels with cancel links, removal of all factors on completion, and a {72 h} elevated watch; support cannot shorten the hold; privileged accounts need second approval by SAD. | Recovery must not be the weakest link. | Recovery service | [DER from Yash FEAT-01-06.3] |
| BR-IDN-020 | Roles are resolved on the server from active grants; the client never supplies a role; authorization is deny by default; privileged platform grants need dual control, a reason and review monthly, and expire after {60 days} unused. | No role forgery. | Role-context resolver | [SRC: SSOT §5.4; Yash BR-T049] |
| BR-IDN-021 | Self-service grants are limited to `CAN`, `FRL` (toggle) and `STD` (with institution code or invitation); `INS`, `MNT`, `REC`, `HMG`, `EAD`, `IAD`, `PLO`, `EXA` come from review, organization creation or membership grants; staff roles come only from BR-IDN-020. | Limits privilege creep. | Onboarding service | [DER] |
| BR-IDN-022 | A session has exactly one active role context `(role, scopeType, scopeId)`; permissions are those of that context only; there is no union of roles; a person cannot review their own application in any context. | Prevents conflict of interest and confused-deputy. | Role-context resolver + policy | [DER] (conflicts with SSOT "highest wins", OD-IDN-02) |
| BR-IDN-023 | Invitation tokens are ≥ 128-bit, hashed, bound to the invited email, TTL {7 d}, single use; acceptance needs a verified email equal to the invited one; the last `EAD` cannot be removed or leave; invitations never grant platform staff roles. | Prevents hijacking invitations and orphaned orgs. | Domain layer | [DER] |
| BR-IDN-024 | An external identity is linked only after proof of control of the target account (existing session with step-up or fresh sign-in); a provider email is trusted only if the provider asserts it verified; a provider subject links to one account; matching emails never merge silently; a verified provider identity overrides an unverified local registration of the same email. | Prevents takeover and pre-registration hijack. | Linking service | [SRC: SSOT §9.1 step 8] + [DER] |
| BR-IDN-025 | A sign-in method cannot be removed if it is the last one; a user must add another first. | Prevents lockout. | Domain layer | [SRC: Yash BR-T055] |
| BR-IDN-026 | Deactivation is reversible, requires step-up, ends all sessions, hides the profile, keeps data for {12 months} (open), and notifies 30 and 7 days before the retention end; a sole org owner must transfer first. | Honest pause. | Account service | [SRC: Yash FEAT-01-10]; value [DEC-REQ] OD-IDN-04 |
| BR-IDN-027 | An erasure request needs step-up and typed email, moves the account to `pending_erasure` (sessions ended), allows cancel in cooling-off ({7 d}), and is parked `on_hold` if the account is suspended, under a moderation case, or under legal hold. | Reversibility and evidence preservation. | Account service + SET | [SRC: Yash BR-T066, BR-T124] |
| BR-IDN-028 | Impersonation requires a ticket, a reason code, a scoped time-boxed grant (≤ {4 h}), is read-only, never exposes credentials or secrets, is fully audited, and the subject is notified unless notice is prohibited; targets cannot be PAD or SAD. | Support access without risk. | Support-access service + policy | [SRC: Yash BR-T041..T043] |
| BR-IDN-029 | Registration requires an age attestation at or above the regional minimum age ({16} default); the date of birth is not stored, only an `isOfAge` result; a failed attempt blocks retry on that device for {24 h}. | Compliance with data minimization. | Registration service | [SRC: SSOT AUTH-017, V61-24]; value [DEC-REQ] OD-IDN-11 |
| BR-IDN-030 | Bot defenses are risk-based and layered; authentication never requires a cognitive test; passkey sign-in is never challenged; the risk provider failing means stricter static limits, not open access. | Security with accessibility. | Edge + API | [PROP] |
| BR-IDN-031 | A `suspended` account may sign in only to a restricted appeal session (notice, appeal, data rights). | Due process. | Session service | [SRC: Yash AC-01-02-05] |
| BR-IDN-032 | Authentication failures use generic wording; secrets, tokens, codes and credentials never appear in logs, analytics or error messages. | No leakage. | All layers | [SRC: SSOT HDN-010] |
| BR-IDN-033 | Registration and sign-in after a material policy change require acceptance of the current policy versions, recorded in an append-only ledger; acceptance is separate from other consents and never pre-ticked. | Auditable lawful basis. | Registration + gate | [SRC: Yash FEAT-01-13] |
| BR-IDN-034 | SSO domains need DNS proof; JIT provisioning only for verified domains; SSO mappings can never grant `EAD` or platform roles; enforced SSO blocks password and social sign-in for that domain except two break-glass admins. | Safe federation. | SSO service | [PROP] |
| BR-IDN-035 | Session revocation, role revocation and account-state changes take effect on every request within {60 s} p95; if the revocation store is unavailable, requests are denied (fail closed). | Timely containment. | Session service | [SRC: Yash SPEC-01 §3.4] |
| BR-IDN-036 | A verified phone number belongs to one account at a time, is encrypted at rest, masked in UI, and is never the sole recovery factor; SMS sends are capped per account, IP and prefix. | SIM-swap and pumping defense. | Domain + rate limit | [PROP] |
| BR-IDN-037 | An org may send ≤ {50} invitations per request and ≤ {200} per day; complaints suspend sending for that org. | Prevents spam via invitations. | Invitation service | [PROP] |
| BR-IDN-038 | Credential, session, role, MFA, recovery, support-access and state-change events are written to the tamper-evident audit log with actor, subject, time and outcome, and subjects can read their own. | Accountability and subject transparency. | Audit service | [SRC: SSOT HDN-009; Yash INV-T18] |
| BR-IDN-039 | Magic-link and email-code sign-in bind the request to the requesting browser, require a confirm step on the landing page (GET consumes nothing), are single use, TTL {15 min}, and are unavailable for privileged roles and SSO-enforced domains. | Defeats link scanners and phishing relays. | Sign-in service | [PROP] |
| BR-IDN-040 | A machine principal authenticates only with a scoped, revocable credential issued by `PLT`; it has no cookie session, no refresh, no role switching, and is rate limited per credential. | Least privilege automation. | API gateway | [SRC: SSOT HDN-015] + [DER] |

## INS

Source: [02_MODULES/INS_Institutions_Managed_Learning.md](../02_MODULES/INS_Institutions_Managed_Learning.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-INS-001 | Every institution-owned record carries `institution_id`; cross-tenant reads and writes are denied server-side and by row-level security. | Tenant isolation is the core safety property of B2B2C. | Data layer policies, API middleware, tests for every table | [SRC: BR-080; HDN-018; §23.4 exit 5] |
| BR-INS-002 | A tenant not yet `verified` runs in sandbox: at most 25 students, no certificates, no public page, no drives, no employer sharing. | Prevents abuse by fake institutions. | Tenant guard on create/issue actions | [DER] |
| BR-INS-003 | Verification needs proof of domain control and one proof of legal existence; the reviewer must be independent of the applicant and decisions are immutable. | Trust in institution-issued credentials. | Verification workflow, ADM queue | [DER] |
| BR-INS-004 | Staff roles are scoped grants; faculty and placement officers have no billing, seat purchase or user-management rights; the last active `IAD` cannot be removed or downgraded. | Least privilege, no orphan tenant. | Authorization layer | [SRC: BR-078] [DER] |
| BR-INS-005 | A user has at most one active membership per institution; a user may hold memberships at several institutions; one primary program per membership. | Avoids duplicate seats and records. | Unique constraint | [DER] |
| BR-INS-006 | Bulk imports and sync runs require a dry-run preview and explicit confirmation; no silent partial import; excluded rows are listed. | Data integrity. | Import service state machine | [SRC: BR-077] |
| BR-INS-007 | Imports are idempotent on (import batch id, row hash) and sync on (source id, external id). | Retries never duplicate. | Unique keys | [SRC: SCI-10] |
| BR-INS-008 | The institution sees only institution-scope data and data the student shared by consent; it cannot read applications, messages, private evidence or personal profile fields. | Student sovereignty. | Query layer field allowlists | [DER] |
| BR-INS-009 | Seat consumption is atomic; assigned seats never exceed total; no overselling under concurrency. | Revenue and fairness. | Row lock plus check constraint | [SRC: BR-074] |
| BR-INS-010 | Course access is decided server-side from institution status, membership, seat validity, enrollment and validity window on every request. | Prevents UI-only gating. | Course access service | [SRC: BR-072, BR-082] |
| BR-INS-011 | Seat revocation gives a 7-day grace (configurable 0-30); in-progress assessments are never interrupted; progress and certificates are retained; seats return to the pool. | Student fairness. | Seat service, ASM hook | [SRC: BR-073, BR-075] |
| BR-INS-012 | Institutional pricing is configured per course or package in BIL, never hard-coded in INS. | Pricing is OD-gated. | Reads from BIL price book | [SRC: BR-081] |
| BR-INS-013 | Employer-facing student showcases need recorded, revocable, purpose-bound consent; default is no sharing. | Privacy and trust. | Showcase service | [SRC: BR-079] |
| BR-INS-014 | Students below the age of majority need guardian consent before profile creation; minors have private-by-default profiles, restricted outreach, no employer showcase or drives without a guardian-granted purpose; the age floor is a platform parameter. | Child safety and legal compliance. | Membership activation guard, discovery filters | [SRC: BR-128] [DEC-REQ] OD-INS-05 |
| BR-INS-015 | Education records are classed Restricted; every identity-bearing disclosure creates a log entry; students can request access and correction. | FERPA-style accountability. | Disclosure service, export layer | [DER] OD-INS-05 |
| BR-INS-016 | Graduation or leaving retains all verified signals on the student's account, severs institution-restricted records from the student's profile and ends tenant access to non-institution data; alumni network joining is opt-in. | Flywheel without capturing the student. | Transition service | [SRC: BR-076, BR-247] |
| BR-INS-017 | Institutional student records are retained 7 years after last activity by default, configurable within platform bounds, and purged afterwards unless on legal hold. | Compliance and storage limitation. | Retention job | [SRC: OD-19] |
| BR-INS-018 | Intervention notes and at-risk flags are internal; the student sees only items marked shared; employers and external parties never see them. | Student dignity and legal exposure. | Case visibility field and query filters | [DER] |
| BR-INS-019 | At-risk flags are produced by declared rules with listed signals; no unexplained score may raise a flag; flags never trigger automatic adverse action. | Explainability and fairness. | Flag generator schema | [DER] |
| BR-INS-020 | Drive eligibility uses an allowlist of job-relevant criteria; protected attributes are refused. | Non-discrimination. | Drive validation | [DER] |
| BR-INS-021 | Drive participation is voluntary; the institution's one-offer policy (if on) blocks further registration after acceptance; dream-offer exception is configurable. | Fairness and student autonomy. | Registration guard | [PROP] |
| BR-INS-022 | Placement outcomes are student-confirmed or verified before they enter public or accreditation outputs; unconfirmed are labeled institution-reported. | Honest statistics. | Reporting filters | [DER] |
| BR-INS-023 | Any aggregate shown outside direct in-tenant per-student views suppresses cells with fewer than `min_cohort_k` students (default 10). | Re-identification risk. | Report engine | [SRC: V61-04, OD-38] |
| BR-INS-024 | Every report run stores its parameters, query version and as-of time and can be reproduced. | Auditability. | Report run record | [DER] |
| BR-INS-025 | Certificate branding is snapshotted at issuance; certificates are verifiable by a public unguessable code; revocation propagates to linked evidence. | Credential trust. | Certificate service | [SRC: SCI-17; CF-41] |
| BR-INS-026 | SSO may only provision or sign in users whose asserted email domain is verified for the tenant and who match a roster entry (or domain claim is enabled). | Prevents takeover of tenant membership. | SSO callback | [DER] |
| BR-INS-027 | LTI launches validate signature, nonce, state, issuer, audience, deployment id and expiry; each registration belongs to one tenant. | Standard LTI 1.3 security. | LTI endpoint | [PROP] |
| BR-INS-028 | A user may hold one open institution application; a verified domain belongs to exactly one tenant. | Impersonation protection. | Unique constraints | [DER] |
| BR-INS-029 | Invitations and guardian links are single-use bearer tokens, stored hashed, expiring (default 14 days); claiming requires control of the invited email. | Account takeover prevention. | Token service | [DER] |
| BR-INS-030 | Structure nodes (departments, programs, batches) cannot be archived while active children exist; history is retained; institution-private courses never appear in public search without STU review. | Referential integrity and privacy. | Service guards | [DER] |
| BR-INS-031 | Faculty read and grade only batches and courses they are assigned to. | Least privilege. | Scope filter | [SRC: BR-078] |
| BR-INS-032 | Offboarding gives a 30-day export window, transitions students as independents, purges institution-scoped data after the window unless on hold or unpaid items block it. | Fair exit. | Offboarding workflow | [DER] |
| BR-INS-033 | Employer relations is a partnership list with consented sharing only: no scraping, sequences, lead scoring or bulk cold outreach; invite volume is capped. | Stays inside SSOT non-goal. | Invite service | [SRC: §4.2] [DEC-REQ] OD-INS-03 |
| BR-INS-034 | Employers see only students who registered for that drive and consented; access ends when the drive closes plus 30 days. | Purpose limitation. | Drive view builder | [SRC: BR-079] |
| BR-INS-035 | Mandatory academic notices cannot be opted out; opportunity and coaching messages follow opt-out classes. | Clarity of obligations. | NTF template classes | [DER] |
| BR-INS-036 | A student may leave an institution at any time; their independent account continues and institution access ends per FR-INS-025 rules. | Student ownership. | Membership service | [DER] |
| BR-INS-037 | Roster sources are authoritative only for institution-scope fields and never overwrite student-owned profile fields. | Data ownership. | Sync mapper | [DER] |
| BR-INS-038 | Destructive bulk actions on more than 50 students need typed confirmation and are undoable for 24 hours; sync guard stops withdrawals above 10 percent of the roster per run. | Prevent mass accidents. | Bulk action service | [PROP] |

## INT

Source: [02_MODULES/INT_Interviews_Scheduling.md](../02_MODULES/INT_Interviews_Scheduling.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-INT-001 | An interview may be created only for an active, non-terminal application in a stage that has a plan round. | No orphan interviews. | Scheduling command | [DER] |
| BR-INT-002 | Interviewers must be active employer members on the job's hiring team, hold required qualifications, and have no declared conflict with the candidate. | Quality and fairness. | Matching, scheduling | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-003 | Offered slots must be free for all required interviewers considering buffers, notice, caps and holidays; soft holds last 24 hours. | No impossible offers. | Availability engine | [DER] |
| BR-INT-004 | Booking is atomic and rechecks live availability; double booking of a person is impossible; the loser of a race gets fresh slots. | Reliability. | Booking transaction | [DER] |
| BR-INT-005 | Times are stored as UTC with IANA zone and always displayed with zone label in the viewer's zone. | Avoid wrong-hour no-shows. | UI, notifications | [DER] |
