| BR-INT-006 | Candidates may self-reschedule up to 2 times with at least 24 hours notice; otherwise recruiter approval is needed. | Balance flexibility and cost. | Reschedule command | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-007 | Late cancellations are recorded but never penalize the candidate automatically. | Fairness. | Cancel command | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-008 | Reminders default to 24 h and 1 h for candidates and 24 h and 15 min for interviewers; email may be muted, the in-app reminder cannot. | Reduce no-shows. | Reminder service | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-009 | Calendar access uses minimal scopes, reads busy blocks only, stores tokens encrypted and revokes on disconnect. | Privacy. | Calendar service | [DER] |
| BR-INT-010 | Candidate calendars are never accessed; candidates receive ICS only. | Privacy. | Calendar service | [DER] |
| BR-INT-011 | Room join tokens are one-time, bound to interview and participant; candidates wait in a lobby; the room opens 15 minutes before start. | Security. | Room service | [DER] |
| BR-INT-012 | Recording needs dual consent (candidate consent and employer policy, with interviewer notice); all-party consent rules are honored; a visible indicator is shown; declining has no effect on evaluation. | Consent and law. | Room, recording service | [SRC: BR-169] |
| BR-INT-013 | Recordings and derived data are encrypted at rest and retained 30 days by default, at most 90 days unless legal hold. | Data minimization. | Retention job | [SRC: BR-170] |
| BR-INT-014 | Transcription and AI notes require a separate explicit candidate consent recorded before processing. | Consent. | AI gateway | [PROP] [SRC: BR-169] |
| BR-INT-015 | Interview questions are org-scoped and never visible to candidates before or after the interview through the platform. | Question integrity. | API authorization | [SRC: BR-173] |
| BR-INT-016 | Interviews follow structured plans: kit questions are linked to competencies; ad hoc questions are allowed but flagged. | Comparability. | Live notes, scorecard | [SRC: BR-176] |
| BR-INT-017 | Kit questions and live notes are linted for unlawful topics; blocked topics cannot be saved in kits. | Non-discrimination. | Kit editor | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-018 | Interviewer notes are private until their scorecard is submitted; feedback is due 24 hours after the interview. | Independent judgment. | Feedback service | [PROP] aligns BR-ATS-017 |
| BR-INT-019 | A candidate no-show never rejects automatically; the recruiter decides; a first excused no-show gets a free reschedule. | Fairness. | No-show workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-020 | Transcripts are labelled machine-generated with confidence; candidates may request correction or deletion. | Honesty. | Transcript UI | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-021 | AI summaries are advisory, cite evidence, exclude protected attributes and affect nothing automatically; no voice, face or emotion analysis; confidence below 0.5 suppressed. | Safe AI. | AI gateway | [SRC: BR-171, BR-172, BR-065, BR-066] |
| BR-INT-022 | Async interview limits (questions, time, retakes, deadline) are disclosed before the candidate starts, and text and audio alternatives are available. | Fairness and accessibility. | Async service | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-023 | Async timers start only on recording start; interrupted sessions resume; submission is final. | Fairness. | Async service | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-024 | Self-scheduling links are signed, single-use per request and expire with the invitation. | Security. | Scheduling API | [DER] |
| BR-INT-025 | Panel interviewers are selected by round-robin or least load among qualified people; matching never uses protected attributes. | Fairness. | Matching | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-026 | Interviewer load caps apply (default 5 per week, 3 per day); exceeding requires an audited override. | Burnout and quality. | Availability engine | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-027 | Code execution uses the assessment sandbox limits; artifacts are stored only with candidate consent. | Security and consent. | Editor service | [SRC: BR-175, BR-049, BR-050] |
| BR-INT-028 | Interviewers who declare a relationship or conflict with a candidate are excluded from that candidate's interviews. | Integrity. | Matching | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-029 | Scheduling automation fires only after a human stage move and is idempotent per stage entry. | Human oversight. | Automation service | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-030 | A debrief shows others' feedback only to people who submitted their own, and records decisions with rubric rationale. | Independent judgment. | Debrief service | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-031 | Candidate-facing interview pages show only candidate-safe information (no questions, no scorecards); location and phone details release 24 hours before; personal phone numbers are not exposed. | Safety and integrity. | Hub, logistics | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-032 | Accommodation requests are confidential to REC and Coordinator, interviewers see only operational adjustments, and nothing is used in evaluation. | Anti-discrimination. | Accommodation service | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-033 | When the platform room fails, a fallback (dial-in or alternate link) is offered; platform faults never count against a candidate. | Fairness. | Room telemetry, no-show | [PROP] |
| BR-INT-034 | Interview status events and access logs are append-only. | Auditability. | Data layer | [SRC: BR-067] |

## JOB

Source: [02_MODULES/JOB_Job_Marketplace_Candidate_Applications.md](../02_MODULES/JOB_Job_Marketplace_Candidate_Applications.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-JOB-001 | Only accounts in a candidate-capable role (CAN, STD, FRL) may submit applications. Recruiter, hiring manager and employer admin roles cannot apply. | Separation of hiring and applying roles; prevents self-dealing. | API authorization on apply command | [SRC: BR-02] |
| BR-JOB-002 | An application can be created only for a listing that is live, not past its deadline, and not suppressed. Closed or unavailable listings return 410. | Prevents wasted work and phantom applications. | Apply gate, DB check at insert | [SRC: BR-16, BR-038] |
| BR-JOB-003 | At most one active application per candidate per listing. After a terminal outcome the candidate may reapply only after a cooldown (default 90 days; waived once if withdrawn within 24 hours of submit). | Stops spam and duplicates. | Partial unique index (authority), apply gate | [SRC: BR-15, BR-039; OD-JOB-01] |
| BR-JOB-004 | Profile completeness must be at or above the threshold (default 70 percent) to apply. | Ensures employers get usable applications. | Apply gate (server) | [SRC: BR-037, BR-061; OD-JOB-02] |
| BR-JOB-005 | Apply rate limit: 5 submissions per hour and 50 per day per candidate. | Abuse control. | API rate limiter | [SRC: SSOT F-04 security] / daily [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-006 | Application status is owned by the server, changes only through defined commands, and each change appends a status event; events are never edited or deleted. | Auditable lifecycle. | Domain command, DB append-only | [SRC: BR-17, BR-20] |
| BR-JOB-007 | The candidate view is a projection that contains only candidate-safe fields. Internal notes, scorecards, ratings, tags, reviewer identities and sourcing data never appear. | Protect hiring team candour and fairness. | Projection serializer plus contract test | [SRC: BR-19] |
| BR-JOB-008 | Pay is stored as minimum and maximum minor units with ISO 4217 currency and period; displayed ranges must be truthful; where disclosure is required the listing cannot be served without pay. | Pay transparency law and trust. | Listing projection builder | [SRC: BR-179, F-04] [DER] |
| BR-JOB-009 | Drafts autosave locally every 5 seconds and to the server every 30 seconds, keep the last 10 versions, and expire 90 days after last edit. | Recover work. | Client and draft service | [SRC: BR-18] / expiry [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-010 | Submit is idempotent on a client-supplied idempotency key. | Network retries must not duplicate. | Apply command | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-011 | On submit, profile fields, resume and answers are frozen into an immutable snapshot version. Later changes create new versions only through FR-JOB-028. | Evidence integrity. | Application service | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-012 | Hidden jobs and companies are private to the candidate, reversible, and removed from every candidate surface immediately. Employers are never told. | Candidate control. | Query layer filter | [SRC: BR-13] |
| BR-JOB-013 | Saved searches: max 25 per candidate; alerts include only listings published after last evaluation (no backfill). | Predictable alert volume. | Saved search service | [SRC: F-04 step 7] / limit [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-014 | Alert delivery is a service-owned audited scheduler with idempotent delivery keys, honors consent and quiet hours, and unsubscribe takes effect before the next send. | Legal and trust. | Scheduler, NTF (planned) | [SRC: BR-14, BR-31] |
| BR-JOB-015 | Feed and search return only live, non-suppressed listings from the projection; unpublished, moderated, or hidden-by-user items never appear. | Data safety. | Search index filter | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-016 | A chronological view is always available; Newest sorts by original publish time; ranking factors are disclosed on demand. | Transparency. | Query and UI | [SRC: BR-124] |
| BR-JOB-017 | Ranking, filtering, recommendations and fit never use protected attributes or proxies (age, gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, marital status, nationality except stated work eligibility). | Fairness and law. | Feature allowlist, model review | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-018 | Knockout questions are limited to objective, job-related, platform-approved rule types, disclosed to the candidate before answering, auto-decline only if the employer enabled strict mode, with a reason category and a right to human review. | No hidden automated rejection. | ATS config validation and apply flow | [SRC: BR-171] [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-019 | Uploaded files are type-checked, size limited (10 MB), virus scanned before text extraction; extracted text is encrypted at rest. | Security. | File service | [SRC: BR-043, BR-044] |
| BR-JOB-020 | A candidate may withdraw any non-terminal application; the action is irreversible by the candidate; scheduled interviews are cancelled and pending offers are declined. | Candidate autonomy. | Application command | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-021 | Withdrawal is refused once an offer is accepted; the candidate must contact the employer or ATS unwind applies. | Prevent invalid hire state. | Application command | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-022 | Post-submit edits are limited to contact details, additional documents and clarification notes; required and knockout answers are locked; each edit creates a version; disabled at offer stage. | Fairness and integrity. | Application command | [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-023 | Offer decisions are made only by the candidate account, with typed confirmation, once per offer, honoring expiry; support and other roles cannot decide for the candidate. | Consent integrity. | ATS offer command with actor check | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-024 | Interview slot acceptance is atomic and one accepted slot per invite; an expired or revoked invite cannot be accepted. | No double booking. | INT scheduling command | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-025 | Rejection always carries a reason category; feedback text is visible only to the candidate; candidates may request feedback within 30 days; the employer is due to reply in 7 days. | Candidate feedback loop. | Projection, task engine | [SRC: BR-217, BR-219, BR-222, BR-218] |
| BR-JOB-026 | A listing with no employer activity for 21 days and waiting applicants is labelled Inactive and demoted; reconfirmation requested at 30 days; default expiry 60 days. | Ghost-job control. | Freshness job | [PROP] / expiry [SRC: BR-057; OD-JOB-03] |
| BR-JOB-027 | Reposted listings display the original publish date and a Reposted tag; reposting does not reset freshness sorting. | Honest freshness. | Projection builder | [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-028 | Listings that request fees, gift cards, bank details or identity numbers are blocked or held; application forms may not request national id numbers, bank details or passwords. | Fraud and privacy. | Publish scan, form validator | [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-029 | Reporter identity is hidden from the reported employer and public; known only to MOD and PAD. Reports of the same listing by the same user within 30 days merge. | Safe reporting. | Report service | [SRC: BR-136 analogy] [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-030 | Imported listings are labelled with source, never presented as native, and removed within 24 hours of a valid takedown request. | Honesty and legal. | Import pipeline | [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-031 | Applying to an imported listing redirects to the source; no candidate data is sent without the candidate submitting on the source. | Privacy. | UI, outbound link policy | [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-032 | External (self-reported) applications are private to the candidate, labelled self-reported, and never used in employer-facing signals. | Trust of signals. | Tracker, API scope | [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-033 | Company follows are private; employers see only aggregate follower counts when at least 10. | Privacy. | Employer analytics API | [PROP] aligns [SRC: BR-207 k>=10] |
| BR-JOB-034 | Only the chosen place is stored; commute origin is coarsened to about 1 km; exact addresses never reach employers. | Location privacy. | Search service | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-035 | Work-authorization answers are sensitive, used only for eligibility and shown only to the hiring team after submission; never used in ranking. | Sensitive data and non-discrimination. | Form and projection | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-036 | A blocked employer cannot see the candidate in sourcing or receive outreach, and the candidate must unblock before applying to it. Employers are not told of blocks. | Candidate protection (for example current employer). | Sourcing API, apply gate | [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-037 | Recommendations respect negative signals immediately; items under confidence 0.5 are suppressed and 0.5 to 0.7 labelled; recommendations carry a reason. | Quality and honesty. | Recommendation assembler | [SRC: BR-065, BR-066] |
| BR-JOB-038 | Candidate data export is delivered within 30 days (target minutes); deletion honors employer legal holds with disclosure. | Data rights. | Export job | [SRC: BR-063] |
| BR-JOB-039 | Easy apply is available only when the listing requires no custom questions, cover letter or extra documents; otherwise the full form is used. | Predictable UX. | Listing flag from ATS | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-040 | Applications with no status event for 90 days after submission become `expired` and show "No response"; the candidate is notified once. | Avoid stale limbo. | Scheduler | [SRC: BR-058] |
| BR-JOB-041 | When a listing closes, applicants are notified once; existing applications continue under ATS control. | Clarity. | Listing close handler | [DER] |
| BR-JOB-042 | Machine-translated listing text is labelled as translated, with a toggle to the original. | Honesty. | UI | [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-043 | Referral codes are valid for 90 days, cannot be self-referrals, and progress sharing with the referrer needs the candidate's consent. | Fraud and privacy. | Referral validator | [SRC: BR-235] [PROP] |
| BR-JOB-044 | Status notifications are deduplicated per change and batched when more than 3 arrive within 10 minutes. | Avoid notification spam. | Notification dispatcher | [PROP] |

## LRN

Source: [02_MODULES/LRN_Learning_Course_Experience.md](../02_MODULES/LRN_Learning_Course_Experience.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-LRN-001 | Only courses in state `published` appear in the public catalog, search and sitemap. `unlisted` courses are reachable only by direct link or invite. Drafts, in-review, unpublished, archived and taken-down courses never appear. | Learners must not see unfinished or removed content. | Catalog read model, search index, API | [SRC: SSOT §10.22 BR-093] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-002 | Visibility is decided server-side for every list, count, facet and direct read: institution-private, region-blocked and sanctioned items are excluded, and counts exclude them too. | Prevent leakage of private catalog and counts. | API and index filters | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-003 | Each course has one primary category, up to 3 secondary categories, up to 10 tags, exactly one level from {beginner, intermediate, advanced, all_levels} and one primary language. | Reliable filtering and navigation. | Publish check (STU), taxonomy service | [SRC: SSOT BR-096] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-004 | Prerequisites marked `required` block enrollment with an explanation; `recommended` ones only warn. Free-text items are never evaluated. | Avoid false blocks; keep honesty. | Eligibility gate | [SRC: SSOT §9.2 F-07 step 7; BR-022] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-005 | At most one active enrollment per (account, course). Enroll is idempotent on this natural key. | Prevent duplicates and double charges. | DB unique index, enroll service | [SRC: SSOT BR-046] |
| BR-LRN-006 | An enrollment is pinned to one published course version; completion is judged on that version. Moving to a newer version is optional and never forced; completed enrollments are never reopened. | Fair rules for the learner who started. | Enrollment service | [SRC: SSOT BR-105; YASH-G3 SPEC-06 §3.4] |
| BR-LRN-007 | Paid access begins only after a verified payment event from BIL (planned); returning from checkout grants nothing. Activation is idempotent on the payment event id. | Redirects can be forged. | Enrollment consumer | [SRC: SSOT BR-115; YASH-G3 SPEC-06 INV-T17] |
| BR-LRN-008 | Anonymous and non-enrolled viewers can reach only lessons flagged `preview`; every other lesson, manifest and resource returns 403. | Protect paid content. | Content API | [SRC: SSOT BR-094] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-009 | Every lesson content, media-token and resource request is authorized against the enrollment state (`active`, or `completed` within retention) and lock state at request time. | Zero unauthorized access. | Content API, edge | [SRC: SSOT §9.2 F-07 security] |
| BR-LRN-010 | Refund eligibility: full refund when requested within `refundWindowDays` {30} of purchase and progress is at most `refundProgressThresholdPct` {20}; otherwise pro-rated per BIL policy; after completion only by human exception with a recorded reason. | Fairness and abuse control. | Refund service, BIL | [SRC: SSOT BR-100; OD-29] [DEC-REQ] OD-LRN-03 |
| BR-LRN-011 | Access expiry ends access to lessons but preserves progress and never revokes credentials already earned. | Learners keep what they earned. | Expiry sweep | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-012 | After `dropped` or `expired`, progress is retained {90} days; re-enrollment within that time restores it, after that starts fresh. | Allow return without indefinite storage. | Enrollment service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-06 §3.2] |
| BR-LRN-013 | Progress events are idempotent on (enrollmentId, lessonKey, kind, clientSeq); the server keeps the highest `clientSeq`; `completed` is sticky and never reverted by later `started` or `position` events. | Offline replay, out-of-order delivery. | Progress service | [SRC: SSOT BR-021; YASH-G3 SPEC-06 §3.3] |
| BR-LRN-014 | Completion of lessons graded by rule, and of courses, is decided only by server-side rule evaluation on the pinned version. The client can never assert completion except for lessons whose rule is `manual`. | Trustworthy credentials. | Rule evaluator | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-06 §3.4] |
| BR-LRN-015 | A video lesson with rule `watch` completes when unique watched time is at least `videoCompletionThresholdPct` {90} of duration; seek-skipped time beyond `seekSkipCreditCapPct` {25} is not credited; media time, not wall time, is used. | Honest completion. | Progress service | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-06 §3.3] [DEC-REQ] OD-LRN-04 |
| BR-LRN-016 | Resume is offered when the saved position is at least 5 seconds and below 95 percent of duration; the latest server timestamp wins across devices. | Predictable continuity. | Player, progress service | [SRC: YASH-MICRO FEAT-08-03.1] |
| BR-LRN-017 | Quiz lessons complete on a passing result from ASM; graded quizzes count toward the course grade, practice quizzes are unlimited and ungraded; attempts are bounded by the configured maximum. | Consistent assessment semantics. | Lesson rules, ASM consumer | [SRC: SSOT BR-107, BR-108] |
| BR-LRN-018 | When a section or course is `sequential`, lesson N+1 is locked until lesson N is complete; default is free navigation. | Author-intended order. | Content API | [SRC: SSOT BR-047] |
| BR-LRN-019 | An instructor or co-instructor of a course cannot rate or review it and cannot sign off their own enrollment; any learner enrollment they hold never yields ratings or instructor-class evidence for themselves. | Conflict of interest. | Review and sign-off services | [SRC: SSOT BR-104; YASH-MICRO AC-05-04-53] |
| BR-LRN-020 | A review requires a verified enrollment (active or completed, not refunded) and at least {20} percent progress. One review per learner per course, editable. Reviews on refunded enrollments are excluded from aggregates. | Authentic reviews. | Review service | [SRC: SSOT BR-095] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-021 | A numeric average rating is shown publicly only when at least {5} eligible reviews exist; before that the course shows "New" and the count. | Avoid misleading small samples. | Catalog and review read models | [PROP] OD-LRN-08 |
| BR-LRN-022 | Reviews publish immediately unless auto-moderation holds them; instructors may reply once publicly (no edit after 24 hours) and can never edit, hide or delete a learner review; removals follow moderation with appeal. | Fair, tamper-resistant reviews. | Review and moderation services | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-023 | One certificate is issued per completed enrollment (or per program completion), only after rule-based completion; it has an unguessable id and a reproducible SHA-256 hash of its canonical payload. | Verifiable and non-duplicable. | Certificate service | [SRC: SSOT §9.2 F-07 acceptance; F-52] |
| BR-LRN-024 | Revoked, expired and superseded certificates remain verifiable with their status and reason class; they are never silently deleted. | Auditability. | Certificate service, verify page | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-025 | Evidence hand-off happens exactly once per completed enrollment (idempotent on enrollmentId). Authority-verified evidence requires at least one graded integrity-protected assessment passed or an independent instructor sign-off (class `instructor`); watch-only completion yields none. | No inflated authority. | Evidence consumer | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-06 §3.4; V61-17] [DEC-REQ] OD-LRN-02 |
| BR-LRN-026 | At most {3} non-transactional learning nudges per learner per week; inactivity nudges only at 7, 14 and 30 days once per gap; quiet hours and opt-outs are honored. | Avoid nagging. | Nudge scheduler | [SRC: SSOT §9.2 F-07 notifications] [PROP] |
| BR-LRN-027 | A streak day counts when at least one qualifying activity (a lesson completed or {5} or more minutes of media watched) occurs in the learner's local day; one freeze per week; streaks never gate access. | Gentle consistency. | Streak service | [PROP] |
| BR-LRN-028 | Instructors see learner-level data only for their own course and only fields needed (progress, scores, Q&A); aggregate outcome analytics require at least 30 learners with measurable outcomes; individual outcomes are never exposed without consent; analytics are labeled correlational. | Privacy and honest analytics. | Analytics API | [SRC: SSOT BR-189 to BR-193] |
| BR-LRN-029 | Notes, bookmarks, highlights, flashcards and saved lists are private to the learner and never visible to instructors, institutions or recruiters. | Safe personal study space. | API authorization | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-030 | Only learners with an active or completed enrollment (and course staff) can post in Q&A and discussions; rate limits {5 questions and 20 answers per hour}; links limited for new accounts. | Quality and spam control. | Social service | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-031 | Course announcements are limited to 1 per day per course; learners can mute emails and push per course. | Avoid noise. | Announcement service | [SRC: SSOT BR-102] |
| BR-LRN-032 | Offline downloads only for lessons the author allowed, active enrollments, at most {3} devices, license TTL {30} days renewed online, revoked on drop, expiry, refund and takedown; completion is still decided online. | Protect content and rights. | License service | [PROP] OD-LRN-05 |
| BR-LRN-033 | External-provider lessons expose only controls the provider's declared capabilities support; unsupported providers are rejected at authoring; embeds come only from allowlisted domains; protected content is never downloaded or proxied. | Honest, safe embeds. | Player, CSP, authoring | [SRC: SSOT BR-084, BR-085, BR-088, BR-090] |
| BR-LRN-034 | A failing media provider or asset affects only its lesson; the course stays usable and the learner can report the problem. | Containment. | Player | [SRC: SSOT BR-086] |
| BR-LRN-035 | Every published video lesson has captions or a transcript available to learners; auto-generated text is labeled until the author reviews it. | Accessibility. | Publish check (STU), player | [SRC: YASH-MICRO FEAT-08-03.3] |
| BR-LRN-036 | At most {2} concurrent playback sessions per account; a newer session evicts the oldest with a message; patterns of sharing are flagged for review, not auto-banned. | Limit account sharing. | Playback session service | [PROP] OD-LRN-09 |
| BR-LRN-037 | Playback and download authorization uses signed tokens with a TTL of {5} minutes, bound to enrollment, lesson and device session; tokens are never logged or placed in analytics. | Prevent link sharing. | Media edge | [SRC: SSOT §9.2 F-07 security] |
| BR-LRN-038 | Cohort runs have enrollment open and close times, start, end and a grace period; deadlines are soft or hard; late submissions are flagged and treated per the author's policy; extensions are per learner, audited. | Predictable schedules. | Cohort and assignment services | [SRC: SSOT BR-111] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-039 | A submission snapshot is immutable once submitted; resubmission creates a new revision within the allowed count; grades attach to a revision. | Fair, auditable grading. | Submission service | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-040 | Each peer-reviewed submission needs at least 2 completed reviews; reviewers cannot review their own or their group's work; reviews are anonymous to reviewees by default. | Reliable peer grades. | Peer review service | [SRC: SSOT BR-103] |
| BR-LRN-041 | Live-session attendance is recorded when the learner is present at least {50} percent of the scheduled duration; the recording notice is shown before joining. | Fair attendance and consent. | Live session service | [PROP] |
| BR-LRN-042 | Sequenced paths unlock courses in the declared order; a program certificate is issued only when all required path courses are complete and any capstone is passed; path progress is derived from member enrollments. | Program integrity. | Path service | [SRC: SSOT BR-106, BR-110] |
| BR-LRN-043 | Personal learning plans hold at most 50 items and never gate enrollment or access; learning goals are limited to 3 active. | Planning aid, not a lock. | Plan service | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-044 | Recommendations carry a reason, exclude completed, enrolled and dismissed items, use only data covered by the learner's personalization consent, use no protected attributes, and never mix unlabeled sponsored items. | Trust and fairness. | Recommendation service | [SRC: SSOT BR-184 to BR-188] |
| BR-LRN-045 | Prerequisites are evaluated at enrollment time only and not re-evaluated afterwards. | Stable enrollments. | Eligibility gate | [SRC: YASH-G3 SPEC-06 §9] |
| BR-LRN-046 | Skills declared by authors are claims until completion; evidence is created only at rule-based completion, never from partial progress, and is tied to the course version. | Honest skill evidence. | Evidence consumer | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-047 | Unpublishing or archiving a course blocks new enrollments but preserves access for existing enrollees; safety or legal takedown can revoke access. | Fair treatment of learners. | Catalog and content API | [SRC: SSOT BR-114; YASH-G3 SPEC-06 §3.5] |
| BR-LRN-048 | Course grade = sum of item weight times score over graded items, rounded half up to 1 decimal; ungraded items are pending; instructor overrides require a reason and are audited and visible to the learner. | Transparent grading. | Gradebook service | [SRC: SSOT BR-108] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-049 | Moderators and instructors hide posts, never hard-delete them, with a reason and audit; the author sees the placeholder and reason. | Accountable moderation. | Social service | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-050 | Study groups are opt-in, limited to {8} members; members choose what they share; no default sharing. | Privacy. | Group service | [PROP] |
| BR-LRN-051 | Adaptive review and spaced repetition are suggestions only; they never gate access or completion and never mint evidence. | Avoid hidden gates. | Review service | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-052 | Public course pages carry only published catalog data (with structured data and canonical URLs); no learner data appears in public HTML. | Privacy and SEO. | Page rendering | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-053 | Wishlist holds at most 200 items; comparison holds at most 3 courses. | Bounded lists. | Wishlist API, compare view | [PROP] |
| BR-LRN-054 | Institution assignments may override advisory prerequisites and, if institution policy permits, enforced ones (recorded); institutions see learner data only within the visibility scope shown to the learner before the first lesson, and never notes or discussions. | Respect learner and institution needs. | Enrollment and analytics services | [SRC: SSOT §10.20 BR-072..BR-082] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-055 | Access and discount codes are random, stored hashed, and have a use limit and expiry; redemption is atomic and idempotent per (code, account); more than 5 failures in 10 minutes triggers delays, 20 a one-hour lock. | Prevent guessing and over-use. | Redemption service | [PROP] |
| BR-LRN-056 | Plan-entitled enrollments end after a grace period {7 days} when the entitlement ends; progress and credentials are kept; re-subscription restores access within retention. | Fair subscription behavior. | Entitlement consumer | [SRC: SSOT §9.2 F-07 step 3] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-057 | Days and weeks for goals and streaks use the learner's profile time zone; time zone changes take effect at the next period boundary. | Consistent counting. | Goal and streak services | [PROP] |
| BR-LRN-058 | Pause is allowed once per enrollment for at most {90} days on self-paced courses only (not cohort-bound or institution-assigned), and freezes the access clock. | Fair breaks. | Enrollment service | [PROP] |
| BR-LRN-059 | The certificate name is the learner's chosen legal or display name set before first issuance; corrections need a reason and create a superseding version while the original stays verifiable. | Accurate credentials. | Certificate service | [DER] |
| BR-LRN-060 | On export or erasure, learning records are exported fully; erasure removes personal content and leaves a tombstone certificate record verifying as "Record removed at the holder's request" without personal data. | Privacy with credential integrity. | Data-rights service | [SRC: SSOT Appendix E V61-19] [DER] |
| BR-LRN-061 | Search queries linked to an account are retained at most {90} days, used only for relevance and gap reporting, never for advertising; zero-result queries are logged without account ids. | Privacy. | Search logging | [PROP] |

## MEN

Source: [02_MODULES/MEN_Mentorship_Coaching_Career_Services.md](../02_MODULES/MEN_Mentorship_Coaching_Career_Services.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-MEN-001 | Verification levels gate capability: free peer mentoring needs L1; paid sessions and services need L2; work with minors and program lead roles for minors need L3. | Proportionate trust. | Capability guard | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-002 | Mentoring of minors happens only inside institution or approved programs with guardian consent, L3 mentors, platform-only communication and sessions, and no recording without guardian consent. | Child safety. | Program, session, messaging guards | [SRC: BR-128] [DEC-REQ] OD-MEN-06 |
| BR-MEN-003 | A mentor with hiring authority cannot be paid by, or evaluate, a candidate with an open application at the same employer; conflicts are disclosed. | Prevents hidden hiring advantage. | Booking guard, ATS cross-check | [PROP] [SRC: §4.2] |
| BR-MEN-004 | Paid sessions are paid through the platform; contact details and off-platform payment solicitation are masked and flagged in pre-booking and first-30-day messages; circumvention leads to enforcement. | Marketplace integrity and safety. | Message filter, TSF | [PROP] [DEC-REQ] OD-MEN-07 |
| BR-MEN-005 | A peer mentorship with no session or message for 30 days auto-closes, warned at 21 days; pauses up to 60 days stop the clock. | Keeps relationships alive. | Sweep job | [SRC: BR-194] |
| BR-MEN-006 | Alumni mentorship is opt-in only and never enabled by default at graduation. | Consent. | Settings default | [SRC: BR-245] |
| BR-MEN-007 | A rating requires a completed session; one rating per rater per session; ratings reveal when both submit or after 7 days; a mentor score shows only after 3 ratings. | Honest, unbiased reviews. | Feedback service | [PROP] [SRC: BR-095 pattern] |
| BR-MEN-008 | Cancellation and no-show rules: mentee cancels at least 24 hours before for a full refund; mentor cancels always refund fully and count against reliability; no-show after 15 minutes. | Predictability. | Booking and refund services | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-009 | Private notes are readable only by their author; shared notes and goals only by the pair; AI summaries need both parties' opt-in. | Confidentiality. | Notes service | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-010 | Sessions are not recorded unless every participant consents in-session; consent can be withdrawn; recordings retained 30 days by default. | Privacy. | Session room | [SRC: OD-48] [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-011 | Mentors have a configured capacity (default 10 active mentees); mentees have at most 5 pending requests and one request per mentor per 30 days after a decline. | Quality and anti-spam. | Request service | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-012 | Mentor search, suggestions and badges never use payment, plan or promotion; ranking inputs are documented. | No pay-to-rank. | Ranking service | [SRC: §4.2; BR-BIL-004] |
| BR-MEN-013 | Mentors set their own prices within platform bounds or offer free; the platform fee comes from BIL parameters. | Fair marketplace. | Pricing validation | [PROP] [SRC: OD-28] |
| BR-MEN-014 | Resume reviewers see only the shared resume version, cannot edit the profile and must not advise fabricating experience or credentials. | Integrity. | Reviewer access scope | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-015 | Mock interview scorecards are private to the mentee, advice only and never sent to employers or used in ranking. | Candidate protection. | Visibility rules | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-016 | A safeguarding report in a serious category suspends the mentor's new bookings immediately pending review. | Child and participant safety. | Report workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-017 | Program organizers see participation metrics and milestone status, never session notes, messages or goals content. | Confidentiality in programs. | Program dashboards | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-018 | Program participants may request one re-pair without giving a reason; further re-pairs need organizer approval. | Autonomy. | Pairing service | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-019 | Mentor verification expires after 12 months and must be renewed; lapsed mentors are paused. | Current trust. | Verification job | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-020 | Group sessions have capacity limits, and minors may join only institution or program groups with guardian consent. | Safety and quality. | Registration guard | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-021 | In employer programs no one is paired with a person in their own reporting line; mentors and mentees in the same program are paired with conflict checks. | Power imbalance. | Pairing service | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-022 | Mentors see only the mentee fields shared in the request or pairing; intake, profile and messages are otherwise private. | Data minimization. | Field allowlist | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-023 | Mentor suspension or removal refunds or reassigns booked sessions and unused package credits. | Fairness to mentees. | Suspension workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-024 | Listings and sessions must not guarantee jobs, salary or outcomes; claims are scanned and reviewed. | Honest marketing. | Listing validation | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-025 | Session times are stored in UTC with each participant's time zone; all windows (cancel, reveal, edit, availability) are computed server-side. | Correctness across zones. | Time service | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-026 | A slot can be booked once; checkout holds a slot for 10 minutes. | No double booking. | Atomic reservation | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-027 | Listings are limited to career-guidance categories on an allowlist; legal, medical, therapy, financial planning, immigration advice and job placement for a fee are excluded. | Scope and regulatory safety. | Category validation | [PROP] [SRC: §4.2] |
| BR-MEN-028 | Paid listings require completed payout onboarding in a supported country. | Payments feasibility. | Publish guard | [PROP] [SRC: BR-BIL-024] |
| BR-MEN-029 | Expert calls and group sessions follow the same verification, conduct and refund rules as one-to-one sessions. | Consistency. | Shared services | [PROP] |
| BR-MEN-030 | Employer-run programs use mentoring tools only; compensation, performance and HR records for internal mentors are outside the platform. | SSOT non-goal (generic HR/payroll). | Program scope | [SRC: §4.2] |

## MKT

Source: [02_MODULES/MKT_Market_Intelligence_Career_Pathing.md](../02_MODULES/MKT_Market_Intelligence_Career_Pathing.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-MKT-001 | Canonical skills and roles are created and changed only by users with the taxonomy-curator permission; other users may only propose. | Prevents taxonomy pollution. | Taxonomy service, admin console | [SRC: SSOT BR-141] |
| BR-MKT-002 | Every skill tag on a course, challenge, job, profile or role requirement references a canonical `skillId`; free text is resolved or queued. | Comparable counts and matching. | Skills API, tag validators in consumers | [SRC: SSOT BR-144] |
| BR-MKT-003 | Skill relationships are directional (`prerequisite_of`, `subskill_of`, `supersedes`) or symmetric (`related_to`); `prerequisite_of` must be acyclic, checked at write; traversal depth is at most 5. | Valid dependency reasoning. | Graph service | [SRC: SSOT BR-142, BR-146, BR-147] |
| BR-MKT-004 | `correlates_with` edges are computed statistically from aggregates above sample thresholds and are never edited manually. | Objectivity. | Nightly job | [SRC: SSOT BR-143] |
| BR-MKT-005 | A candidate emerging skill needs at least 5 independent signals (distinct employers, jobs, users, courses or institutions, counted once per source entity; default also at least 3 distinct employer or institution sources) before promotion review. | Avoids hype and manipulation. | Candidate evaluator | [SRC: SSOT BR-148]; independence detail [PROP] (`OD-MKT-06`) |
| BR-MKT-006 | Taxonomy changes ship only in published, immutable versions with four-eyes approval and automatic reference migration; deprecation requires a successor. | Safe evolution. | Version service | [SRC: SSOT §6.2]; four-eyes [PROP] |
| BR-MKT-007 | No aggregate is published with fewer than `min_cohort_k` distinct contributors in the cell (default 10); feature overrides: career-transition edges at least 20 [SRC: BR-160]; stricter values are allowed; values below default need a decision record. | Re-identification protection. | Privacy engine (FR-MKT-033) | [SRC: SSOT BR-178, BR-160, BR-158, BR-207, BR-220] |
| BR-MKT-008 | Suppression is complementary: a suppressed cell must not be derivable from totals, siblings, or overlapping queries; counts are rounded; query dimensions and budgets are capped per client. | Blocks differencing attacks. | Privacy engine | [DER] |
| BR-MKT-009 | Salary reports carry a weight: 0.5 self-reported, 1.0 employment-verified. | Data quality. | Salary service | [SRC: SSOT BR-177] |
| BR-MKT-010 | Money is stored and displayed in minor units with an ISO-4217 currency. | Correctness. | Domain types | [SRC: SSOT BR-179] |
| BR-MKT-011 | Company-specific salary figures are shown only above the threshold (default `min_cohort_k`); the SSOT value of 3 is an override below default and needs an owner and counsel decision; an employer opt-in cannot lower it until decided (`OD-MKT-05`). | Privacy. | Display service | [SRC: SSOT BR-180]; [DEC-REQ] |
| BR-MKT-012 | Contributors may withdraw any submission at any time; aggregates are recomputed and the contribution removed within 24 hours. | Data rights. | Salary and consent services | [SRC: SSOT BR-181] |
| BR-MKT-013 | Equity data is aggregated separately and never merged into base-pay percentiles. | Prevents distortion. | Aggregation job | [SRC: SSOT BR-183] |
| BR-MKT-014 | Reports outside ±3σ (robust) of the cell median, duplicates, bursts and impossible values are flagged and excluded until reviewed; rate limit is 5 reports per user per day. | Data integrity. | Quality service | [SRC: SSOT F-86 step 7] |
| BR-MKT-015 | Published snapshots are versioned and immutable; compute may run nightly, publication cadence is set by `OD-MKT-02` (SSOT states nightly in F-86 and quarterly in BR-182). | Reproducibility; conflict recorded. | Snapshot service | [SRC: SSOT BR-182, F-86]; conflict recorded |
| BR-MKT-016 | Career transitions are collected only with explicit opt-in; an individual's transitions are visible only to that individual. | Consent. | Transition service, authz | [SRC: SSOT BR-157, BR-159] |
| BR-MKT-017 | Updates to the graph or taxonomy never retroactively change published historical snapshots; new data produces a new snapshot version. | Auditability. | Snapshot service | [SRC: SSOT BR-162] |
| BR-MKT-018 | Every insight or recommendation shows its data sources, sample size, window and, where applicable, a confidence interval. | Transparency. | API contract, UI | [SRC: SSOT BR-163] |
| BR-MKT-019 | Outcome and trend statements are descriptive or correlational; the product never states or implies a guarantee or causation. | Honesty. | Copy review, UI templates | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT BR-193] |
| BR-MKT-020 | When data is insufficient the product shows a "not enough data" state; it never fabricates, interpolates silently, or shows zero for suppressed cells. | Trust. | UI and API | [SRC: SSOT F-85 failure modes] |
| BR-MKT-021 | Every snapshot records sources, window, method version, taxonomy version, sample size, computed-at; a snapshot older than 2× its cadence is flagged stale; snapshots without provenance are not published. | Traceability. | Publication gate | [DER] |
| BR-MKT-022 | External data is used, displayed and exported only as its license allows, with the required attribution; expired licenses disable the source. | Legal compliance. | Source registry, export | [PROP] |
| BR-MKT-023 | No individual-level record appears in any export, API response, dashboard or admin view of aggregates. | Privacy. | API gateway, exports | [DER] |
| BR-MKT-024 | Readiness and path indicators are explainable (factors and weights shown), never use protected attributes or proxies, and are never exposed to employers, recruiters or matching. | Fairness; non-goal on opaque scoring. | Authz, model gate | [SRC: SSOT §4.2, BR-185]; [DER] |
| BR-MKT-025 | Employer-facing supply and talent views are aggregate only, rounded, and suppressed under threshold; they never list or rank individuals. | Candidate protection. | Employer dashboards | [DER] |
| BR-MKT-026 | Employer pay-equity analysis uses data the employer uploads, stays inside that tenant, outputs aggregates only, suppresses small cells, and deletes raw rows per retention. | Narrow HR boundary. | Equity job | [PROP] (`OD-MKT-08`) |
| BR-MKT-027 | Forecasts cover at most 12 months, always show an interval and model version, and need at least 12 months of valid history. | Honest uncertainty. | Forecast job | [SRC: SSOT F-151] |
| BR-MKT-028 | Institution dashboards are cohort-level only; faculty and administrators cannot see non-consented individual data. | Student privacy. | Authz | [DER] from [SRC: docs/experience, METRICS_CATALOG §6.2] |
| BR-MKT-029 | Partner API keys are scoped, rate-limited, hashed at rest, auditable and revocable; responses obey the same suppression as the UI. | Safe API. | API gateway | [PROP] |
| BR-MKT-030 | Reposted jobs (same employer, title and location within 30 days) count once in demand signals. | Accurate demand. | Ingestion | [PROP] |
| BR-MKT-031 | Geography is published no finer than metro or region where thresholds pass; no street-level or postal-level insight. | Re-identification control. | Display service | [DER] |
| BR-MKT-032 | Breakdowns by sensitive attributes come only from voluntary, separate, purpose-limited self-identification, subject to threshold and review, and are never used as inputs to any score. | Fairness data handling. | Fairness store | [SRC: SSOT F-119]; [DER] |
| BR-MKT-033 | Disputes about displayed data are reviewed within the SLA; upheld disputes lead to a corrected version and notification of the filer. | Accountability. | Dispute workflow | [PROP] |
| BR-MKT-034 | Currency conversion uses dated rates; on conversion failure the original currency is shown and the report is excluded from cross-currency aggregates. | Correctness. | Salary service | [SRC: SSOT F-86 failure modes] |

## MSG

Source: [02_MODULES/MSG_Messaging_Realtime_Communication.md](../02_MODULES/MSG_Messaging_Realtime_Communication.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-MSG-001 | A direct conversation can be started only between two active members who are connected and not blocked. A non-connection can send only a message request, and only if the recipient's setting allows requests. If the recipient chose Everyone, the message goes to the main inbox. | Strangers never reach the main inbox by default. | Messaging service at conversation create and send | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT BR-129] |
| BR-MSG-002 | A message request is one message of 1 to 500 characters with no attachments or links. One pending request per sender and recipient. After Decline or Ignore the sender waits 30 days; after 2 declines or expiries the sender cannot request that person again. Declines are silent. Requests expire after 30 days. A sender may send at most 20 requests per day. | Limits unsolicited contact without revealing refusals. | Messaging service | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-003 | Recruiter outreach requires a verified organization, a stated purpose (specific open job, talent pool, or interview request), a message of 50 to 1,500 characters, no phone numbers, emails or external links, and a candidate who allows outreach. No bulk sends or automated sequences. | Accountable, hiring-only contact; keeps the product out of sales prospecting (SSOT §4.2). | Outreach service | [DER] [PROP] `OD-MSG-01` |
| BR-MSG-004 | An outreach credit is consumed on send to a non-connection and refunded if the candidate replies within 7 days. No refund for decline or silence. | Rewards relevant outreach. | Credit ledger service | [SRC: SSOT BR-129] |
| BR-MSG-005 | Outreach is capped per rolling 7 days at 20 (Pro), 50 (Team) or a custom number (Enterprise). A second outreach to the same candidate for the same purpose is blocked for 14 days unless the candidate replied. Org daily cap default 200. | Volume control. | Outreach service, BIL entitlements | [SRC: SSOT BR-130] caps; repeat and org cap [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-006 | Candidate preferences are binding: outreach is blocked for excluded companies, excluded industries, candidates with outreach Off, and quiet hours defer notifications. The recruiter is never told which preference blocked the send. Preferences such as minimum compensation are never disclosed. | Candidate control and privacy. | Outreach service | [DER] |
| BR-MSG-007 | Introduction messages are separate from cold outreach, use no outreach credit and do not count against caps. | Dignified warm intros. | Context thread service | [SRC: SSOT BR-214] |
| BR-MSG-008 | Members aged 16 and 17 cannot receive recruiter outreach, message requests from non-connections or broadcasts from non-institution senders; they can message connections and institution staff and peers allowed by their institution; groups with unconnected adults are not allowed. | Protects minors. | Messaging service using age claim from IDN | [SRC: SSOT BR-128] `OD-MSG-06` |
| BR-MSG-009 | A message is 1 to 5,000 characters; up to 10 attachments, 25 MB each, 100 MB per message; allowed types only; content sniffing decides type; attachments are unavailable until scanned. | Abuse and cost control. | Messaging and media services | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-010 | Each send carries a client message id. The server persists before acknowledging, dedupes on (conversation, sender, client id), assigns a per-conversation sequence, and delivery is at least once with exactly-once display. Order is by sequence. | Reliability on poor networks. | Messaging service | [SRC: SSOT WF-10 clientMessageId dedupe] |
| BR-MSG-011 | Edit within 15 minutes with an Edited marker and kept revisions. Delete for me anytime. Delete for everyone within 60 minutes leaves a tombstone. Reported or flagged content is preserved for TSF regardless of deletion. | Accountability. | Messaging service | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-012 | Read receipts are reciprocal and member-controlled; none in requests or outreach before reply or acceptance; recruiters see Read on outreach only after a reply. Group receipts show counts unless the group has at most 8 members. | Privacy and pressure reduction. | Messaging service | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-013 | Typing indicators are ephemeral and only in accepted conversations. Presence is off by default and visible only to connections when on. | Privacy. | Realtime service | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-014 | Groups have 2 to 50 members; only the creator's connections can be added directly; others must accept an invitation; new members see history only from their join time; groups with unconnected adults are not allowed for minors. | Safety and privacy. | Messaging service | [PROP] `OD-MSG-02` |
| BR-MSG-015 | Search is server-side, scoped to the member's accessible messages and join times; deleted messages leave the index within 5 minutes. | No leakage through search. | Search service | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-016 | Direct messages are retained while at least one participant's copy exists. Deleting for self removes that copy. When all participants have deleted, content purges after 30 days. Members may set auto-delete of their own copy (12, 24, 60 months). | Data minimization with member control. | Retention job | [DER] |
| BR-MSG-017 | Application-context threads are retained for the employer's retention period (default 24 months, bounded 6 to 84) for hiring records; the candidate may hide but not force deletion before then unless law requires; the candidate is told at the first message. | Hiring record obligations. | Retention job, ATS | [PROP] `OD-MSG-05` |
| BR-MSG-018 | Messages are encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher in transit and AES-256 at rest. End-to-end encryption is not provided in v1. | Server access is required for safety, search and legal duties. | Platform | [DER] `OD-MSG-04` |
| BR-MSG-019 | Staff cannot read message content except: reported content (scope limited), member consent in a ticket (scoped, time-boxed), valid legal order, or security incident break-glass with two approvers. Every access is logged and visible to the member after any legal bar lapses. | Privacy by design. | Access service, audit log | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT §5.9] |
| BR-MSG-020 | Message content is never used for advertising, recruiter ranking, profiling or model training. Scanning is limited to malware, illegal-content hashes, link reputation, and rate and scam patterns. AIC features read a conversation only on the member's per-use request. | Trust. | Delivery pipeline, AI gateway | [DER] [SRC: SSOT §16.5] |
| BR-MSG-021 | Rate limits: 30 messages per minute and 600 per hour per member; new accounts limited to 10 new conversations or requests per day and no links in first messages; group creation 10 per day; duplicate text to more than 5 recipients per hour triggers throttle and TSF flag. | Abuse resistance. | Rate limiter | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-022 | A report shares with TSF only the selected messages and attachments (default the reported message and 20 around it). | Data minimization. | Report service | [DER] |
| BR-MSG-023 | After a block, the blocked sender's messages are accepted but not delivered, and the sender sees the normal Sent state; nothing reveals the block. Groups hide each other's messages. | Safety without retaliation. | Messaging service, NET block state | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT BR-238; NET `BR-NET-008`] |
| BR-MSG-024 | Scam and off-platform warnings are advisory banners; they never delete or hide messages; high-severity banners cannot be disabled by users. | Protects job seekers. | Delivery pipeline | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-025 | Realtime uses the ladder WebSocket, SSE, long polling, interval polling; reconnect with jitter and resume by last seen sequence; sessions revoked disconnect within 60 seconds; at most 5 devices connected per member. | Works on every network. | Realtime gateway | [DER] |
| BR-MSG-026 | Push notifications show no message text by default; muted conversations send none; quiet hours defer non-safety notifications; no push when active in the conversation. | Privacy and noise control. | Notification adapter | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-027 | Employer messages show the organization name and verified badge; the candidate is told when team members can read the thread; the disclosure cannot be disabled; internal notes are never visible to candidates. | Transparency. | Messaging service, EMP | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-028 | Broadcasts are one-way, limited to audiences the sender administers, at most 2 per day and 1,000 recipients, no promotional content; recipients can mute except mandatory notices. | No spam. | Broadcast service | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-029 | Export contains only what the requester could see, excludes internal notes, is limited to 3 per day, expires after 7 days. | Data rights without leakage. | Export service | [DER] |
| BR-MSG-030 | Messaging meets WCAG 2.1 AA: keyboard operation, live-region announcements, text status labels, reduced motion, 200 percent zoom. | Accessibility. | UI and QA | [DER] |
| BR-MSG-031 | Links are scanned at send and click; shorteners are expanded; unknown domains show an interstitial; `javascript:` and `data:` links are refused; previews only for allowlisted domains and never for requests before acceptance. | Phishing defense. | Link service | [DER] |
| BR-MSG-032 | Plans may bound attachment storage, group size, broadcasts and outreach, but plain messaging between connections, receiving, replying, reporting, blocking and export are never paywalled. | Safety is not a feature tier. | BIL entitlements, Messaging | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-033 | Offline: cached conversations for 30 days encrypted on device, cleared at sign-out; queued sends expire after 24 hours; the server re-validates every rule on replay; no offline requests, outreach, edits or deletes. | Server authority. | PWA and Messaging service | [SRC: SSOT §19] [DER] |
| BR-MSG-034 | Response-time badges use a 90-day median of recruiter first replies and are shown only with at least 10 replied threads. | Fair, non-misleading signal. | Analytics job | [PROP] |
| BR-MSG-035 | When an account is deleted, the owner's copy is removed; other participants keep received messages with the sender shown as "Former member". | Data rights balanced with recipient records. | Lifecycle job | [DER] |

## NET

Source: [02_MODULES/NET_Networking_Community_Referrals.md](../02_MODULES/NET_Networking_Community_Referrals.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-NET-001 | A connection request requires two active accounts, no existing connection, no pending request in either direction, no block in either direction, and a recipient setting that permits the sender. A concurrent opposite request auto-accepts. | Prevents duplicates and unwanted contact. | NET service, request create | [DER] |
| BR-NET-002 | Outstanding sent requests are capped at 100 and new requests at 30 per day per member. | Spam and harassment control. | NET service, per-member counters | [PROP] `OD-NET-07` |
| BR-NET-003 | The request note is at most 300 characters; URLs and email addresses are removed from notes of accounts younger than 7 days. | Reduces scam outreach. | NET service validation | [PROP] |
| BR-NET-004 | Decline and ignore are silent: the sender sees Pending until expiry, then Not accepted. After a decline or expiry, the sender may re-request after 30 days; after 3 declines or expiries from the same sender to the same recipient the sender cannot request that person again. | Protects recipients from retaliation and repeat pressure. | NET service, request create | [PROP] |
| BR-NET-005 | Pending requests are nudged on day 7 and day 21 (max 2) and expire on day 45. Senders may withdraw at any time. | Keeps caps usable and the inbox clean. | Daily job | [PROP] `OD-NET-07` |
| BR-NET-006 | A connection is mutual. Removal is silent and unilateral. Connection-only access ends at once. | Predictable symmetric trust model. | NET service | [DER] |
| BR-NET-007 | Follows are unique per (follower, target); they never grant access beyond the target's public content; blocked or muted targets cannot be followed. | Separates attention from trust. | NET service | [SRC: SSOT BR-121] |
| BR-NET-008 | Block removes connection, follows, pending requests, introductions and referral requests in both directions, hides both parties from each other everywhere, and is never revealed to the blocked party. Blocked users cannot request referrals or be offered as introducers. | Safety, privacy. | One shared relationship check in every read and write path | [SRC: SSOT BR-213, BR-216, BR-238] |
| BR-NET-009 | Mute hides a person's or topic's content from the muter without unfollowing and without notifying the muted party. | Low-confrontation control. | Feed and notification filters | [SRC: SSOT BR-127] |
| BR-NET-010 | Visibility (Public, Connections, Followers and connections, Group, Private) is enforced server-side on every read, search, notification and share. | No client-side-only privacy. | NET service, read path | [SRC: SSOT BR-122] |
| BR-NET-011 | Members aged 16 and 17 have private-by-default profiles, receive connection requests only from people sharing a verified context (institution, group, mutual connection), do not appear in discovery to unrelated adults, cannot use contact discovery or introductions, and cannot choose Named for profile views. Under 16 are not permitted. | Protects minors. | NET service with age claim from IDN | [SRC: SSOT BR-128] `OD-NET-08` |
| BR-NET-012 | People suggestions use only declared, consented signals and show the reasons; protected attributes and inferred sensitive attributes are never used. | Fairness and transparency. | Discovery service | [SRC: SSOT BR-184, BR-185] |
| BR-NET-013 | Contact discovery uses client-side hashed emails, mutual opt-in, 30-day TTL, no import of any social graph, no invitations to non-members. | Privacy by design. | Discovery service | [SRC: SSOT MIG-05] |
| BR-NET-014 | Introductions are separate from cold outreach; requesters are capped at 10 per week; the introducer and the target can opt out; paths are visible only to the requester. | Dignified warm intros. | Introduction service | [SRC: SSOT BR-209..BR-216] |
| BR-NET-015 | Endorsements require an existing connection at the time of giving, one per (giver, receiver, skill), and are never treated as verification. | Prevents fake proof. | NET service | [SRC: SSOT BR-131] |
| BR-NET-016 | A written recommendation is displayed only after the recipient accepts it; edits after acceptance require re-acceptance. | Recipient control. | NET service | [SRC: SSOT BR-132] |
| BR-NET-017 | Every post, comment and article passes a pre-publish abuse scan. Per-member limits: 10 posts per day, 60 comments per hour, 10 mentions per post, 5 topics per post. | Abuse resistance. | Content service, rate limiter | [SRC: SSOT BR-125] limits [PROP] |
| BR-NET-018 | One reaction per user per target (changeable); one repost per user per post; reposting requires a Public original. | Honest counts. | Content service | [SRC: SSOT BR-116, BR-117] |
| BR-NET-019 | Edits keep an Edited marker and version history. | Accountability. | Content service | [SRC: SSOT BR-118] |
| BR-NET-020 | Post authors and comment authors may hide or delete comments on their posts; authors may disable comments; moderators may override. | Author control. | Content service | [SRC: SSOT BR-119] |
| BR-NET-021 | Mentions notify only members who allow mentions from that author; mentions in text are never blocked by recipient settings. | Anti-harassment. | Notification fan-out | [SRC: SSOT BR-120] |
| BR-NET-022 | A strict chronological feed view is always available; ranking factors are disclosed on demand. | Member agency. | Feed service | [SRC: SSOT BR-124] |
| BR-NET-023 | Ranking may use only these signals: recency, relationship type and strength, declared topic interests, group membership, content quality signals (completeness, reports ratio), member feedback (not interested, snooze), format preference. It may never use protected or inferred sensitive attributes, private messages, assessment results, application or interview status, location trails, affinity memberships, or payment. | Fairness. | Ranking service allowlist | [DER] from [SRC: SSOT BR-185, §18] |
| BR-NET-024 | Sponsored content, if ever enabled, is labelled, sits in separate slots, has no effect on organic ranking or hiring visibility, and uses no sensitive targeting. | Honesty; avoids pay-to-rank. | Feed service, BIL | [SRC: SSOT BR-126, BR-187] |
| BR-NET-025 | Groups have at least one owner; group moderators act only within the group; platform moderation overrides group decisions. | Clear accountability. | Group service | [PROP] |
| BR-NET-026 | Join mode is Public, Private (approval) or Hidden (invitation); bans prevent rejoin; admin declines are silent. | Community self-governance. | Group service | [PROP] |
| BR-NET-027 | Alumni group membership requires a verified affiliation; graduates keep alumni status; members may opt out of default join; no cross-institution data leakage. | Trust and privacy. | Group service | [SRC: SSOT BR-241, BR-243, BR-246, BR-247] |
| BR-NET-028 | A referral request needs: an open job in an enabled programme, at least one verified current employee connection, a skill match of at least 70 percent, and fewer than 3 prior requests in the last 30 days (maximum 3 per rolling 30 days; see `OD-NET-05`). A pitch is 50 to 300 characters. | Quality and anti-spam. | Referral service | [SRC: SSOT F-142, BR-233] |
| BR-NET-029 | Every referral requires the referrer's explicit consent and a verified current employment at the employer; the candidate's resume is shared only after consent. | Consent and integrity. | Referral service | [SRC: SSOT BR-234, BR-237] |
| BR-NET-030 | The referral tag is a visible priority signal for human recruiters only; it never auto-ranks, auto-advances, rejects or demotes any application and is never used by matching to hide other candidates. | Avoids opaque pay-to-rank and bias. | ATS integration, matching | [SRC: SSOT BR-235] [DER] |
| BR-NET-031 | A referrer may make at most 20 referrals per calendar quarter; attribution lasts 12 months from the referral date (configurable 3 to 24 months); earliest consented referral wins. | Fairness and fraud control. | Referral service | [SRC: SSOT BR-239, BR-240] |
| BR-NET-032 | Referral rewards follow employer policy; XP is the default; TalentSphere records eligibility and never disburses money. | Avoids payroll scope. | Referral service | [SRC: SSOT BR-236] [DEC-REQ `OD-NET-04`] |
| BR-NET-033 | Self-referral, referrals for payment, reciprocal rings and referrals of already-active candidates for reward are prohibited; flagged referrals withhold rewards until human review; no automatic sanction. | Integrity. | Referral service, TSF | [PROP] |
| BR-NET-034 | Profile-view logging honours the viewer's privacy mode at the time of the view; Private views are not logged individually. | Viewer privacy. | Profile service | [SRC: SSOT BR-133] |
| BR-NET-035 | Privacy defaults: connections visible to connections only, requests from shared context, discoverable on, follows on, activity status off, mentions Everyone, introductions on, alumni listing on, affinity listing off. | Safe defaults. | Settings service | [PROP] |
| BR-NET-036 | An external person referred by an employee shares no data with the employer until they consent; invitation email is sent once; non-consenting emails are deleted after 30 days. | Data minimization. | Referral service | [PROP] |
| BR-NET-037 | Content hidden by moderation stays visible to its author with a notice and appeal path; severe categories bypass group moderators and go straight to TSF. | Due process. | Content service, TSF | [DER] |
| BR-NET-038 | Deleted social content is hidden at once, retained 30 days in restricted storage, then purged, except TSF evidence and legal holds; blocks are retained for the retention window; referral records are kept in minimal form for 12 months. | Data rights with safety. | Lifecycle job | [DER] |
| BR-NET-039 | Graph limits: 30,000 connections, 5,000 follows, 5,000 blocks, 1,000 bookmarks per folder. | Abuse and performance. | NET service | [PROP] |
| BR-NET-040 | Dismissals, snoozes and mutes train only the member's own ranking and never affect another member's content ranking. | Prevents brigading. | Ranking service | [SRC: SSOT BR-186] |
| BR-NET-041 | Newsletter subscriptions are opt-in with one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058). | Anti-spam law alignment. | Newsletter service | [SRC: SSOT BR-123] |

## NTF

Source: [02_MODULES/NTF_Notifications_Communication.md](../02_MODULES/NTF_Notifications_Communication.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-NTF-001 | Preference classes: mandatory transactional (security, verification, legal, billing) cannot be disabled; time-critical (interview reminder, offer) is channel-selectable and ignores quiet hours; engagement is opt-out; nudge is opt-out and capped; marketing is opt-in. | Law and trust. | Catalog + router | [SRC: Yash BR-T085] |
| BR-NTF-002 | Routing evaluates in a fixed order, first match wins: suppression, mandatory, time-critical, disabled category, quiet hours, digest, nudge cap, marketing opt-in, otherwise send on enabled channels with in-app always. | Predictable behavior. | Router | [SRC: Yash DT-07] |
| BR-NTF-003 | Every non-marketing notification creates an in-app item that is the source of truth, regardless of other channels or suppression. | Nothing is lost. | Router | [SRC: Yash DT-07 row 9] |
| BR-NTF-004 | The unread count is server-authoritative and reconciled on every panel open and page focus; clients show at most one optimistic step beyond the last server value. | The badge cannot lie. | API + client | [SRC: SSOT Appendix D M-55] |
| BR-NTF-005 | Delivery is idempotent by `(notificationId, channel)`; duplicate requests by idempotency key collapse; the dispatcher is at-least-once with consumer de-duplication. | No duplicate sends. | Dispatcher | [SRC: Yash SM-NOTIFY, ADR-T09; SSOT BR-31] |
| BR-NTF-006 | Quiet hours default 21:00–08:00 in the user's time zone, DST-safe; they defer non-mandatory, non-time-critical email, push and SMS to the window end; users may change or disable them. | Respect for sleep. | Router + worker | [SRC: Yash BR-T086] |
| BR-NTF-007 | Nudges ≤ {3} per week and ≤ 1 per day; digests ≤ 1 per day; per-channel daily caps for engagement; anomaly caps for mandatory bursts. | Avoid fatigue. | Router + throttle | [SRC: Yash BR-T087] |
| BR-NTF-008 | No message is sent to a suppressed address; hard bounces suppress; complaints suppress marketing and engagement; mandatory notices to a hard-bounced address surface in-app instead. | Reputation and consent. | Router + webhook handler | [SRC: Yash SM-NOTIFY forbidden] |
| BR-NTF-009 | Non-mandatory email carries a working unsubscribe (header and footer); one-click POST applies immediately; GET changes nothing; mandatory email has none and explains why. | Standards and trust. | Email service | [SRC: Yash TEST-MSG-010] |
| BR-NTF-010 | Marketing and product news need explicit opt-in (`comms.marketing_email`), use a separate sending stream and domain with a legal footer, are paced, and auto-pause on complaint thresholds; transactional trust is never lent to marketing. | Reputation separation. | Campaign service | [SRC: Yash DT-07 row 8, CSC] |
| BR-NTF-011 | Push subscriptions are created only after a user gesture, browser permission and in-product opt-in; payloads are generic and encrypted; subscriptions are deleted on logout, session revoke and 410; ≤ {10} devices. | Privacy by design. | Push service | [SRC: Yash INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE] |
| BR-NTF-012 | SMS needs a verified number and explicit per-category opt-in, honors STOP and HELP immediately, is limited to time-critical and security categories, and obeys country rules; marketing SMS is not offered. | Carrier and legal rules. | SMS service | [PROP] |
| BR-NTF-013 | Every notification type is registered in the catalog with class, channels, defaults, TTL and owner; unregistered keys fail CI; a template exists per enabled channel in the default locale. | Governed catalog. | CI + catalog service | [DER] |
| BR-NTF-014 | Templates are versioned and immutable once published; mandatory-class changes need maker-checker; locale fallback is whole-template, never mixed; legal and consent text versions match their source. | Safe content change. | Template service | [SRC: Yash SPEC-02 §8] |
| BR-NTF-015 | Retry schedule 1 m, 5 m, 30 m, 2 h, 12 h, maximum 5 attempts; permanent errors fail at once; TTL 72 h for time-sensitive and 7 d for others; expiry is not a failure of intent. | Bounded retries. | Dispatcher | [SRC: Yash SM-NOTIFY t6..t10] |
| BR-NTF-016 | Mandatory and time-critical lanes have priority and bypass user caps but obey provider limits and anomaly caps. | Reliability. | Throttle | [DER] |
| BR-NTF-017 | Grouped notifications merge by group key and window; nudges obey cool-downs, dormancy limits and send-time re-checks. | Reduce noise. | Router | [PROP] |
| BR-NTF-018 | Digest items are generated at send time from live data, exclude inaccessible content and never include mandatory or time-critical notices; empty digests are not sent. | Accuracy. | Digest worker | [SRC: SSOT F-29] |
| BR-NTF-019 | Emails have complete plain-text parts, accessible markup (contrast, alt text, `lang`), escaped variables and no tracking in mandatory messages; tracking elsewhere only where analytics consent allows. | Accessibility and privacy. | Renderer | [DER] |
| BR-NTF-020 | Push, lock-screen and in-app titles for entries flagged `sensitiveContent` use generic wording and never carry sensitive details. | Shoulder-surfing safety. | Renderer | [DER] |
| BR-NTF-021 | Admin broadcasts need approval, map to mandatory, time-critical or engagement classes (never marketing), and critical banners persist until resolved. | Honest operations communication. | Broadcast service | [PROP] |
| BR-NTF-022 | Org routing expands recipients from assignments and roles at send time; members keep their own preferences; external team channels get minimal data unless detail mode is on and allow-listed; no personal data in push or SMS to teams. | Data minimization. | Org routing | [PROP] |
| BR-NTF-023 | Provider failover requires a sustained error rate above threshold, uses one idempotency token per delivery across providers, and fails back after health returns; it never double-sends. | Reliability without duplicates. | Dispatcher | [DER] |
| BR-NTF-024 | A user may hold ≤ {20} alert subscriptions; matches respect the visibility and consent of the matched content; instant alerts are capped per alert per day. | No leakage via alerts. | Alert service | [SRC: SSOT BR-14] |
| BR-NTF-025 | Delivery rows are retained {90 days} in detail and 24 months aggregated; users can see their own metadata; bodies are not retained beyond delivery. | Storage limitation. | Retention job | [PROP] |
| BR-NTF-026 | Non-production environments never send real messages unless in explicit allow-list mode; production refuses outbox mode without an override; outbox items are labeled not delivered. | Safety. | Config + boot check | [SRC: CLAUDE.md dev outbox] |
| BR-NTF-027 | Sending domains authenticate with SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment; complaint above {0.1%} or hard bounce above {2%} auto-pauses a non-transactional stream. | Deliverability. | Deliverability monitor | [PROP] |
| BR-NTF-028 | Non-mandatory notifications are not sent to accounts that are not `active` (deactivated, suspended, pending erasure); on erasure queued items for the subject are purged and only privacy receipts remain. | Respect for account state. | Router | [DER] |
| BR-NTF-029 | Delivery states are truthful: `delivered` only on provider confirmation (email), inbox row (in-app) or acknowledgment (push); the outbox reports `sent` only. | No false delivery claims. | Dispatcher | [SRC: Yash SM-NOTIFY] |
| BR-NTF-030 | Callers identify recipients by account id; raw addresses and numbers are resolved inside NTF and never returned to callers. | Data minimization. | API | [DER] |
| BR-NTF-031 | Security notices use a fixed recognizable layout and sender, carry no tracked links, contain no direct sign-in links and state that the platform never asks for passwords or codes by message. | Anti-phishing. | Templates + CI | [DER] |
| BR-NTF-032 | In-app items and emails use plain language (reading grade ≤ 9) and every actionable message names the action and its target. | Clarity. | Template review | [DER] |

## PLT

Source: [02_MODULES/PLT_Platform_API_Integrations_Media_Files.md](../02_MODULES/PLT_Platform_API_Integrations_Media_Files.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-PLT-001 | The public API is path-versioned (`/api/v1`). Within a major version only additive changes are allowed; breaking changes need a new major and a deprecation window of at least 6 months (OD-PLT-01) announced with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers, changelog, email and per-client reports; sunset returns 410. | Integrator trust. | Contract diff in CI; gateway headers | [SRC: SSOT §12.18, CON-002] |
| BR-PLT-002 | Every route declares a policy action; authorization is enforced server-side per resource and tenant; clients never learn permissions except as UI hints; direct browser writes to domain tables are prohibited. | Single enforcement point. | API framework; route registry | [SRC: Yash 13 API-STD §1] [SRC: SSOT §12.18] |
| BR-PLT-003 | Access tokens are short-lived (default 30 minutes); refresh tokens rotate and reuse revokes the family; authorization codes are single-use for 60 seconds; API keys and secrets are shown once, stored hashed or encrypted, expire (maximum 1 year), can be IP-restricted and rotate with an overlap. | Limits credential theft impact. | OAuth server; key service | [DER] [PROP] values |
| BR-PLT-004 | Scopes follow `resource.action[:own | :org]`, are least-privilege, are intersected with the grantor's permissions at consent time and re-checked on every request, and widen only through re-consent; no wildcard scopes. | Prevent over-grant. | OAuth server; resource guard · [DER] |
| BR-PLT-005 | Rate limits and quotas apply in layers (edge IP, per principal and endpoint class, per tenant quota, concurrency); counters live in a store shared by all instances; the fail mode is fail-closed for authentication and write bursts and fail-open at a conservative local limit for reads; exceeding returns 429 with `Retry-After`; quota exhaustion is explicit, never a silent throttle. | Availability and fairness. | Gateway limiter | [SRC: SSOT CON-006] [SRC: SSOT §20.1 open] |
| BR-PLT-006 | List endpoints use signed, expiring cursor (keyset) pagination only, default limit 25 and maximum 100 (OD-PLT-03), allow-listed filters and sort keys with a unique tiebreaker, and no offset pagination. | Stable and cheap traversal. | API framework | [SRC: SSOT CON-003, CON-004] |
| BR-PLT-007 | Unsafe writes honor `Idempotency-Key`: same key and payload replays the stored response, same key with another payload is 422, in-progress is 409; keys are retained 14 days (OD-PLT-03); versioned resources require `If-Match` (428 when missing). | Retry safety including offline clients. | Idempotency store | [SRC: SSOT CON-005, CON-012] [SRC: Yash 08 OFF-01-REV2] |
| BR-PLT-008 | All errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with stable `code`, `requestId` and field errors; no internals are exposed; every response carries `X-Request-Id`. | Debuggability and safety. | Error middleware | [SRC: SSOT CON-001] |
| BR-PLT-009 | The API contract is generated from the shared Zod schemas; OpenAPI, SDKs and examples are generated or tested from it; hand-edited OpenAPI is a defect; routes without policy action, scopes and rate class fail the build. | No drift. | CI | [SRC: Yash 13 API-STD §1] |
| BR-PLT-010 | Outbound webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over `timestamp.rawBody` using a per-endpoint secret, with a 5-minute tolerance, dual signatures during a 24-hour rotation overlap; inbound provider webhooks must pass their provider's signature verification and are deduplicated by provider event id before processing. | Authenticity and replay protection. | Webhook subsystem; adapters | [SRC: SSOT CON-007] |
| BR-PLT-011 | Webhook delivery is at-least-once with a bounded retry schedule (standard 7 attempts over about 34 hours, extended to 72 hours), 10-second timeout, no redirects, honoring 429 and 410, circuit breaking to `degraded` and `auto_disabled`, ordering not guaranteed (per-resource sequence provided), and replayability for 30 days. | Reliability without overload. | Webhook delivery job | [SRC: SSOT CON-007, CON-008] [PROP] schedule |
| BR-PLT-012 | Every server-side fetch of a tenant- or user-supplied URL goes through the egress client: https only, allowed ports, checked and pinned DNS, deny ranges (loopback, private, link-local, metadata, IPv6 equivalents), no redirects by default, size and time limits, no ambient credentials. | SSRF prevention. | Egress library; network rules | [SRC: SSOT §13.16] |
| BR-PLT-013 | The domain never calls a vendor SDK directly: every external dependency sits behind a provider port with an adapter, anti-corruption mappers, an owner, a documented degraded mode, contract tests and a removal drill as a release gate. | Vendor replaceability. | Architecture tests; release checklist | [SRC: SSOT §13.4 ADR-009] |
