| BR-PLT-014 | Integration and platform secrets live only in the vault (envelope encryption, tenant-scoped keys), are write-only to users, are decrypted only in the calling process, never logged, rotated on schedule or demand, and access is audited; no plaintext fallback exists. | Secret safety. | Vault service | [SRC: SSOT §13.4] [DER] |
| BR-PLT-015 | An integration connects only with explicit consent to a generated data-sharing summary; disconnect revokes tokens at the provider, stops syncs and asks what to do with imported data; imported records carry provenance (integration id, external id, imported time). | Transparency and control. | Connection service | [DER] |
| BR-PLT-016 | Synchronization is idempotent, resumable and bounded; every two-way sync declares a field ownership table naming the system of record per field; unresolved conflicts go to review, not silent overwrite; source-deleted records are marked, not auto-deleted. | Data integrity. | Sync engine | [SRC: SSOT §19.3 principle] [DER] |
| BR-PLT-017 | SSO requires a DNS-verified domain, strict signature, audience and replay checks, no silent takeover of existing accounts, and an always-available break-glass owner account before enforcement; SCIM deactivation revokes sessions within 5 minutes; JIT provisioning is off by default and least-privilege. | Enterprise security. | SSO and SCIM service | [DER] |
| BR-PLT-018 | LTI 1.3 launches validate the id token (signature via JWKS, issuer, audience, nonce, expiry, deployment id), use one-time state and nonce, and pass back only authorized scores and completions for bound contexts. | LMS interop security. | LTI service | [PROP] |
| BR-PLT-019 | Integration health uses `live`, `inferred`, `degraded`, `not_configured`, `reauth_required` and `unknown`; missing data for two probe intervals is `unknown`, never healthy; breaker state is visible to operators and tenant admins. | Honest status. | Health service | [SRC: SSOT BR-28, §20.2] |
| BR-PLT-020 | Third-party apps are not listed in any directory until the marketplace gate criteria are met and approved; sealed scopes are never available; listing is limited to the career domain; unlisted private apps for one customer are permitted. | Avoid drifting into a general marketplace. | Decision gate | [SRC: SSOT §4.2] [PROP] |
| BR-PLT-021 | Uploads are validated by sniffed content type against a purpose allow-list, with size, count and archive limits; executable and active content is rejected; EXIF and metadata are stripped from images; filenames are normalized and kept apart from random storage keys. | Safe intake. | Upload service | [SRC: SSOT CON-011] |
| BR-PLT-022 | A file is unavailable (not downloadable or embeddable) until it has a clean scan verdict; scan failure or engine outage fails closed; infected files are quarantined and never released; suspicious files go to manual review. | Malware containment. | File state machine | [SRC: SSOT §13.15, CON-011] |
| BR-PLT-023 | Storage quotas are enforced per principal and tenant with reservation at session creation; exceeding blocks new uploads only; plan downgrade never deletes existing data and gives a 30-day grace; warnings at 80% and 100%. | Fair and safe limits. | Quota service | [PROP] |
| BR-PLT-024 | File deletion is two-phase (soft delete with 30-day restore, then purge of object, renditions, CDN entries and index references); erasure propagates except under legal hold or legal retention, with exceptions reported; deletion leaves a content-free record. | Lifecycle and erasure. | Retention service | [SRC: SSOT CON-015] |
| BR-PLT-025 | Private files are served only through short-lived, object-scoped signed URLs (default 15 minutes, maximum 1 hour; share links up to 30 days, revocable); active content (HTML, SVG) is served from a separate sandbox origin with nosniff and CSP; tokens are never logged. | Access control. | Access service; CDN | [SRC: SSOT §13.16] [DER] |
| BR-PLT-026 | Media processing sits behind a provider port; renditions are idempotent by (content hash, profile version); originals are retained; a failed or delayed item affects only itself and the page still renders. | Isolation and cost control. | Media pipeline | [SRC: SSOT §13.15, BR-086] |
| BR-PLT-027 | External media embeds are validated before publication; provider restrictions are never bypassed; protected content is never downloaded; capabilities decide playback and completion options; tenant allowlists are enforced on the server; authors attest rights; unsupported providers fail explicitly. | Rights and safety. | Embed service | [SRC: SSOT BR-083 to BR-090] |
| BR-PLT-028 | Imports are validate-then-commit: validation writes nothing; commit is batched with per-row idempotency keys; a file changed after validation must be re-validated; one active import per entity type per tenant; undo is available within 24 hours where the handler supports it. | Data integrity. | Import engine | [SRC: SSOT WF-17] |
| BR-PLT-029 | Exports are asynchronous, authorization is checked at request and at generation, files are encrypted and delivered by expiring signed links, row and concurrency limits apply, sealed classes are excluded except for the data subject's own package or an approved legal process, and each export carries a manifest. | Safe portability. | Export engine | [SRC: SSOT BR-063] |
| BR-PLT-030 | Jobs are idempotent and bounded: each kind declares attempts, backoff, timeout, concurrency, `replaySafe` and an idempotency key; a lease with fencing token prevents stale workers from committing; a job whose lease expires after its last allowed attempt becomes `dead`; non-retryable errors go straight to `dead`. | No loops or duplicates. | Job engine | [SRC: SSOT §13.8, CON-008] |
| BR-PLT-031 | Job states are `queued`, `running`, `retrying`, `succeeded`, `dead`, `cancelled`; `failed` is not a state (it is `retrying` or `dead`); terminal states are `succeeded`, `dead`, `cancelled`. | Resolves the legacy terminal-set ambiguity. | Job schema | [SRC: SSOT §13.8 open] [DEC-REQ] OD-PLT-05 |
| BR-PLT-032 | Schedules declare a time zone and a missed-run and overlap policy; exactly one instance creates each slot (unique slot key); new schedules with side effects can start in dry-run. | Predictable recurring work. | Scheduler | [SRC: SSOT BR-31, §13.6] |
| BR-PLT-033 | The sandbox is isolated from production (separate data, hosts and credentials), uses synthetic data and test modes of providers, never sends real email, SMS or payments, and rejects live credentials. | Safety of testing. | Sandbox environment | [PROP] |
| BR-PLT-034 | Developer apps need a verified publisher for user-delegated scopes, exact https redirect URIs, privacy and terms URLs, justified high-risk scopes and review before live use; scope widening or redirect changes re-trigger review; suspension revokes tokens within 60 seconds. | App ecosystem trust. | Developer portal | [PROP] |
| BR-PLT-035 | Every API call, job, file, webhook and integration carries tenant and purpose context; cross-tenant access is impossible by construction (tenant-scoped keys, queries and caches); caches include tenant in keys. | Tenant isolation. | Request context; data layer | [SRC: SSOT §20.2, CON-014] |
| BR-PLT-036 | Domain events are written in the same transaction as the state change (outbox) and delivered at least once; consumers are idempotent by event id; one failing consumer does not block others. | No dual-write loss. | Outbox dispatcher | [SRC: SSOT §13.5 ADR-T05] |
| BR-PLT-037 | Event types are registered with versioned schemas; within a version changes are additive; breaking changes publish a new version in parallel for a deprecation period; event payloads are thin snapshots with ids. | Stable integrations. | Event registry | [DER] |
| BR-PLT-038 | API request logs keep metadata 30 days and no bodies by default; debug body capture is time-boxed (60 minutes), redacted, deleted after 7 days and never for sealed classes; webhook payload snapshots follow 30-day retention. | Minimization. | Logging pipeline | [SRC: SSOT CON-016] [PROP] values |
| BR-PLT-039 | Integrations request only the scopes and fields declared in their definition; HRIS and similar sources are read with a field allowlist that excludes compensation, performance, medical and protected-class data. | Data minimization. | Adapter definitions | [DER] |
| BR-PLT-040 | Every adapter and queue consumer defines a degraded mode, bounded timeouts and a circuit breaker; provider outages degrade the specific feature with a clear message and queue work instead of failing silently or duplicating effects on recovery. | Graceful degradation. | Adapter framework | [SRC: SSOT §20.1, §13.4] |
| BR-PLT-041 | Sealed data classes (assessment answers and keys, message bodies, identity documents, background-check reports, health-class data) are not offered through third-party scopes, webhook payloads or org exports; only the data subject's own package or an approved legal process may include them. | Containment. | Scope catalog; payload builders | [DER] (aligned with BR-ADM-017) |
| BR-PLT-042 | CDN caching applies only to public or tokenized-and-verified content; cache keys include tenant for tenant-scoped content and exclude tokens; purge by tag completes within 60 seconds; private content is `Cache-Control: private` otherwise. | No leakage through caches. | CDN configuration | [SRC: SSOT CON-014] |
| BR-PLT-043 | Payment and subscription state is changed only by verified, deduplicated provider webhooks applied idempotently; webhooks acknowledge after durable enqueue; provider calls carry idempotency keys; reconciliation compares provider records to the ledger daily. | Financial integrity. | Payment adapter; BIL | [SRC: SSOT BR-32] |
| BR-PLT-044 | Email and SMS go through provider ports with suppression lists (hard bounces, complaints, opt-outs), authenticated sender domains (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), separate streams for transactional and bulk, no message bodies or addresses in logs, and idempotency keys; mandatory security messages may bypass marketing suppression but not hard-bounce suppression. | Deliverability and privacy. | Email and SMS adapters | [DER] |
| BR-PLT-045 | Meeting providers create unique links with waiting-room defaults; recording is off by default and requires consent flags before scheduling; recordings are ingested only under a retention class. | Consent. | Meeting adapter | [PROP] |
| BR-PLT-046 | Identity verification stores only outcome facts (verified, level, name match, document country and type, expiry month, time, vendor reference); no document images or biometrics are stored by TalentSphere; attempts are limited (3 per 24 hours); results expire per policy. | Minimization. | IDV adapter | [DER] |
| BR-PLT-047 | Calendar access uses the least scope: free/busy by default and event write on one chosen calendar; reading event titles needs the user's explicit choice; cached availability is deleted on disconnect. | Privacy. | Calendar adapter | [PROP] |

## PRF

Source: [02_MODULES/PRF_Profile_Resume_Portfolio.md](../02_MODULES/PRF_Profile_Resume_Portfolio.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-PRF-001 | Only the profile owner may create, edit or delete profile content. Staff may only act under BR-PRF-034. | Identity data integrity and trust. | API authz on every write; database row policy by owner id | [SRC: SSOT F-12 "Own-row edit only"; BR-005] |
| BR-PRF-002 | Every profile write carries the expected `version`; a mismatch returns 409 and writes nothing. | Prevents silent overwrite between tabs or devices. | API + database `version` check | [SRC: SSOT F-12 edge cases] |
| BR-PRF-003 | Rich text is sanitized server-side to an allowlist (bold, italic, lists, `https`/`mailto` links with `rel="nofollow ugc noopener"`); raw HTML and scripts are removed. | Stored XSS prevention. | Write path and render path | [SRC: SSOT F-12 Security Requirements] |
| BR-PRF-004 | Public and cross-user responses contain only public-safe fields. Phone, login email, date of birth, address and tax identifiers are never returned unless the owner chose a contact audience that includes the viewer. | PII protection. | Serializer allowlist per viewer class | [SRC: SSOT F-12 step 10] |
| BR-PRF-005 | A profile that does not exist, is hidden, archived, suspended, erased, or blocked for the viewer yields the same 404 response body, headers and timing class. | No existence leak. | Public profile route and all lookups | [SRC: SSOT F-12 failure modes] |
| BR-PRF-006 | Each section has one visibility value (public, connections, recruiters, private). The effective visibility is the narrower of section visibility and profile state; decided only on the server. | Single enforcement point. | `visibleSections()` used by page, API, search snippets, resume pages, exports | [SRC: SSOT F-12 step 9] |
| BR-PRF-007 | Completeness is a deterministic server-side function of profile content and the active weight set (default basic 20, skills 15, experience 20, education 15, certifications 10, portfolio 10, summary 10); weights sum to 100. The job-application threshold of 70 is owned by JOB (planned) and reads this score. | Reproducible gating. | Domain function; weights table with versioning | [SRC: SSOT F-12 step 8; BR-037; BR-061] |
| BR-PRF-008 | Every skill on a profile references a canonical skill id from the governed taxonomy. Users cannot create canonical skills; unknown skills go to a suggestion queue. | Clean matching and search. | Skills write path | [SRC: SSOT BR-141, BR-144] |
| BR-PRF-009 | A profile lists at most 50 skills and pins at most 5 as top skills. | Signal quality; UI sanity. Limits are defaults. | Skills write path | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-010 | Dates must be valid: end not before start; experience start not in the future; education end year up to current year + 8; no `end` when current. | Data quality. | Section validators | [DER] |
| BR-PRF-011 | Editing employer, title, start date or end date of a verified work entry, or issuer, title or dates of a verified credential claim, removes the verified mark and notifies EVD. The UI warns before saving. Non-locked fields (description, skills used) may change freely. | Verification must describe what was verified. | Section update handlers; EVD event | [DER] from SSOT §6.1 |
| BR-PRF-012 | Slug: 3–30 chars of `a-z0-9-`, no edge or double hyphen, not all digits, unique case-insensitively, not reserved or offensive; at most 3 changes per rolling 12 months; old slug redirects 90 days then is quarantined 30 days before anyone can claim it. | Stable links, anti-squatting and impersonation control. | Slug service + unique index | [SRC: SSOT F-12 slug edge case]; numbers [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-013 | Profile images: JPEG, PNG, WebP, ≤ 4 MB (avatar), MIME verified from bytes, malware scanned, EXIF and GPS stripped, re-encoded. | Safe media. | Media pipeline | [SRC: SSOT F-12 step 2] |
| BR-PRF-014 | Resume exports are append-only records; deleting an export soft-deletes the file artifact only. Each export or application creates an automatic version. | Evidence of what was sent. | Export service; storage policy | [SRC: SSOT BR-26] |
| BR-PRF-015 | Verification marks appear on a resume export only if the owner toggled them on and the underlying item is currently verified at render time. | Marks must be true at the moment shown. | Resume renderer | [DER] |
| BR-PRF-016 | Parsed, imported or AI-suggested content is a draft. It is written to the profile only after explicit user confirmation, and AI may not add skills, employers, dates or credentials the user has not claimed. | User remains author of claims. | Import, parse, tailor flows | [SRC: SSOT BR-33] |
| BR-PRF-017 | Uploaded resumes and import files are malware scanned before any parsing; extracted text is encrypted at rest; raw files are deleted after 30 days (resume) or 24 hours (import file) unless the user keeps them as a resume original. | Sensitive data handling. | Upload pipeline | [SRC: SSOT BR-043, BR-044]; retention [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-018 | A user has at most one default resume; if the default is deleted or archived, the user must pick another or have none. | Predictable apply-time behavior. | Resume service | [DER] |
| BR-PRF-019 | Limits: 10 active resumes per user, 50 saved versions per resume, 20 active share links. | Abuse and cost control. Defaults. | Resume service | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-020 | The ATS check is advisory. It never blocks saving, exporting, sharing or applying. | Avoid false blocking from heuristics. | UI and export service | [DER] |
| BR-PRF-021 | Resume share links use random 128-bit tokens stored hashed, expire (default 30 days, max 365), are revocable, `noindex`, and return 410 when expired or revoked. | Safe link sharing. | Share service | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-022 | Recommendations require an authenticated author; anonymous recommendations are not permitted. | Accountability. | Recommendation service | [DER] from SSOT BR-153 |
| BR-PRF-023 | A recommendation is 50–3000 characters, states a relationship, is shown only after the recipient approves, and there is at most one per author-recipient pair (edits are revisions that need re-approval). The owner can hide or delete it but never edit its text. | Authenticity of social proof. | Recommendation service | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-024 | An open-to-work signal expires 90 days after it is set unless renewed. Query-time checks treat expired signals as off. | Stale availability misleads recruiters. | Settings service; SRC | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-025 | Open-to-work, preferences and discoverability are used by search, matching and outreach only within the consent the user set; changes apply at query time, not only after re-indexing. | Consent must be immediate. | SRC query filter; AIC and JOB reads | [SRC: SSOT F-92 "consent revocation < 24h"] |
| BR-PRF-026 | Salary expectation and work authorization are never public and are shared only at the audience the user chose. | Sensitive employment data. | Preferences serializer | [DER] |
| BR-PRF-027 | Profile views are attributed to a viewer only if the viewer allows it; private-mode viewers appear as an anonymous category; a user in private mode cannot see their own viewers list. | Viewer privacy and reciprocity. | View logger and analytics API | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-028 | Profile view events are retained 12 months, then reduced to aggregates; breakdowns are suppressed when fewer than 5 views in the period. | Data minimization; re-identification control. | Retention job; analytics API | [PROP]; threshold [DEC-REQ] OD-PRF-05 |
| BR-PRF-029 | Block rules (person, organization, domain) make the profile, its search appearances and its messages unavailable to the blocked party without notifying them. Anonymous links cannot be blocked and the owner is told so. | Personal safety and employer hiding. | Viewer check on all surfaces | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-030 | Protected attributes (age, date of birth, gender, marital status, race, religion, disability, photo, native language, military or volunteer affiliation) are never required, never used in ranking or match scoring by PRF, and optional fields default to hidden. Photos are excluded from resume templates by default in regions where it is not customary. | Anti-discrimination by design. | Schema; resume defaults; reviews | [DER] |
| BR-PRF-031 | Pronouns, preferred name and name pronunciation are optional and displayed only if set. | Inclusion. | Profile UI | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-032 | Imports accept only files the user uploads from their own export; the platform does not scrape or log into third-party sites to read a profile. | Terms-of-service and privacy compliance. | Import feature scope | [SRC: SSOT F-65 LinkedIn Decoupling] |
| BR-PRF-033 | The owner may hide verified marks but cannot hide a Disputed or Revoked status on an item that is displayed. | Prevents using hiding to mislead. | Mark renderer | [DER] |
| BR-PRF-034 | Moderators and support may view private profile content only inside an open case with a stated reason; every view and every content removal is audit logged; staff cannot edit text, only remove content or restore on owner request. | Least privilege. | Admin tools; audit log | [SRC: SSOT BR-67] |
| BR-PRF-035 | Portfolio media: images ≤ 10 MB, PDFs ≤ 50 MB, 20 media per project; external embeds only from allowlisted providers and only if the provider allows embedding; alt text is required before a project is published. | Safety and accessibility. | Media service; publish validator | [SRC: SSOT F-12 step 7; BR-083..084]; limits [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-036 | Skills attached to a project or resume create claims, never verified skills; verification comes only from EVD. | Claims are not evidence. | Skill link service | [SRC: SSOT §6.1] |
| BR-PRF-037 | Spoken language level uses CEFR (A1–C2) plus Native. | Common, comparable scale. | Language validator | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-038 | Public profiles carry `noindex` unless the owner opts into search engine visibility; indexable pages expose only public fields. | Control over external discovery. | Page headers and structured data | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-039 | JSON resume export conforms to JSON Resume schema v1.0.0 plus a namespaced `meta.talentsphere` block. | Portability. | Export service | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-040 | Profile history keeps up to 30 snapshots for at least 12 months; content removed for moderation or by erasure is redacted from all snapshots. | Recovery without retaining removed data. | Version service; erasure handler | [PROP] |
| BR-PRF-041 | Accounts flagged under 18 by IDN (planned) can never have public or recruiter-visible sections, cannot be discoverable, and cannot set open-to-work to recruiters. | Child safety. | Visibility service | [DER] |
| BR-PRF-042 | A resume template may carry the "ATS-safe" flag only if it passes the template checklist: real text, standard headings, no layout tables, no text in images, embedded fonts, tagged PDF. | Truthful labeling. | Template publish gate | [DER] |

## PWA

Source: [02_MODULES/PWA_PWA_Offline_Mobile_Extension.md](../02_MODULES/PWA_PWA_Offline_Mobile_Extension.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-PWA-001 | The service worker and every client cache are disposable conveniences, never the business source of truth. A cached response is never proof of current state, authorization or consent; server authority decides. | Integrity and security. | Cache layer; server APIs | [SRC: SSOT §19.2] [SRC: Yash 08 INV-T13] |
| BR-PWA-002 | The never-cache list is enforced in code and tests: authentication, session, MFA, payment and checkout, assessments and proctoring, interview rooms, the admin origin and back-office bundles, sealed data classes, tokenized public URLs (`/r/*`, `/invite/*`), signed file URLs. Admin surfaces are never installable and never offline. | Prevents leakage and stale authorization. | SW routing; CI policy tests | [SRC: Yash 08 PWA-01 R2b] [DER] |
| BR-PWA-003 | On logout, session expiry (after the retention window), account switch, "Clear offline data" or a forced purge, all caches, drafts, outbox rows, local settings and push subscriptions of the account are removed; shared-device mode retains nothing. | Shared-device safety. | Client storage manager; server unsubscribe | [SRC: Yash 08 OFF-01 §10] |
| BR-PWA-004 | Offline writes follow the capability registry: drafts (LD) for reversible content, queued writes (QW) only for allowlisted idempotent actions after OD-PWA-01 fires, and everything consequential, legal, financial, assessed, security-related or real-time is online-only (ON). Unregistered actions default to ON. | Safety by default. | Registry; CI; UI wrappers | [SRC: SSOT §19.2] [SRC: Yash 08 OFF-01-REV2] |
| BR-PWA-005 | Every user intent that may be retried has a UUID idempotency key generated when the intent is created and stored with it; drafts and queued items live 14 days with a warning at 5 days and removal only with consent; server key retention is at least 14 days. | Retry safety. | Client stores; PLT idempotency | [SRC: Yash 08 OFF-01-REV2 §2] |
| BR-PWA-006 | Concurrent changes are detected with entity versions (`If-Match`); material conflicts are never silently overwritten; monotonic data resolves by rule, others by explicit user choice. | No silent data loss. | API (428, 409/412); conflict dialog | [SRC: SSOT §19.3] |
| BR-PWA-007 | The install prompt is shown only to signed-in users after engagement criteria and never during forms, assessments, checkout or interviews; frequency is limited (first, +14 days, +60 days, then never); dismissal and "Don't ask again" are honored. | Respect for users. | Install controller | [PROP] |
| BR-PWA-008 | The service worker never calls `skipWaiting` automatically; updates apply at safe moments with drafts persisted; required updates are set only by minimum version and enforced by API 426; a remote passthrough or unregister mode exists. | Prevent data loss and bricking. | SW; version manifest; API | [SRC: Yash 08 PWA-01 §5] |
| BR-PWA-009 | Notification permission is requested only after a user tap following an explanation, never on load; denial is remembered and not re-prompted for 90 days; push is opt-in per device. | Consent and trust. | Push controller | [SRC: SSOT §19.1] [PROP] |
| BR-PWA-010 | Client storage has budgets per category; the app evicts in a fixed order (images, lazy code, reference data, own-data cache) and never evicts drafts or the outbox without consent; write failures surface to the user. | No silent loss. | Storage manager | [SRC: Yash 08 OFF-01 §6] |
| BR-PWA-011 | The precache holds only the shell critical path and offline page within a 1.5 MB budget; lazy chunks are runtime-cached on first use; back-office bundles are never precached. | Fast install, small footprint. | Build checks | [SRC: Yash 08 PWA-01 R2 B13] |
| BR-PWA-012 | UI labels about local data are literal: "Unsent. Saved on this device only", "Waiting to send", "As of <time>"; never "Synced" or "Sent" unless the server confirmed. | Honesty. | UI components | [SRC: Yash 08 OFF-01-REV2 §1] |
| BR-PWA-013 | Low-bandwidth mode is automatic on Save-Data or slow effective connection and manually overridable; it never removes essential flows and never changes legal or safety content. | Inclusion. | Client and CDN renditions | [PROP] |
| BR-PWA-014 | Mobile UI rules: touch targets ≥ 44 px, no hover-only functions, gesture alternatives, correct input types, zoom never disabled, 16 px inputs, safe-area insets, reflow at 400% zoom, `prefers-reduced-motion` respected. | Usability and accessibility. | `packages/ui`; tests | [SRC: SSOT Appendix D] [DER] |
| BR-PWA-015 | A wrapper or native client is built only after a documented trigger (iOS push or install friction, Android store presence, native-only capability, institution distribution) is measured and approved; a thin web-view-only wrapper is not approved alone. | Cost and store policy risk. | Decision gate (FR-PWA-030) | [SRC: Yash 08 MOB-01 §5] |
| BR-PWA-016 | The extension is local-first: scanning, matching and form detection run on the device; page content, browsing activity and form values are not transmitted or stored beyond in-memory use unless the user saves or fills; the only network calls are the user-initiated actions listed in the privacy disclosure (pairing, profile refresh, save job, resume attach, config fetch); no third-party analytics; no remote code. | Privacy and store compliance. | Extension code; CI; review | [SRC: SSOT BR-30, ADR-006] [DEC-REQ] OD-PWA-02 |
| BR-PWA-017 | The extension requests the minimum permissions (`activeTab`, `storage`, `scripting`, `identity`, `sidePanel`, TalentSphere hosts); job-site and form-site access uses optional host permissions requested at the moment of use; forbidden: `tabs`, `history`, `webRequest`, `cookies`, `<all_urls>`, `webNavigation`; any change needs SAD approval. | Least privilege. | Manifest CI | [DER] |
| BR-PWA-018 | Autofill never submits, never fills on load, never fills sensitive fields (passwords, payment, government identifiers, date of birth, gender, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, health, EEO self-identification) and never generates answers to free-text questions; every value is shown and editable before filling. | Safety and fairness. | Autofill engine | [PROP] |
| BR-PWA-019 | Extension pairing uses OAuth authorization code with PKCE; tokens are short-lived and scoped (`extension.profile.read`, `extension.jobs.save`, `extension.autofill.read`); pairings are listed and revocable; revocation takes effect at once. | Secure delegation. | Auth server; extension | [DER] |
| BR-PWA-020 | Remote extension config is signed, may only disable features or require updates, never add behavior or permissions, and its version counter is monotonic; kill state persists until a newer config changes it. | Safe remote control. | Extension config handler | [DER] |
| BR-PWA-021 | Offline downloadable media is not available until OD-PWA-07 is decided; when enabled, only licensed, provider-permitted content is downloadable, stored encrypted, time-limited and revoked at unenrollment; protected third-party content is never downloaded. | Rights and ADR-T10. | Download manager | [SRC: Yash 08 OFF-01-REV2 §0] [SRC: SSOT BR-084] |
| BR-PWA-022 | Deep links, share targets and file handlers are untrusted input: routes are allowlisted, content size and type validated, no action is performed by a link itself, and staged payloads expire in 10 minutes. | Abuse prevention. | Router; SW | [DER] |
| BR-PWA-023 | App badge counts equal server unread counts, contain no content, are capped at 99 and cleared on read or logout. | Accuracy and privacy. | Badge service | [PROP] |
| BR-PWA-024 | PWA and extension telemetry is whitelist-only, without personal data, content or tokenized URLs; route templates replace paths; sampling applies; nothing is sent without consent or in shared-device mode. | Privacy. | Telemetry client; server schema | [SRC: SSOT BR-27] |
| BR-PWA-025 | Background Sync and Periodic Sync are enhancements only; correctness never depends on them; the app also flushes on open, on focus after reconnection and on a visible timer. | Browser variance. | Sync controller | [SRC: Yash 08 PLATFORM_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX] |
| BR-PWA-026 | `navigator.onLine` is a hint only; connectivity state combines request outcomes and a small reachability probe; captive portals are detected. | Accurate state. | Connectivity module | [DER] |
| BR-PWA-027 | Store listings must be truthful and consistent with behavior: single-purpose statement, permission justifications, data-use disclosure equal to the manifest, real screenshots, no keyword stuffing; listing metadata is monitored for drift. | Approval and trust. | Release checklist | [PROP] |
| BR-PWA-028 | Extension-held personal data (profile snapshot, local resumes, saved-job outbox) is stored encrypted where possible, never leaves the device except through listed actions, and is deleted on disconnect, "Delete local data" or account deletion. | Data minimization. | Extension storage | [SRC: SSOT BR-30] |
| BR-PWA-029 | Capabilities are feature-detected, never inferred from the user agent; every capability-dependent feature has a defined fallback; no core journey requires install, push or any single browser API. | Robustness. | `capabilities` module | [SRC: SSOT §19.1] [SRC: Yash 08 FF-09] |
| BR-PWA-030 | Only one outbox flusher runs per account per device at a time (Web Locks lease, with a BroadcastChannel fallback); delivery is FIFO per entity. | Prevent duplicates and reordering. | Outbox | [SRC: Yash 08 OFF-01] |
| BR-PWA-031 | Push is a convenience channel: payloads are sensitive-content-free and consequential events (offers, legal notices, security alerts) are always also delivered in-app and by email; lock-screen text assumes bystanders. | Privacy and reliability. | NTF routing; payload builder | [SRC: Yash 08 MOB-01 §4] |

## REP

Source: [02_MODULES/REP_Gamification_Reputation.md](../02_MODULES/REP_Gamification_Reputation.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-REP-001 | XP is awarded only by rules in the catalog for verified qualifying events from platform modules; self-reported claims and client-submitted amounts never earn XP. | XP must mean something. | Award engine | [SRC: SSOT BR-053 spirit; F-22] |
| BR-REP-002 | An XP award is idempotent by `(subject, referenceType, referenceId, kind)`; one source event yields at most one award. | No double credit. | Database unique key + engine | [SRC: SSOT BR-25] |
| BR-REP-003 | Positive XP per subject per local day is capped at {200} with cap groups per rule category; excess is recorded in a cap note and not carried over. | Bound farming. | Ledger service | [SRC: SSOT BR-25 daily cap 200] |
| BR-REP-004 | The XP ledger is append-only; balance and level are rebuildable projections; corrections are reversing or adjusting rows with reasons. | Auditability. | Database privileges + domain | [SRC: SSOT table `xp_transactions`] |
| BR-REP-005 | Challenge XP is {20–100} by difficulty, awarded only on a pass, once per challenge for life; practice mode and failed attempts earn nothing. | Meaningful effort. | Rule catalog | [SRC: SSOT F-08 step 7, BR-25] |
| BR-REP-006 | Level is a deterministic function of total XP using a versioned threshold table; it decreases only through reversal or sanction; table changes never lower existing levels. | Predictability and fairness. | Level service | [SRC: SSOT WF-11]; thresholds [PROP] |
| BR-REP-007 | XP, levels and badges have no monetary value, cannot be purchased, sold, transferred or gifted, and no badge criterion includes payment. | Honest incentives. | Rule validation | [SRC: SSOT BR-202] |
| BR-REP-008 | A badge is minted only when verified milestone criteria hold; criteria are declarative, versioned and reference only verified events; instructor and institution badges show their issuer class. | Trustworthy badges. | Badge evaluator | [SRC: SSOT BR-053; Yash BR-T118] |
| BR-REP-009 | A reversal references one original entry, executes at most once and up to its amount; derived awards are re-evaluated; the subject is told the reason. | Transparent corrections. | Ledger service | [DER] |
| BR-REP-010 | Badges expire or are revoked only for stated reasons (expiry policy, invalid basis, sanction), with notice and an appeal path for sanctions; revoked state is reflected in public verification. | Fair removal. | Badge service | [DER from Yash BR-T012] |
| BR-REP-011 | Verifiable badge export is holder-controlled, signed by the platform, includes only holder-approved data, and reports valid, expired or revoked truthfully. | Portability with integrity. | Export service | [PROP] |
| BR-REP-012 | Peer recognition gives no XP; it is limited to {5} per giver per day, once per giver per target, never to self or blocked parties, and enters reputation only as a weighted signal. | Prevents kudos farming. | Recognition service | [PROP] |
| BR-REP-013 | A streak day or week is evaluated in the user's time zone, DST-safe; it needs a qualifying activity; protection and vacation mode are earned or user-set, never purchased; the longest streak is kept. | Fair habit tracking. | Streak service | [SRC: SSOT §13.6 `streak.rollover`; DOR-010 open] |
| BR-REP-014 | Gamification messages never use loss-aversion, guilt or shaming wording; streak reminders are nudges under NTF caps and quiet hours; at most one reminder per day. | Humane design. | Template review + NTF | [PROP]; [SRC: Yash BR-T087] |
| BR-REP-015 | Goals are user-chosen or suggested, max {5} active, carry no penalty for missing, and cannot be public failures. | No pressure. | Goal service | [PROP] |
| BR-REP-016 | A person appears on a leaderboard only after opting in; default is not included; display is name or alias; users under integrity review, sanctioned, deactivated, suspended or erased are excluded; boards under {10} participants show no percentiles. | Privacy and integrity. | Leaderboard service | [DER from SSOT §15.2, BR-167] |
| BR-REP-017 | Boards are computed from ledger entries in the period; the default tabs are weekly and all-time; ties share a rank; reversals adjust ranks at the next snapshot. | Deterministic ranking. | Leaderboard service | [SRC: SSOT F-08, OD-06] |
| BR-REP-018 | A reputation score is derived from signals and configuration, never manually set; computation is deterministic and nightly; corrections change signals. | Integrity of scores. | Reputation engine | [SRC: SSOT BR-164, F-144] |
| BR-REP-019 | Reputation is domain-specific (skill) and context-specific; signals older than the half-life (default {24 months}) count less; labels need ≥ {3} distinct sources. | Relevance and robustness. | Reputation engine | [SRC: SSOT BR-165, BR-166] |
| BR-REP-020 | Reputation is private by default; others see labels only with the subject's consent or within an application the subject submitted; revocation is effective on next read. | Privacy. | Decision function (SET) | [SRC: SSOT BR-167] |
| BR-REP-021 | Reputation signals are auditable by authorized staff; individual signals and their sources are never exposed to the subject or third parties; explanations aggregate by category with a minimum of {3} sources. | Accountability without leakage. | Reputation + explanation service | [SRC: SSOT BR-168, F-144] |
| BR-REP-022 | Signal weight combines base, source credibility (capped), difficulty, proximity and independence; self-signals are excluded; reciprocal and ring patterns are discounted. | Resist collusion. | Reputation engine | [SRC: SSOT F-144 weighting]; discounts [PROP] |
| BR-REP-023 | Negative signals expire after a recovery period (default {12 months} of clean history) or on plan completion; recovery never inflates positive signals. | Second chances. | Reputation engine | [SRC: SSOT F-144 recovery]; values [PROP] |
| BR-REP-024 | XP, levels, streaks, badges and reputation are advisory indicators: they are never the sole basis of an employment, admission or assessment decision, never trigger automated rejection, and enter matching only through the allowlisted inputs of the matching rules. | Human gate. | Policy + matching allowlist | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.1; Yash BR-T070]; OD-REP-07 |
| BR-REP-025 | Suspicious activity is discounted, held or blocked by server-side rules (velocity, repetition, duplication, collusion, identity, automation); holds auto-release after {14 days} unless a case is opened. | Gaming does not pay. | Detector | [SRC: SSOT BR-052]; thresholds [PROP] |
| BR-REP-026 | Sanctions are decided by humans, proportionate, with notice, reason code, and an appeal reviewed by a different person; clawbacks over {500 XP} and bans over {30 days} need a second reviewer. | Due process. | Case workflow | [SRC: Yash BR-T045..T047] |
| BR-REP-027 | Users may set gamification intensity Standard, Minimal or Off and choose to keep or stop tracking; opting out never affects access, eligibility, matching, search visibility or recruiter evaluation. | No coercion. | Preference service + policy | [PROP] |
| BR-REP-028 | Seasons have fixed dates, cannot be changed after start except a notified extension ≤ {7 days}, and finalize results into archives; rank-band badges need a participating cohort ≥ {50}. | Fair competition. | Season service | [PROP] |
| BR-REP-029 | Rule, threshold and weight changes are versioned, simulated, approved by a different person, effective-dated (≥ {7 days} ahead for user-visible changes) and not retroactive except documented fixes approved by SAD. | Safe change. | Config service | [DER] |
| BR-REP-030 | Gamification and reputation logic uses no protected attributes or proxies, no emotion or sentiment analysis, and no biometric behavior; quarterly fairness review is required. | Fairness. | Rule validation + audit | [SRC: SSOT §15.10.2, §15.9.2] |
| BR-REP-031 | Ledgers, streaks, badges, reputation data and preferences are personal data: included in export, removed or anonymized on erasure, and boards remove the person within {15 min} of erasure start. | Data rights. | SET contributors | [SRC: SSOT §15.9.1] |
| BR-REP-032 | Minors are excluded from public leaderboards, share cards and competitive seasons; their gamification is private and minimal. | Child protection. | Preference + board service | [PROP]; OD-IDN-11 |
| BR-REP-033 | Institutional boards require student opt-in for identity, exclude grade data, never influence grading or honors, and are anonymized or deleted at graduation severance. | FERPA-aware design. | Cohort board service | [SRC: SSOT §15.9.2, §15.9.4] |
| BR-REP-034 | XP, level, badges, streaks and leaderboard rank are engagement indicators and are labeled as such; they never substitute for verified evidence, credentials or rungs. | No misleading signals. | UI + API labeling | [DER from SSOT §6] |
| BR-REP-035 | Enterprise internal boards are opt-in, show only team aggregates to managers, are never used for performance, pay, promotion or termination decisions, and cannot be exported to HR systems. | Narrow scope near the HR non-goal. | Enterprise board service | [PROP]; OD-REP-04 |
| BR-REP-036 | Share cards contain only holder-selected fields, use revocable high-entropy links with `noindex`, and make no claim beyond the facts (for example "earned a badge" not "certified"). | Safe sharing. | Share service | [PROP] |
| BR-REP-037 | Reputation contexts (candidate, instructor, mentor, employer, community) have separate signal sets and never blend; public employer or instructor aggregates need a minimum sample of {10} and anonymized sources. | Context integrity. | Reputation engine | [SRC: SSOT F-144, F-148, F-149, HDN-026] |

## SET

Source: [02_MODULES/SET_Settings_Privacy_Consent.md](../02_MODULES/SET_Settings_Privacy_Consent.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-SET-001 | A consent record is purpose-bound, versioned, timestamped and carries a grantee; the default for every scope is no consent; recruiter access beyond an application requires a scope. | Lawful, minimal sharing. | Consent service | [SRC: Yash BR-T061] |
| BR-SET-002 | The consent ledger is append-only (no update or delete by the application role); current state is a rebuildable fold; grants, revokes and expiries are rows. | Auditability. | Database privileges + domain | [SRC: Yash INV-T35] |
| BR-SET-003 | A revocation is effective on the first read after the revoking transaction commits (read-time check, no consent cache); search index removal ≤ 15 min; already exported data is not recalled and the UI says so. | Honest, immediate control. | Decision function + indexer | [SRC: Yash BR-T063, CSC §6] |
| BR-SET-004 | A change of meaning to a purpose text creates a new version and the scope is treated as not granted until re-confirmed (after a {14 d} grace); wording-only changes (non-material) leave grants bound to the old version. | Purpose limitation. | Consent service | [SRC: Yash CSC §1] vs [SRC: SPEC-02 AC-22-01-04]; OD-SET-03 |
| BR-SET-005 | No consent is pre-ticked, bundled with terms, or presented with an asymmetric choice; accept and decline have equal prominence; reading grade ≤ 9. | No dark patterns. | UI standards + review | [SRC: Yash SPEC-02 §4] |
| BR-SET-006 | Visibility choices that imply a consent scope call the consent API in the same transaction; there is no second flag. | Single source of truth. | Domain layer | [SRC: Yash SPEC-02 §3.3] |
| BR-SET-007 | Field visibility is one of `private`, `applications`, `discoverable`, `public`; default `private`; contact details can never be `discoverable` or `public`. | Safe defaults. | Domain layer | [SRC: Yash SPEC-02 §3.1] |
| BR-SET-008 | Per-grantee grants may carry an expiry (default {12 months}, max {24 months}), a reminder 14 days before, and end when the grantee org is closed. | Bounded sharing. | Consent service + worker | [SRC: Yash CSC §3.2] |
| BR-SET-009 | `search.discoverable` and `profile.public_view` prompt re-confirmation every {12 months}; the prompt is not an expiry. | Keeps consent fresh. | Worker | [SRC: Yash SPEC-02 §5] |
| BR-SET-010 | A blocklist holds ≤ {200} orgs, applies to search, suggestions, outreach and grants, covers all members of an org, and is never disclosed to the org; the candidate may still apply after an explicit confirmation. | Protects job seekers. | Decision function | [SRC: Yash FEAT-03-09.3, INV-T40] |
| BR-SET-011 | Search exclusion removes the profile from recruiter search and overrides discoverability without affecting applications or messaging. | Granular restriction. | Indexer + fetch guard | [SRC: Yash BR-T069] |
| BR-SET-012 | The access log shows accessing organization, purpose and time; individual recruiter names only if org policy allows; support and admin access always appear; retained {24 months}; recruiter privacy modes cannot hide from it. | Transparency. | Access service | [SRC: Yash BR-T068; SSOT BR-133 viewer privacy applies to viewer-side only] |
| BR-SET-013 | Export: step-up required; one open request per type; ≤ 1 completed per {24 h}; own data only; archive TTL {7 d}; download via one-time URL TTL {15 min} after step-up; the file is never emailed. | Safe delivery. | Privacy service | [SRC: Yash BR-T064] |
| BR-SET-014 | Every module that owns personal data must register an export contributor and an erase contributor; CI fails otherwise. | Completeness by construction. | CI lint + orchestrator | [SRC: Yash SPEC-13 §5] |
| BR-SET-015 | Erasure completes within {30 d} of the request (target ≤ 10 d); it may be marked complete only after a sweep finds zero residuals in every store; alerts at day 20, 25, 28; day 30 breach is an incident. | Enforceable deadline. | Orchestrator + monitor | [SRC: Yash BR-T060] |
| BR-SET-016 | Erasure for a `suspended` account, an account under an open moderation case, or a subject under legal hold is accepted but parked `on_hold`; sole owners of orgs must transfer first. | Evidence preservation. | Orchestrator | [SRC: Yash BR-T124] |
| BR-SET-017 | Audit, consent and stage-transition history is never rewritten: it holds opaque subject references and erasure deletes the reference-to-identity mapping. | Integrity with erasure. | Data layer | [SRC: Yash BR-T065; SSOT V61-19] |
| BR-SET-018 | Backups age out within {35 d}; restores replay the erasure log before serving. | Erasure survives restore. | Operations | [SRC: Yash SPEC-13 §9]; value open OD-SET-02 |
| BR-SET-019 | The erasure receipt lists what was deleted, what was retained and why, and the date; it holds no personal data beyond a salted email hash kept {30 d}. | Transparency. | Privacy service | [SRC: Yash SPEC-13 §3.2] |
| BR-SET-020 | Rectification, restriction, objection and access requests are answered within {30 d}; identity is verified before any data change or disclosure; extensions are limited, reasoned and notified before the due date. | Rights SLAs. | DSAR queue | [SRC: SSOT §15.9.5] |
| BR-SET-021 | Staff handling requests see metadata only, never subject content; every action needs a reason and is audited; declines state a reason and the right to complain; holds are never explained to the subject. | Least privilege. | Admin policy | [SRC: Yash SPEC-13 §2] |
| BR-SET-022 | Every personal-data class has a retention period and a disposal action in a versioned schedule; unscheduled retention is not allowed; legal holds suspend disposal. | Storage limitation. | Retention engine + CI | [SRC: SSOT §15.9.1 5(1)(e)] |
| BR-SET-023 | Locale must be supported, time zone a valid IANA id; times are stored in UTC and rendered in the user's zone; detection suggests, never silently changes. | Correct time handling. | Preference service | [DER] |
| BR-SET-024 | Accessibility and display preferences are honored from OS signals as defaults, apply before first paint, and are never used for profiling or shown to third parties. | Inclusion and privacy. | UI + policy | [DER] |
| BR-SET-025 | Connected apps and accounts receive only minimal, purpose-bound scopes; an app cannot receive data the user has not consented to share; revocation invalidates tokens immediately; idle grants expire after {12 months}. | Delegated-token care. | PLT + decision function | [SRC: SSOT HDN-012] |
| BR-SET-026 | Personal API tokens are random, hashed, shown once, scoped to the owner's data and current permissions, ≤ {10} active, expire ≤ 365 d (default 90), and are revoked on erasure, suspension and loss of the role. | Least privilege automation. | Token service | [PROP] |
| BR-SET-027 | Regional rules are versioned configuration; strictest wins on ambiguity; relaxations need dual control; compliance claims in UI require a legal-review flag. | Lawful operation without claims of certification. | Rules engine | [SRC: SSOT §15.9.2, §15.9.3] |
| BR-SET-028 | Policy versions are immutable once published; material changes need a notice period (default {30 d}) and re-acceptance; acceptance rows are append-only. | Auditable acceptance. | Policy service | [SRC: Yash FEAT-22-06] |
| BR-SET-029 | AI processing of a person's content requires `ai.assist.process` at call time; no training use; EU-region data goes to EU endpoints or the feature is unavailable. | Lawful AI. | AI gateway | [SRC: SSOT §15.9.3, §15.10] |
| BR-SET-030 | All settings are defined in a registry with type, default, scope and sensitivity; protected settings need step-up; every change is recorded in history (sensitive values omitted) retained {12 months}. | Consistent, auditable settings. | Settings service | [DER] |
| BR-SET-031 | Org locks come from a closed catalog that excludes consent scopes, third-party visibility, export, erasure, security and accessibility settings; org defaults can only be more private; locks end when the member leaves. | Org cannot override personal rights. | Settings service | [DER]; OD-SET-09 |
| BR-SET-032 | Guardian-sourced consent never enables discoverability, outreach, public view or marketing for a minor; majority handover resets guardian grants to off. | Child protection. | Consent service | [PROP] |
| BR-SET-033 | Non-essential cookies and tags load only after consent in opt-in regions; the Global Privacy Control signal is treated as an opt-out; essential storage needs no consent; choices re-asked at most every 12 months. | Lawful tracking. | Tag loader | [DER] |
| BR-SET-034 | The privacy dashboard states facts from live data and never shows a derived privacy score. | No gamification of privacy. | UI + review | [PROP] |

## SRC

Source: [02_MODULES/SRC_Search_Discovery.md](../02_MODULES/SRC_Search_Discovery.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-SRC-001 | Every query is evaluated with the viewer's permissions. Results the viewer may not see are never returned, counted, faceted, suggested, highlighted or alerted. Permission is checked at query time against the source of truth for the result page in addition to index-time ACLs; failure to check drops the hit. | Zero leakage. | Query service; hydration | [SRC: SSOT F-147 "0 RLS leakage", F-92 "zero stealth leakage"] |
| BR-SRC-002 | Only fields allowed for search are indexed, grouped by audience. Contact data, salary expectation, work authorization, background-check data, private evidence, hidden test cases, solutions and private messages are never indexed. Every indexable entity declares an audience policy. | Minimization. | Document builder; schema registry | [DER] from SSOT F-12 and F-92 |
| BR-SRC-003 | Deletions, visibility reductions, suspensions and erasures propagate to the index within 15 minutes (erasure within 24 h). The query-time check covers the gap. | Privacy changes must be fast. | Indexer; query service | [SRC: SSOT F-92 "consent revocation < 24h"]; 15 min [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-004 | Ranking inputs are documented per entity, derived from stored features, and the explanation shown to users is generated from the same features. Protected attributes and their proxies are never inputs. | Honest transparency and fairness. | Ranking service; contract tests | [SRC: SSOT F-04 "Why am I seeing this?"] |
| BR-SRC-005 | Default job ranking weights are skill match 0.45, experience 0.20, location 0.10, title 0.10, organization rating 0.10, recency 0.05 until revised through FR-SRC-027. The organization-rating input is disclosed and is an open decision. | Legacy baseline retained. | Ranking profile `jobs-v1` | [SRC: SSOT F-04 step 2]; [DEC-REQ] OD-SRC-03 |
| BR-SRC-006 | Talent search never filters, sorts or ranks on name, photo, age or date of birth, gender, pronouns, ethnicity, religion, disability, marital status, nationality or proxies (such as graduation year as an age proxy). Such filters do not exist in the UI or API. | Anti-discrimination. | Filter allowlist; feature allowlist | [PROP]; [DER] |
| BR-SRC-007 | A candidate appears in talent search only if published, not stealth, discoverable to recruiters (or applied to the searching org), not blocking the recruiter or org, not under 18, not suspended; filters use only fields the candidate shared with recruiters. Enforced at query time. | Candidate control. | Talent query layer | [SRC: SSOT F-92 steps 7–8]; PRF BR-PRF-025, 029, 041 |
| BR-SRC-008 | Talent search queries, profile views and exports are logged (recruiter, org, parsed query, counts, viewed ids), rate limited, and result windows are capped at 1000. Logs are visible to the org admin and staff. | Accountability and anti-harvesting. | Talent search service | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-009 | Talent results show why each candidate matched (criteria) and no hidden score; blind review mode removes names, photos, school names, pronouns and graduation years from payloads; ties may be shuffled. | Explainable, fairer first pass. | Talent search UI and API | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-010 | Selection-rate audits for talent search run at least monthly on aggregated, k-anonymized cohorts using voluntary demographic data where lawfully collected; thresholds raise alerts to PAD and the org. | Detect disparate impact. | Fairness job | [PROP]; [DEC-REQ] OD-SRC-04 |
| BR-SRC-011 | A user may keep up to 25 saved searches (talent searches count separately up to 50 per recruiter), each a structured query with unique name; alerts are new-only with no backfill. | Bounded load; clear semantics. | Saved search service | [SRC: SSOT F-04 step 7]; limits [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-012 | Alert items are re-checked for permission, status and duplicates at send time; max 3 instant alerts per day per user, overflow goes to the digest; one-click unsubscribe is always present. | Safe, quiet alerts. | Alert job | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-013 | Recent searches are kept per user (max 20, 90 days), deletable, pausable, and excluded from others' views. | User control. | History service | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-014 | Queries matching identifier patterns (email, phone, national or card numbers) are not stored in history, logs or analytics; autocomplete suggests only queries used by ≥ 20 distinct users; raw query logs are retained 90 days with restricted access. | Prevent leaking personal data via search. | Logging and suggest pipeline | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-015 | Personalization is optional, disclosed, applies only to the user's own results, never to recruiter ranking of candidates, and turning it off deletes the profile within 24 h and stops its use immediately. | Control and fairness. | Ranking service | [SRC: SSOT F-147 personalization]; control [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-016 | Typo tolerance: edit distance 1 for terms of 4–7 characters, 2 for 8 or more, none for shorter terms, quoted phrases, fields or numbers; low-confidence corrections are suggestions, high-confidence ones are announced and reversible; exact matches rank above fuzzy ones. | Predictable. | Query analyzer | [SRC: SSOT F-147 typo tolerance]; thresholds [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-017 | Synonym and alias expansion is curated, directional where meaningful, shown to the user, switchable, and suppressed for quoted or field-prefixed terms; expanded matches rank below exact ones. | Recall without surprises. | Query analyzer | [SRC: SSOT F-84]; [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-018 | Skill filters use canonical skill ids; hierarchy expansion is opt-in, one hop by default, with traversal bounded to 5 hops. | Taxonomy integrity. | Filter builder | [SRC: SSOT BR-144, BR-146] |
| BR-SRC-019 | Pagination is cursor-based, 20 per page default, 100 maximum; total reachable results per query are capped at 1000; guests get no deep paging in people search. | Performance and anti-scraping. | API | [SRC: SSOT F-04 step 1]; cap [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-020 | Search state (query, filters, sort, tab) is encoded in the URL; invalid or non-permitted parameters are dropped with a notice; URLs contain no personal data other than the typed query. | Shareable and safe. | Web app and API | [SRC: SSOT F-04 step 1] |
| BR-SRC-021 | Facet and tab counts are computed under permissions, shown as "1000+" above 1000, and suppressed below 5 for people facets (talent facets below 10) to prevent re-identification. | Privacy. | Facet service | [PROP]; [SRC: SSOT BR-158 default k] |
| BR-SRC-022 | Each entity has a documented default sort and allowed sorts; ties break deterministically; "newest" uses publication date; items lacking the sort attribute are placed last. | Predictable ordering. | Query service | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-023 | Zero-result and error states give recovery steps, and responses for hidden, blocked or non-existent entities are indistinguishable. | No dead ends; no existence leak. | Query service; UI | [SRC: SSOT §11.2]; [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-024 | Freshness targets: jobs and content ≤ 5 min; people and courses ≤ 15 min; deletions and visibility reductions ≤ 15 min. | Quality of results. | Indexer | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-025 | Index changes ship as new versions validated against a judgment set and leak canaries, swapped atomically with two approvals, and roll-backable. | Safe change. | Index admin | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-026 | Abuse controls apply to all search surfaces: rate limits per role, caps for guests, enumeration-safe responses, anomaly detection, step-up challenges, and honeypots; limiter failure falls back to conservative limits. | Anti-scraping. | Edge and search service | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-027 | Queries are limited to 256 characters and 20 terms; talent search allows up to 15 boolean clauses; engine syntax is never passed through. | Safety and cost. | Parser | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-028 | Command search actions are filtered by the user's role and context; the palette never reveals pages or entities the user may not access. | Least privilege. | Action registry | [SRC: SSOT F-20]; [DER] |
| BR-SRC-029 | Search analytics store whitelisted metadata only, report aggregates, hash session ids, truncate IPs, and suppress cells below k = 10. | Privacy. | Analytics pipeline | [SRC: SSOT BR-27, BR-158] |
| BR-SRC-030 | Ranking profiles, synonym sets and analyzers are versioned, evaluated offline and in shadow against judgment sets, approved by two people, and roll-backable; each release has a changelog. | Controlled quality. | Relevance console | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-031 | Candidate-side search appearance insights are aggregates only, name no recruiter or organization, and suppress breakdowns below 5 events. | Privacy both ways. | Insights job | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-032 | Fairness data is voluntary, held outside SRC, used in aggregates only with k ≥ 10, and never available per person to recruiters or search. | Lawful, minimal. | Fairness job | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-033 | People locations are indexed at city level or coarser; street addresses are never indexed; device location is used for one query only and not stored. | Location privacy. | Document builder; query | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-034 | In degraded mode, search falls back only to tiers that enforce identical visibility rules; people and talent search are not served from fallback; permission-service failure returns no results. | Fail closed. | Search gateway | [PROP]; [SRC: SSOT BR-28 honest status] |
| BR-SRC-035 | Autocomplete and suggestions exclude offensive and sensitive completions and never suggest private individuals' names to unauthorized viewers. | Safe suggestions. | Suggest pipeline | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-036 | People search excludes unpublished, suspended, blocked-for-viewer and under-18 profiles and shows only fields visible to the viewer. | Respect PRF settings. | People query | [DER] from PRF |
| BR-SRC-037 | Alert emails and push messages contain only items and snippets the recipient can see and exclude sensitive fields. | Safe notifications. | Alert templates | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-038 | Paid or sponsored placement is not part of organic ranking. Any future promotion must be visually labeled, separate from ranked results, and approved as a scope decision. | Trust; SSOT §4.2 "not an ad network". | Ranking service | [SRC: SSOT §4.2 non-goals]; OD-SRC-08 |
| BR-SRC-039 | A public "How results are ranked" page per entity lists inputs, exclusions and the last change date, and is updated at each ranking release. | Transparency. | Docs and release process | [SRC: SSOT BR-124 analog] |
| BR-SRC-040 | Evidence-based filters in talent search default to "Any"; choosing a minimum shows a notice that candidates without evidence are hidden; filters use only recruiter-visible evidence. | Don't penalize unverified candidates silently. | Talent filter builder | [DER]; EVD BR-EVD-025 |
| BR-SRC-041 | Queries are analyzed per language; unsupported languages fall back to a generic analyzer with a notice; skills resolve to language-independent canonical ids. | Inclusive search. | Analyzer | [PROP] |
| BR-SRC-042 | Canonical skills are created only by taxonomy editors; merges leave redirects; relationships are directional and `prerequisite_of` is acyclic; traversal is bounded to 5 hops. | Governed taxonomy. | Taxonomy service | [SRC: SSOT BR-141, BR-142, BR-146, BR-147] |
| BR-SRC-043 | A skill candidate is promoted only with at least 5 independent signals in the window and editor approval; `correlates_with` edges are computed, not manual. | Quality control. | Emerging skills job | [SRC: SSOT BR-143, BR-148] |
| BR-SRC-044 | Each skill has a decay class that EVD uses for freshness; changing a class recomputes freshness with a note and is versioned. | Consistent freshness. | Taxonomy service | [SRC: SSOT F-123]; [PROP] |

## STU

Source: [02_MODULES/STU_Instructor_Studio_Content_Production.md](../02_MODULES/STU_Instructor_Studio_Content_Production.md)

| ID | Rule | Rationale | Enforced where | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BR-STU-001 | Only an instructor with an approved application, accepted current agreement and the verification level required for the action may submit a course for review or publish. | Quality and accountability. | Submission and publish services | [SRC: SSOT BR-097] |
| BR-STU-002 | Only a version in state `approved` (or a patch passing automated checks) can be published; publishing records actor, time and version. | No unreviewed structural content. | Publish service | [SRC: SSOT WF-24] [DER] |
